n: What is React and why does it exist?
t: Start Here — What is React and Why Does it Exist?
x: Without React: updating the DOM manually is slow, tedious, and error-prone at scale. React solves this with a component model where you describe what the UI should look like, and React figures out how to update the DOM efficiently. Built by Facebook in 2013. What problem does React solve? What was wrong with updating the DOM manually? Declarative tum batate ho "screen aisi dikhni chahiye" — kaise karna hai wo React sochta hai Imperative tum step-by-step batate ho — ye element pakdo, ye text badlo, ye class hatao UI = f(state) UI ek function ka result hai jiska input state hai Definition: React ek JavaScript library hai jo UI banane ke liye hai. Iska core idea ek line mein — UI = f(state) . T

n: Setting up a React project — Vite, create-react-app, or Next.js
t: Start Here — What is React and Why Does it Exist?
x: Vite: npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react → fastest setup. CRA: npx create-react-app my-app → older, slower. Next.js: npx create-next-app@latest → for SSR/full-stack. For learning React basics, use Vite. How do you create a new React project? What is the role of a bundler like Vite or Webpack? Bundler tumhari 100 files ko browser ke liye chalne layak bana deta hai (Vite, webpack) HMR Hot Module Replacement — file save karte hi browser bina reload update ho jaata hai Meta-framework React ke upar bana framework jisme routing/SSR built-in hai (Next.js) Definition: React project shuru karne ke 3 raste — Vite (fast, simple SPA), Next.js (routing + SSR + backend sab included), aur CR

n: Your first React component — Hello World
t: Start Here — What is React and Why Does it Exist?
x: A React component is just a JavaScript function that returns JSX. function App() { return Hello World ; } — that's a complete component. React renders it to the DOM via createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render( ). What is a React component? How does React turn a component into actual HTML on the page? Component ek function jo UI (JSX) return karta hai Root wo DOM element jisme poora React app render hota hai Render component ko chalana taaki React ko pata chale screen pe kya dikhana hai Definition: React component ek normal JavaScript function hai jo JSX return karta hai. Ek hi niyam hai — naam capital letter se shuru hona chahiye. function Button() = component. function button() =

n: What is JSX? — HTML-like syntax inside JavaScript
t: Start Here — What is React and Why Does it Exist?
x: JSX looks like HTML but it's actually JavaScript. Babel compiles Hello to React.createElement("h1", null, "Hello"). Rules: className instead of class, camelCase for attributes (onClick not onclick), all tags must close ( not ). What is JSX? Is it valid JavaScript? How does it work under the hood? JSX JavaScript ke andar HTML jaisa syntax likhne ka tarika Transpile JSX ko normal JS function calls mein badalna (build time pe) Expression slot JSX ke andar { } jisme koi bhi JS expression daal sakte ho Definition: JSX JavaScript ka extension hai jo HTML jaisa dikhta hai. Browser isko nahi samajhta — build ke waqt ye React.createElement(...) calls mein badal jaata hai (React 17+ mein jsx() ). Matl

n: Props vs State — passing data and managing change
t: Start Here — What is React and Why Does it Exist?
x: Props: data passed FROM parent TO child — read-only, like function parameters. State: data that lives INSIDE a component — when it changes, React re-renders the component. Props are for "configuration", state is for "what changed". function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); return setCount(c => c+1)}>{count} ; } What is the difference between props and state in React? Props parent se child ko diya gaya data — child isse badal nahi sakta State component ka apna data jo badal sakta hai — badalne par re-render hota hai Re-render component function ka dobara chalna taaki naya UI bane Definition: Do tarah ka data hota hai React mein: Props — bahar se aaya (function ke arguments j

JSX is syntactic sugar — Babel compiles it to React.createElement() calls that return plain JS objects called React Elements. What does JSX actually compile to? What is a React Element vs a React Component? React.createElement wo function jisme JSX transpile hota tha (classic runtime) Automatic runtime React 17+ ka naya tarika — jsx() function, import ki zaroorat nahi React Element JSX ka result — ek plain immutable object Definition: JSX compile hokar function call banta hai jo ek plain object return karta hai. Wo object hi "React Element" hai — ek description hai ki screen pe kya hona chahiye, koi asli DOM node nahi. React 17 se pehle: React.createElement (isliye import React zaroori tha).

An in-memory JS object tree mirroring the real DOM — React diffs the new vs old tree and only applies minimal real DOM changes. What is the Virtual DOM and why does React use it? Does it always make things faster? Virtual DOM asli DOM ka JS object mein banaya hua halka copy Diffing purane aur naye tree ko compare karke farak nikalna Reconciliation diff ke hisaab se asli DOM mein minimum changes karna Definition: Virtual DOM asli DOM ka ek lightweight JavaScript representation hai. State badalne par React naya virtual tree banata hai, purane se compare karta hai, aur sirf jo badla hai utna hi asli DOM mein apply karta hai.

Class components use lifecycle methods and this; functional components use hooks. Hooks give functions all the same capabilities — and more. What are the key differences between class and functional components? Why did the React team move to hooks? Class component purana tarika — class extends React.Component, render() method Functional component aaj ka standard — normal function + hooks Lifecycle methods class ke special methods — componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate... Definition: React mein component do tarah se likhe jaate the. Class (2019 se pehle) mein this.state , this.setState , aur lifecycle methods the. Functional (aaj) mein hooks se wahi cheezein hoti hain, bina this ke. Aaj naya

Props are read-only inputs flowing parent → child. Mutating props directly breaks the one-way data flow contract. Why are props immutable? What happens to child components when a parent re-renders? Immutable jo badla na jaa sake children special prop — tag ke andar likha hua content Spread {...obj} se saare props ek saath pass karna Definition: Props parent se child ko diya gaya data hai. React inhe read-only treat karta hai — child props ko badal nahi sakta. React ka rule: "har component apne props ke maamle mein pure function ki tarah behave kare" .

State is private, mutable data that when changed schedules a re-render. React batches state updates for efficiency. What triggers a re-render in React? What does NOT trigger a re-render? useState hook jo state banata hai — [value, setValue] deta hai Batching kai setState ek saath milaakar ek hi re-render karna Functional update setX(prev => ...) — purani value se nayi banana Definition: State component ka apna data hai jo re-render ke beech yaad rehta hai aur jise badalne par React re-render karta hai. const [x, setX] = useState(initial) . Do zaroori sach: (1) setX turant value nahi badalta — agli render mein nayi value milti hai; (2) React ek event ke saare setState ba

Keys help React identify which items in a list changed, were added, or removed — critical for correct reconciliation. Why does React need keys? What happens if you use index as a key? When is index as key actually safe? Key list ke har item ko di gayi unique pehchan Index key array ka position (0,1,2) key ki tarah use karna — aksar galat Remount component ka poora naya banna — saara internal state khatam Definition: Key ek special prop hai jo React ko batata hai ki list ke do render ke beech kaunsa item wahi item hai. Bina key ke React position se match karta hai, jo item add/remove/reorder hone par galat ho jaata hai.

Controlled: React state owns the input value. Uncontrolled: the DOM owns it via refs. Both have legitimate use cases. What is the difference between controlled and uncontrolled inputs? When would you use each? Controlled input ki value React state se aati hai Uncontrolled input apni value khud DOM mein rakhta hai, React sirf ref se padhta hai defaultValue uncontrolled input ki shuruaati value Definition: Do tarah ke form inputs: Controlled — value={state} + onChange . React ke paas har waqt sach hai. Uncontrolled — defaultValue + ref . DOM ke paas sach hai, React sirf submit pe padhta hai.

A development-only tool that double-invokes render/lifecycle functions to surface side effect bugs and deprecated API usage. What does StrictMode do? Why does it call some functions twice in development? StrictMode ek wrapper component jo dev mein extra checks karta hai Double invoke dev mein render aur effect ko jaan-boojh ke do baar chalana Idempotent do baar chalane par bhi wahi natija — koi extra side effect nahi Definition: <StrictMode> ek dev-only wrapper hai. Ye kuch render nahi karta — bas React se kehta hai "extra sakhti se check karo". Sabse dikhne wala effect: components do baar render hote hain aur effects do baar chalte hain (mount → unmount → mount). Production

The complete rewrite of React's reconciler (React 16+). Fiber turns the render tree into a linked list of units of work that can be paused, aborted, and resumed. What is React Fiber and why was it a complete rewrite? What problem does it solve over the old stack reconciler? Fiber ek JS object jo ek component ke kaam ko represent karta hai Stack reconciler purana React (v15) — recursion se chalta tha, rok nahi sakte the Interruptible kaam beech mein rok ke baad mein resume kar sakna Definition: Fiber React 16+ ka reconciliation engine hai. Har component ke liye ek fiber node banta hai — ek plain object jisme us component ka type, props, state, aur uske parent/child/sibling ke pointers hote ha

React's O(n) algorithm for comparing two trees using two heuristics: elements of different types produce different trees; keys identify stable elements across renders. Explain how React's diffing algorithm works. What are its two key assumptions that make it O(n) instead of O(n³)? Reconciliation purane aur naye tree ko compare karke DOM changes nikalna Heuristic shortcut rule jo hamesha perfect nahi par practically sahi hota hai O(n) n items ke liye n steps — linear, fast Definition: Reconciliation wo algorithm hai jo purane fiber tree ko naye element tree se compare karta hai. Perfect tree-diff O(n³) hota hai — 1000 nodes ke liye ek arab operations. React do heuristics lagakar isko O(n) ban

Render phase: pure, interruptible work — React builds the new Fiber tree. Commit phase: synchronous, non-interruptible — React applies DOM mutations and runs effects. What is the difference between the render phase and commit phase? Why must the render phase be pure? Render phase React soch raha hai kya badla — pure, interruptible Commit phase React DOM ko sach mein badal raha hai — synchronous, uninterruptible Effect list un fibers ki list jinme kuch DOM kaam karna hai Definition: Har update do phases mein hota hai: Render (soch) — component functions chalte hain, naya tree banta hai, diff hota hai. Koi DOM change nahi. Ye ruk sakta hai, dobara chal sakta hai, cancel ho sakta hai . Commit (

React's scheduler assigns priority lanes to updates (SyncLane, InputContinuousLane, DefaultLane, IdleLane) and processes high-priority work first. How does React prioritize which updates to process first? What are lanes in React? Scheduler React ka apna module jo decide karta hai kaunsa kaam kab chale Lane priority ka ek bit — React 18 mein 31 lanes hain Starvation low-priority kaam ka kabhi chance na milna Definition: Scheduler React ka priority system hai. Har update ko ek lane milti hai. Zyada urgent lane pehle process hoti hai; kam urgent kaam ruk ke wait karta hai. Priority order (upar sabse urgent): Sync (discrete events jaise click/input) → InputContinuous (hover, drag) → De

The Fiber work loop processes one Fiber node at a time, yielding back to the browser every ~5ms so frames aren't blocked — enabling interruptible rendering. What is time slicing in React? How does the work loop enable rendering without blocking the browser? Work loop wo loop jo ek-ek fiber process karta hai Time slicing kaam ko 5ms ke tukdon mein baant ke chalana Yield main thread browser ko wapas de dena Definition: Work loop React ka main engine hai. Ye ek while loop hai jo ek-ek fiber pe kaam karta hai, aur har fiber ke baad poochta hai — "kya mera 5ms ka time khatam ho gaya?" Agar haan, to yield karta hai (browser ko chalne deta hai) aur agle frame mein wahin se resume karta hai.

React 17 only batches state updates inside React event handlers. React 18 batches ALL updates — including setTimeout, promises, and native events — automatically. What is state batching? How does React 18's automatic batching differ from React 17? How do you opt out? Batching kai state updates ko milaakar ek hi re-render karna Automatic batching React 18 ka feature — har jagah batching, sirf event handler mein nahi flushSync batching ko force tod ke turant render karana Definition: Batching yaani ek hi tick mein hue saare setState ko jodkar sirf ek re-render karna. React 17 mein batching sirf React event handlers mein hoti thi. setTimeout , promise, ya native listener ke andar har setState a

n: React Element vs Component vs Instance
x: Element: a plain object describing what to render. Component: a function/class that returns elements. Instance: only class components have instances (this). What is the difference between a React element, a React component, and a React instance? Element plain immutable object — "kya dikhna chahiye" ka description Component function ya class — jo element banata hai Instance fiber node — chalte hue component ka asli record (state, effects) Definition: Teen alag cheezein jo log mila dete hain: Component = recipe (function Card ) Element = order slip ( <Card title="Hi"/> — ek object, abhi kuch chala nahi) Instance = asli dish (fiber node jisme state, effects, DOM pointer hai)

Hooks must be called at top level and only from React functions. React stores hook state in a linked list on the Fiber node, indexed by call order. Why can't hooks be called inside conditionals or loops? What would break internally if you did? Hook use se shuru hone wala special function jo React feature deta hai Call order jis order mein hooks call hote hain — React isi se unhe pehchanta hai Linked list ek ke baad ek jude hue nodes — React hooks isi mein store karta hai Definition: Do rules: Hooks sirf top level pe call karo — if, loop, ya nested function ke andar nahi. Sirf React function component ya custom hook ke andar call karo. Wajah ek line mein: React hooks ko naam se nahi, order se

useState stores its value in a hook queue on the Fiber node. The setter enqueues an update and triggers a re-render. Functional updates avoid stale closure problems. How does useState work under the hood? What is the difference between setState(value) and setState(prev => value)? Hook node fiber ke andar ek object jisme us hook ka state hai Update queue pending setState ki circular list Bailout value same hai to React render skip kar deta hai Definition: useState fiber ke memoizedState linked list mein ek node banata hai. Us node mein hoti hai — current value, aur ek update queue jisme pending setState pade rehte hain. Render ke waqt React queue ke saare updates ek-ek karke apply karta hai a

Runs after paint, asynchronously. The dependency array controls when it re-runs. The cleanup function runs before the next effect or on unmount. Explain useEffect's full lifecycle: when does it run, when does cleanup run, what is the dependency array contract? Side effect render ke bahar ka kaam — fetch, timer, subscription, DOM Dependency array wo values jinke badalne par effect dobara chale Cleanup effect ka return kiya hua function — agle effect se pehle chalta hai Definition: useEffect(fn, deps) React ko kehta hai "commit + paint ke baad ye kaam karo". deps array batati hai kab dobara chalana hai. Koi array nahi → har render [] → sirf mount pe (aur StrictMode dev mein 2 baar) [

useLayoutEffect fires synchronously after DOM mutations but before paint — identical to componentDidMount/Update. useEffect fires after paint. When would you use useLayoutEffect over useEffect? Give a concrete real-world example. Paint browser ka screen pe pixels banana Layout thrashing baar baar DOM measure karke badalna — bahut slow Flicker user ko ek frame ke liye galat UI dikhna Definition: Dono commit ke baad chalte hain, par timing alag: useLayoutEffect — DOM update ke baad, paint se PEHLE . Synchronous, browser ko rok deta hai. useEffect — paint ke BAAD . Async, browser ko nahi rokta. Default hamesha useEffect . useLayoutEffect sirf jab DOM measure karke usi frame mein b

useRef returns a stable object { current } that persists across renders without triggering re-renders. Use it for: DOM access, timers, previous values, and mutable instance variables. What are the three main uses of useRef? How is it different from useState for storing values? Ref ek mutable box — { current: value } Mutable jise seedha badal sakte ho Instance variable wo value jo renders ke beech bachi rahe par render trigger na kare Definition: useRef(init) ek object { current: init } deta hai jo poore component ke jeevan bhar wahi object rehta hai . .current badalne se re-render nahi hota . Do kaam: (1) DOM node pakadna, (2) aisi value rakhna jo yaad rahe par UI se lena-dena na ho (timer i

n: useMemo — When to Use & When Not To
x: Memoizes the result of an expensive computation. Only recalculates when dependencies change. Costs memory and code complexity — only worth it for genuinely expensive work. When should you use useMemo? What is the overhead of useMemo itself? When does it hurt performance? Memoize result yaad rakhna taaki dobara calculate na karna pade Referential stability har render pe wahi object reference milna Premature optimization bina napay optimize karna — aksar nuksaan Definition: useMemo(fn, deps) calculation ka result yaad rakhta hai. Deps na badle to fn dobara nahi chalta — purana result milta hai. Do jaayaz wajah: (1) sach mein mehnga calculation, (2) reference stable rakhna taaki neeche wala mem

Returns a memoized function reference that only changes when dependencies change. Critical when passing callbacks to memoized child components. Why does useCallback exist? When does it actually help performance vs when is it wasted? useCallback function ka reference stable rakhta hai Reference equality do function same hain ya nahi — content nahi, address compare hota hai Definition: useCallback(fn, deps) = useMemo(() => fn, deps) . Ye function ko yaad rakhta hai taaki har render pe wahi reference mile. JavaScript mein har render pe () => {} ek naya function object hai — dikhne mein same, reference alag. Isi wajah se child ka React.memo toot jaata hai.

An alternative to useState for complex state transitions. Takes (state, action) => newState. Makes state logic testable and colocated. When would you choose useReducer over useState? Implement a cart with useReducer. Reducer pure function: (state, action) => naya state Action ek object jo batata hai kya hua — { type: "...", payload } Dispatch action bhejne wala function Definition: useReducer(reducer, initial) — jab kai state values ek doosre se jude hon, unhe alag alag useState mein rakhne ki jagah ek reducer mein rakho. Har badlav ek "action" hai. Rule of thumb: 3+ related states ya ek event kai states badalta ho → useReducer.

Subscribes a component to the nearest context value. Every context value change re-renders ALL consumers — even if they only use part of the value. What is the performance problem with useContext? How do you prevent unnecessary re-renders from context changes? Context tree ke neeche data pahunchane ka rasta bina props ke Provider wo component jo value deta hai Consumer wo component jo useContext se value leta hai Definition: Context prop drilling se bachne ka tarika hai. Provider ek value deta hai, aur tree ke andar kahin bhi useContext se wo value mil jaati hai. Performance trap: jab context ka value badalta hai to saare consumers re-render hote hain — chahe unhone us value ka sirf ek chhot

Functions starting with "use" that call other hooks — encapsulate and reuse stateful logic without changing component hierarchy. What is a custom hook? How does it differ from a utility function? When should you extract one? Custom hook use se shuru hone wala function jo doosre hooks use karta hai Stateful logic wo logic jisme state ya effect ho Composition chhote hooks ko jodkar bada banana Definition: Custom hook ek normal function hai jo (a) use se shuru hota hai aur (b) andar doosre hooks call karta hai. Isse tum stateful logic ko component se alag karke reuse kar sakte ho. Important: har component ko apni alag copy milti hai. Custom hook state share nahi karta — logic share karta h

Local state → component. Shared UI state → lift up or context. Server state → React Query/SWR. Global app state → Zustand/Redux. How do you decide where state should live? Walk me through your decision framework for a real app. Server state data jo server ka hai — tumhare paas uski copy hai (users, posts) Client state data jo sirf tumhare browser ka hai (modal open, form draft) Derived state jo doosre data se calculate ho sakta hai — state hona hi nahi chahiye Definition: State ko jagah dena ek decision hai, default nahi. Sabse zaroori sawaal — ye server ka data hai ya client ka? Server state → React Query / SWR / framework loader. useState mein mat daalo. Client state → jitna neec

Context is designed for low-frequency, global data (theme, auth, locale) — not high-frequency state updates that should use a dedicated store. What is Context good for and what is it NOT good for? What performance problems does heavy Context use cause? createContext context object banata hai Default value jab koi Provider na ho tab milne wali value Custom hook wrapper useContext ko apne hook mein lapetna — safety ke liye Definition: Context ka sahi tarika: hamesha ek custom hook banao jo Provider missing hone pe error de, value ko useMemo karo, aur data + actions ko alag context mein rakho.

Single store, pure reducers, actions as intent. Middleware (thunk, saga) handles side effects. Selectors compute derived state. DevTools enable time-travel debugging. Explain the full Redux data flow. What is the role of middleware? When is Redux overkill? Store ek jagah jahan poore app ka state hai Action plain object jo batata hai kya hua Middleware action aur reducer ke beech ka layer — logging, async, etc. Definition: Redux ek predictable state container hai. Teen niyam: (1) single store , (2) state read-only — sirf action dispatch karke badlo, (3) badlav pure reducers se hote hain. Data flow ek hi direction mein: dispatch(action) → middleware → reducer → naya state →

RTK eliminates Redux boilerplate: createSlice merges actions+reducers, createAsyncThunk handles async flows, RTK Query handles server state. What problems does Redux Toolkit solve over vanilla Redux? Explain createSlice and createAsyncThunk. createSlice reducer + actions ek saath banata hai Immer library jo "mutate" likhne deta hai par andar se immutable copy banata hai RTK Query RTK ka data fetching + caching layer Definition: Redux Toolkit aaj Redux likhne ka official tarika hai. createSlice ek hi jagah state, reducers aur actions bana deta hai. Immer built-in hai isliye tum state.count++ likh sakte ho — dikhne mein mutation, andar se immutable.

A minimal store based on closures and subscriptions. Components subscribe to slices — only re-render when their subscribed slice changes, unlike Context. How does Zustand work under the hood? How does it avoid the re-render problem that Context has? Store ek hook jo state deta hai — create() se banta hai Selector store ka sirf ek hissa chunna — sirf usi pe re-render Shallow compare object ki top-level keys compare karna Definition: Zustand ek chhota (~1KB) state library hai. Store banate ho create() se, aur wo ek hook ban jaata hai. Koi Provider nahi, koi boilerplate nahi. Sabse bada farak Context se: selector support . Tum store ka sirf ek field subscribe kar sakte ho — baaki kuch bhi badle

Manages server state: caching, background refetching, stale-while-revalidate, pagination, optimistic updates. Removes the need for loading/error/data state boilerplate. What problem does React Query solve that useState+useEffect doesn't? Explain stale-while-revalidate. Query key cache ki unique pehchan — array hoti hai Stale data purana ho gaya — background mein refetch hoga Mutation server pe data badalne wala operation (POST/PUT/DELETE) Definition: TanStack Query server data ke liye ek cache hai, state manager nahi. Ye handle karta hai: caching, deduplication (2 component ne same data maanga = 1 request), background refetch, stale-while-revalidate, retry, pagination, optimistic updates.

Atom-based state: tiny, composable units of state. Components subscribe to only the atoms they need — minimal re-renders with a graph-based dependency model. What is atomic state management? How do atoms differ from a single global store like Redux? Atom state ka sabse chhota tukda Derived atom doosre atoms se banaya gaya atom Bottom-up chhote tukdo se bada banana — top-down store ka ulta Definition: Atomic state (Jotai, Recoil) mein ek bada store nahi hota — bahut saare chhote atoms hote hain. Har component sirf jo atom use karta hai usi pe subscribe hota hai. Derived atoms doosre atoms se apne aap calculate ho jaate hain — aur sirf tab recompute hote hain jab unka koi dependency ba

A component re-renders when: its state changes, its parent re-renders, context it consumes changes, or its key changes. Props being the same is NOT enough to prevent re-renders. List every cause of a React re-render. What is the most common source of unnecessary re-renders in production apps? Re-render component function ka dobara chalna Repaint browser ka pixels dobara banana — ye alag cheez hai Bailout React ka render skip kar dena Definition: Component sirf 4 wajah se re-render hota hai: Uska apna state badla Uska parent re-render hua Uska koi context value badla Uske hook (useSyncExternalStore etc.) ne update bheja Props badalna list mein nahi hai — props tabhi badalte hain jab parent re

Wraps a component to memoize its render. Skips re-render if props are shallowly equal. Fails silently with object/array/function props created inline. How does React.memo work? Why does it often fail to prevent re-renders with object or function props? React.memo HOC jo props same hone par re-render skip karta hai Shallow compare har prop ko Object.is se compare — andar nahi jhaankta Custom comparator apna compare function dena Definition: React.memo(Component) component ko lapet deta hai. Parent render hone par React pehle props ko shallow compare karta hai — sab same hain to component ko chalata hi nahi. Shallow = har prop pe Object.is . Object ke andar nahi dekhta, sirf reference.

React.memo + useCallback is the classic pattern: memo prevents re-render, useCallback prevents the function reference from changing on every parent render. Explain the React.memo + useCallback pattern. When is it necessary and when is it premature optimization? Triad teeno ka saath mein kaam karna Memoization chain ek toota to poori chain bekaar Definition: Teeno alag cheezein hain par saath mein kaam karti hain: React.memo — component ka render rokta hai useMemo — value ka reference stable rakhta hai useCallback — function ka reference stable rakhta hai Rule: React.memo ke bina baaki dono bekaar hain (except effect deps ke liye).

React.lazy() enables dynamic import() for components. Suspense shows a fallback while the bundle loads. Reduces initial bundle size and TTI. How does React.lazy and Suspense work? What is the network request pattern it generates? Bundle saara JS ek file mein — bada ho to page late khulta hai Chunk bundle ka alag tukda jo alag se download hota hai Lazy zaroorat padne pe hi load karna Definition: Code splitting bade bundle ko chhote chunks mein todna hai, jo tabhi download hote hain jab chahiye. React mein React.lazy() + <Suspense> se. lazy(() => import('./X')) ek dynamic import hai — bundler ise dekhkar X ko alag file bana deta hai.

Only render DOM nodes for visible items. Libraries like react-window and TanStack Virtual keep a constant-size DOM regardless of list length. What is list virtualization? Explain how react-window implements it. What are its limitations? Virtualization sirf jo dikh raha hai utne hi DOM nodes banana Window screen ka wo hissa jo abhi dikhta hai Overscan window ke thoda upar-neeche extra rows — scroll smooth rahe Definition: 10,000 rows ka DOM banana browser ko maar dalta hai. Virtualization mein sirf ~20 visible rows ka DOM banta hai; scroll pe unhi nodes ko naye data ke saath reuse kar liya jaata hai. Poori list ki height ek spacer div se fake ki jaati hai taaki scrollbar sahi lage.

The Profiler API and DevTools flamegraph show render durations, commit counts, and which component triggered a render — the starting point for any perf investigation. How do you identify performance bottlenecks in a React app? Walk me through your debugging process. Profiler React DevTools ka tab jo render measure karta hai Flamegraph chart jisme har component ka render time bar ki tarah dikhta hai Commit ek update jisme DOM badla Definition: React DevTools Profiler record karta hai ki kaunsa component kab, kitni der, aur kyun render hua. Ye "why did this render" ka jawab andaaze se nahi, data se deta hai. <Profiler> component se tum programmatically bhi timings collect kar sakte ho.

Lifting static children via props.children or slot props means they are created by the parent, not the child — so they don't re-render when the child's state changes. How can component composition prevent unnecessary re-renders without using React.memo? Composition component ko props/children ke through jodna children as props JSX ko prop ki tarah pass karna Element identity React element ka wahi object hona Definition: Agar tum JSX ko parent ke bahar banate ho aur children prop se andar bhejte ho, to us element ka reference badalta nahi. Jab wrapper ka state badalta hai, React children ko same element dekh kar uska render skip kar deta hai — bina memo lagaaye.

React can now pause, interrupt, and restart rendering work. High-priority updates (user input) can interrupt low-priority renders in progress. What is Concurrent Mode? How does interruptible rendering improve user experience? Concurrent ek se zyada UI version ek saath tayyar rakhna Interruptible render beech mein rok ke baad mein resume karna Urgent vs non-urgent kaunsa update turant chahiye, kaunsa ruk sakta hai Definition: Concurrent React ka matlab hai ki React ek render ko rok, resume, ya phenk sakta hai. Ye koi feature nahi jise "on" karte ho — ye ek capability hai jo createRoot se milti hai, aur jise tum useTransition / useDeferredValue / Suspense se use karte ho. Parallel nahi hai — J

Suspense catches "not ready yet" signals from lazy components or data libraries, shows a fallback, and re-renders when data is ready — enabling a waterfall-free fetch-on-render model. How does Suspense work for data fetching vs code splitting? What does a library need to do to support Suspense? Suspense boundary jo "abhi ready nahi" wale children ke liye fallback dikhata hai Fallback jab tak ready na ho tab tak dikhne wala UI Suspend component ka "main abhi tayyar nahi" bolna (promise throw karke) Definition: <Suspense fallback={...}> ek boundary hai. Uske andar ka koi component agar "abhi ready nahi" ho (lazy chunk load ho raha ho, ya data aa raha ho), to React fallback dikhata hai au

Mark a state update as non-urgent. React can interrupt and defer it in favour of urgent updates like typing. Returns [isPending, startTransition]. What does useTransition do? Give a concrete example where it prevents the UI from feeling sluggish. Transition wo update jo ruk sakta hai — non-urgent isPending boolean jo batata hai transition chal raha hai Urgent update typing, click — turant dikhna chahiye Definition: const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition() . startTransition(fn) ke andar ke state updates ko React non-urgent maanta hai — koi urgent update aaya to inhe rok deta hai ya discard karke dobara chalata hai. isPending se tum "loading" feel de sakte ho bina purana content ha

Returns a deferred version of a value — React shows the stale value while re-rendering with the new value in the background. What is the difference between useDeferredValue and useTransition? When would you reach for one over the other? Deferred value value ka thoda purana version Debounce fixed time wait karna — timing tumhare haath mein Throttle fixed rate pe chalane dena Definition: const deferred = useDeferredValue(value) value ka ek "peechhe chalne wala" version deta hai. React pehle nayi value ke saath urgent UI update karta hai, phir background mein deferred value ke saath dobara render karta hai. Farak useTransition se: transition mein tum update ko wrap karte

Components that run only on the server — zero JS in the bundle, direct database/filesystem access, no hooks or state. Client Components still run on both. What are React Server Components? What can and can't they do? How do they differ from SSR? RSC React Server Component — server pe chalta hai, browser mein kabhi nahi Client Component purana normal component — browser mein chalta hai "use client" file ke top pe likha directive jo boundary banata hai Definition: Server Components sirf server pe render hote hain. Unka JavaScript browser ko bheja hi nahi jaata — sirf render ka natija (ek special serialized format) jaata hai. Isliye unme state, effects, event handlers nahi ho sakte. Par wo asyn

React 18's renderToPipeableStream streams HTML as it's ready. Selective hydration lets React prioritise hydrating the part the user interacts with first. How does streaming SSR work? What is selective hydration and why does it improve interactivity (TTI)? SSR server pe HTML banake bhejna Hydration server ke HTML pe client JS ko "jodna" taaki interactive ho Streaming HTML tukdon mein bhejna, poora ban-ne ka intezaar kiye bina Definition: Purana SSR "all-or-nothing" tha — poora page ka data aane tak kuch nahi bheja jaata tha. Streaming SSR mein server jo ready hai wo turant bhej deta hai, aur baaki tukde baad mein aate hain, Suspense boundaries ke hisaab se. Selective hydration — React un hiss

The use() hook (React 19+) reads resources like Promises or Context inside render — unwrapping Promises and suspending automatically. What does the use() hook do? How does it differ from await and useEffect for async data? use() naya React API jo promise ya context "padh" leta hai Unwrap promise se andar ki value nikalna Conditional call if ke andar call karna — use() ke liye ye allowed hai Definition: use(promise) promise ko unwrap karta hai — jab tak resolve na ho, component suspend ho jaata hai (Suspense fallback dikhta hai). use(context) context bhi padh sakta hai. Ye "hook" hai par baaki hooks jaisa nahi — ye conditionally aur loops mein call ho sakta hai .

A function that takes a component and returns an enhanced component — the classic pre-hooks reuse pattern. Now largely replaced by custom hooks. What is an HOC? What problems does it solve and what problems does it create (wrapper hell, prop collision)? HOC function jo component leta hai aur naya component return karta hai Wrapper hell kai HOC nest hone se DevTools mein 8 layer hoistStatics wrapped component ke static properties copy karna Definition: Higher-Order Component ek function hai: Component → Component . Ye purana component leta hai aur usko kuch extra props/behaviour ke saath lapet ke naya component deta hai. Aaj custom hooks ne iski jagah le li hai — par HOC abhi bhi kuch ca

Sharing behaviour by passing a function as a prop that returns JSX. Gives the consumer full control over the rendered output. What is the render props pattern? Compare it to HOCs and custom hooks for sharing logic. Render prop wo prop jiski value ek function hai jo JSX return karti hai Children as function children ko function ki tarah pass karna Inversion of control kya render hoga ye consumer decide kare Definition: Component logic rakhta hai aur rendering ka faisla consumer pe chhod deta hai — ek function prop ke through jise wo apna state deta hai. <Mouse render={pos => <p>{pos.x}</p>} /> ya children-as-function.

A parent component implicitly shares state with a set of child components via Context — creating expressive, flexible APIs like + . What is the compound component pattern? Build a Tabs component using it. Compound components kai components jo milkar ek unit banate hain Implicit state parent ka state jo children ko context se milta hai Flexible layout user decide kare kaunsa hissa kahan ho Definition: Ek parent component apne bacchon ko context se state deta hai. User <Tabs><Tabs.List><Tabs.Tab/></Tabs.List><Tabs.Panel/></Tabs> likhta hai — HTML ke <select>/<option> jaisa.

Class components implementing getDerivedStateFromError / componentDidCatch that catch render errors in their subtree and show fallback UI. What are Error Boundaries? What errors do they NOT catch? Why must they be class components? Error Boundary class component jo apne bacchon ki render errors pakadta hai getDerivedStateFromError error pe fallback UI dikhane ke liye state set karta hai componentDidCatch error log karne ke liye Definition: Error Boundary ek class component hai jo apne children ke render, lifecycle aur constructor ki errors pakadta hai aur crash ki jagah fallback UI dikhata hai. Ye nahi pakadta: event handlers, async code (setTimeout, promise), server-side rendering, aur khud

ReactDOM.createPortal renders children into a different DOM node than the parent — useful for modals and tooltips that need to escape overflow:hidden or z-index stacking. What are Portals? Why do modals use them? How does event bubbling work through a Portal? Portal child ko DOM mein kahin aur render karna, tree mein wahin rakhte hue Stacking context CSS ka wo scope jisme z-index ki tulna hoti hai Event bubbling event ka parent tak upar jaana Definition: createPortal(children, domNode) children ko kisi bhi DOM node mein render karta hai — par React tree mein wo wahin rehta hai . Matlab context milta hai, events React parent tak bubble hote hain, par DOM mein wo document.body mein hai.

forwardRef passes a ref through a component to a child DOM node. useImperativeHandle customizes what the parent sees when it uses that ref. When and why do you need forwardRef? What is the difference between forwardRef and useImperativeHandle? forwardRef ref ko andar ke DOM node tak pahunchana useImperativeHandle ref se kya kya milega wo customize karna Imperative API method call karke kaam karana (declarative ka ulta) Definition: ref normal prop nahi hai — React use alag treat karta hai, isliye wo apne aap child ke andar nahi jaata. forwardRef se tum use andar ke DOM node tak pahuncha sakte ho. useImperativeHandle se tum ref ke through poora DOM node dene ki jagah sirf chuni hui methods de

Wrapping a subtree with a Provider to inject dependencies (services, config, state) without prop drilling — the foundation of most React library APIs. How does the Provider pattern work in React? How is it used as dependency injection for testing? Dependency Injection dependency bahar se dena, andar banane ki jagah Provider wo component jo dependency deta hai Composition kai providers ko jodna Definition: Provider pattern mein tum services/config ko Context ke through tree mein daalte ho. Component sochta nahi ki API client kahan se aaya — bas useApi() maangta hai. Ye React ka dependency injection hai.

Separate data-fetching/logic (container) from pure rendering (presentational). Now done naturally with custom hooks extracting logic from display components. What is the container/presentational pattern? How has it evolved with hooks? Container data laane wala component — logic Presentational sirf dikhane wala component — UI Dumb component presentational ka purana naam Definition: Purana pattern — Container data laata hai aur logic rakhta hai, Presentational sirf props leke UI banata hai. Aaj: hooks ne containers ki zaroorat lagbhag khatam kar di. Par idea zinda hai — bas ab wo "logic hook mein, UI component mein" ban gaya hai. RSC mein ye wapas strong ho gaya (se

"Test the behaviour users see, not implementation details." Queries mirror what users and assistive technology perceive — avoiding brittle tests tied to component internals. What is the React Testing Library philosophy? Why is testing implementation details harmful? RTL React Testing Library — user ki tarah test karne wali library Query element dhoondhne ka tarika — getByRole, getByText... Implementation detail andar ka code jo user ko dikhta hi nahi Definition: RTL ka ek hi principle hai — "tests jitne zyada user ke istemaal jaise hon, utna zyada bharosa dete hain" . Isliye RTL state, props, ya internal functions ko touch hi nahi karta. Wo sirf screen pe jo dikhta hai usse baat karta hai. Q

Test: user interactions, rendered output, async state changes, error states. Do NOT test: internal state, component method calls, or prop types. What makes a good React component test? What should you avoid testing and why? Testing trophy Kent C. Dodds ka model — integration tests sabse zyada Coverage kitna code test se chhua gaya — quality ka proof nahi Regression purana feature naye change se toot jaana Definition: Sab kuch test karna waste hai. Test wahi karo jahan toot-ne ka nuksaan zyada ho: User flows — login, checkout, form submit Business logic — price calculation, permission, validation Edge cases — empty, error, loading, bahut lamba text Purane bugs — har fix ke saath ek test (regr

MSW (Mock Service Worker) intercepts at network level — most realistic. jest.mock replaces modules. Both have their place; MSW is preferred for API tests. What is MSW and why is it better than mocking fetch/axios directly in tests? MSW Mock Service Worker — network level pe API intercept karta hai vi.mock / jest.mock module ko nakli banana Handler MSW mein ek endpoint ka nakli response Definition: Do tarah ka mocking: MSW — network level pe intercept. Tumhara code asli fetch call karta hai; MSW use pakad ke nakli response deta hai. vi.mock — module level pe replace. Poora module nakli. API ke liye MSW behtar hai .

renderHook from RTL wraps hooks in a minimal component so you can test stateful logic in isolation without building a full UI around it. How do you test a custom hook that manages state and side effects? Walk through testing useFetch. renderHook hook ko test mein chalane ka helper act state update ko wrap karna taaki React use process kar le wrapper provider jo hook ko chahiye Definition: Hooks ko akele test karne ke liye renderHook . Wo ek chhota component banata hai jo tumhara hook call karta hai, aur result.current se uski return value deta hai. Par pehle sochо — agar hook kisi component mein use ho raha hai, to component ka test aksar zyada valuable hai.

waitFor retries assertions until they pass or timeout. findBy queries are async. act() wraps state updates to ensure React flushes before assertions. What is act() and when do you need it explicitly? waitFor jab tak assertion pass na ho tab tak retry karta hai findBy getBy + waitFor ek saath Fake timers timer ko nakli banana taaki test mein wait na karna pade Definition: React mein async kaam (fetch, timer, transition) ke baad DOM turant update nahi hota. RTL ke async tools: findBy* — element aane ka intezaar (appear ke liye) waitFor(fn) — koi bhi assertion pass hone tak retry waitForElementToBeRemoved — spinner jaane ka intezaar

SSR har request pe server HTML banata hai SSG build ke waqt HTML ban jaata hai ISR SSG + background mein time-time pe regenerate Definition: Next.js React ke upar ka framework hai — routing, rendering strategies, bundling, image optimization, API routes sab built-in. Hydration server HTML pe client JS jodkar use interactive banana Mismatch server aur client ka HTML alag hona suppressHydrationWarning ek element ke liye warning band karna Definition: Server HTML bhejta hai (dikhta hai par interactive nahi). next/image automatically optimises images (lazy loading, responsive sizing, WebP/AVIF, CDN). next/font optimises font loading (self-hosted, no FOUT, layout-shift-free). API routes (app/api/) let you build backend endpoints inside your Next.js app. Server Actions (v14+) let you call async functions directly from form actions and Server Components without creating API routes — handling mutations server-side. Route Handler app/api/*/route.ts — HTTP endpoint Server Action server pe chalne wala function jo client se call ho sakta hai "use server" directive jo function ko Server Action banata hai Definition: Do tarike server pe kaam karne ke: Route Handler — app/api/x/route.ts mein GET / POST export karo. Edge runtime user ke paas wale server pe chalna — tez par limited APIs Node runtime poora Node.js — sab kuch chalta hai standalone build output jisme sirf zaroori files hoti hain — Docker ke liye Definition: Next.js kai jagah deploy ho sakta hai: Vercel — zero config, sab features (ISR, image optimization, edge) kaam karte hain Docker / self-host — ou

React Hook Form uncontrolled inputs pe based fast form library Resolver validation schema (zod/yup) ko RHF se jodne wala adapter register RHF mein input ko form se jodna Definition: Form banane ke 3 raste: Controlled useState — chhote forms (1-3 fields) ke liye theek React Hook Form — uncontrolled + refs. prop-types: runtime type checking (legacy, replaced by TypeScript). defaultProps: default values for undefined props (deprecated in function components, use default parameters instead). refs callback: function refs for custom logic on mount/unmount. Why are defaultProps deprecated for function components? What replaces them? PropTypes runtime pe props check karne wali purani library defaultProps props ki default value dene ka purana tarika Callback ref ref ki jagah function dena — mount/unmount pe chalta hai Definition: Teen legacy cheezein jo interview mein aati hain: PropTypes — runtime type check.
