x: How elements flow: block (full width), inline (no box dimensions), inline-block (box + inline flow). What is the difference between block, inline, and inline-block? Give a use case for each. block Poori width leta hai, nayi line se shuru; width/height/margin sab kaam karte hain. inline Text ke flow mein; width/height ignore, vertical margin ka layout effect nahi. inline-block Inline ki tarah flow karta hai par block ki tarah width/height leta hai. Definition: display decide karta hai element kaise flow karega. div , p block hote hain; span , a inline; inline-block dono ka mix; none element ko hata deta hai (layout se bhi). Aaj layout ke liye zyada tar flex aur grid use hote hain.

t: CSS Core — Selectors, Cascade, Box Model
x: Adjacent vertical margins collapse to the larger value; when it happens and how to prevent it. What is margin collapsing? Show a case where it surprises developers. Margin collapsing Do adjacent vertical margins add nahi hote — bada wala rehta hai. BFC Block Formatting Context — iske andar margins bahar ke margins ke saath collapse nahi karte. Parent-child collapse Child ka top margin parent ke bahar nikal jata hai agar beech mein padding/border na ho. Definition: Block elements ke vertical margins jab touch karte hain to jodte nahi, balki bada wala hi lagu hota hai ( 20px + 30px = 30px ). Ye sirf vertical direction mein, normal block flow mein hota hai. Flex/grid items ke margins collapse n

n: Units — px, em, rem, %, vw/vh, ch
t: CSS Core — Selectors, Cascade, Box Model
x: Absolute vs relative units; em (relative to parent font-size) vs rem (root); viewport and content units. What is the difference between em and rem? When would you choose each? rem Root (html) font-size ke relative — predictable, accessibility ke liye best. em Current element ke font-size ke relative (padding/margin mein) ya parent ke (font-size mein) — nest karne par compound hota hai. vw / vh / ch Viewport width/height ka 1% aur '0' character ki width. Definition: Absolute: px . Relative: % (parent), em , rem , viewport units ( vw , vh , dvh ) aur content units ( ch , ex ). Font-size ke liye rem , component-internal spacing ke liye em , borders ke liye px common hai.

t: CSS Core — Selectors, Cascade, Box Model
x: --var declarations, var() with fallbacks, scoping/cascade, runtime theming, contrast with Sass variables. How do CSS custom properties differ from Sass variables? Why are they powerful for theming? Custom property --brand: #0a84ff; — apna variable, runtime par change ho sakta hai. var() var(--brand, fallback) se value padhna, fallback ke saath. Scope Variable cascade/inherit hota hai — element par override karo to uske children par lagta hai. Definition: CSS custom properties --name se declare hoti hain aur var(--name) se use. Ye normal cascading properties hain isliye selector, media query ya JS se runtime par badli ja sakti hain. Sass variables compile-time par replace ho jate hain, isliye

flex container vs items, main/cross axis, justify-content, align-items, align-content, flex-direction. Explain the flexbox axes. How do justify-content and align-items differ? Main axis Flex direction ki line (row mein horizontal). justify-content isi par kaam karta hai. Cross axis Main ke perpendicular. align-items isi par kaam karta hai. Flex container display:flex wala parent; uske direct children flex items bante hain. Definition: Flexbox ek dimension (row ya column) mein items ko align aur space dene ka layout system hai. Container par display:flex lagao; flex-direction main axis tay karta hai. justify-content = main axis, align-items = cross axis, gap = items ke beech spacing, flex-wra

The flex shorthand; how items distribute free space; flex-basis vs width; flex:1 meaning. What does flex: 1 expand to and what does it actually do? flex-grow Free space mein se kitna hissa lena hai (ratio). flex-shrink Space kam ho to kitna sikudna hai. flex-basis Grow/shrink se pehle item ki starting size (width se zyada priority). Definition: flex: grow shrink basis shorthand hai. flex: 1 = 1 1 0 — barabar hissa. flex: none = na grow na shrink. flex: 0 0 200px = fixed 200px. Pehle flex-basis se starting size, phir bacha hua (ya kam padha hua) space grow/shrink ratio se baanta jata hai.

grid-template-columns/rows, fr unit, repeat(), gap, minmax(), auto-fit vs auto-fill. When would you choose Grid over Flexbox? Explain fr and minmax(). fr unit Free space ka fraction — 1fr 2fr = 1:2 ratio. minmax() Track ki min aur max size — minmax(200px, 1fr) . auto-fit / auto-fill repeat() ke saath jitne tracks fit hon utne banao; auto-fit khaali tracks collapse kar deta hai. Definition: CSS Grid 2D layout hai: rows aur columns dono. Container par display:grid aur grid-template-columns/rows se tracks define karo; items khud cells mein lag jate hain. gap tracks ke beech spacing hai.

Named grid-template-areas, grid-column/row line placement, spanning, implicit vs explicit grid. How do grid-template-areas work? When are they clearer than line-based placement? grid-template-areas Layout ko ASCII-art jaisa naam dena — padhne mein aasan. Line placement grid-column: 1 / 3 — line numbers se item ko span karana. Implicit grid Jo tracks aapne define nahi kiye par content ke wajah se bane. Definition: grid-template-areas se layout ko naam diye jate hain, aur item par grid-area: name lagate hain. Alternatively line numbers/ span se placement: grid-column: 1 / span 2 . Explicit grid wo hai jo template mein likha; baaki extra items implicit tracks mein jate hain.

Normal flow vs positioned; containing block; offsets; sticky = relative until threshold then fixed. Explain each position value. What is the containing block for an absolutely positioned element? Containing block Absolute element ka reference — nearest positioned ancestor (relative/absolute/fixed/sticky). sticky Relative jaisa chalta hai jab tak scroll threshold na aaye, phir fixed jaisa chipak jata hai. Offset top/right/bottom/left — sirf positioned elements par kaam karte hain. Definition: static (default, normal flow), relative (apni jagah se offset, space reserve rehta hai), absolute (flow se bahar, nearest positioned ancestor ke hisaab se), fixed (viewport ke hisaab se), sticky (scroll

What creates a stacking context (position+z-index, opacity, transform), why z-index:9999 can fail. Why can a z-index: 9999 element still appear behind another? Explain stacking contexts. Stacking context Ek isolated layer group — iske andar ke z-index sirf andar ke liye matter karte hain. z-index Positioned/flex/grid items ki layer order; sirf apne stacking context ke andar compare hota hai. Isolation isolation: isolate bina side-effect ke naya stacking context banata hai. Definition: Naya stacking context banta hai jab: root element, position + z-index (auto nahi), opacity < 1 , transform , filter , isolation:isolate , aur kai aur cases mein. Do alag contexts ke elements ki comparison pa

Flex/grid centering, margin auto, absolute + transform, when each applies. Give me three ways to center a box both horizontally and vertically. Trade-offs of each? Flex centering display:flex; justify-content:center; align-items:center . Grid centering display:grid; place-items:center — sabse chhota. margin auto Block ko horizontally center karta hai jab width set ho. Definition: Context ke hisaab se centering: text ke liye text-align:center ; fixed-width block ke liye margin-inline:auto ; dono axis ke liye flex ya grid; overlay ke liye position:absolute + inset:0; margin:auto .

Historical layout with floats, clearfix hack, why floats caused collapsing parents. What were floats originally for and why did they get abused for layout? float Element ko left/right side par hata kar text ko uske around wrap karana. clearfix Hack jo float wale children ke baad parent ko unki height tak khichta hai. flow-root Modern, clean clearfix: display: flow-root . Definition: float original use text ko image ke around wrap karna tha. 2000s mein ise layout (columns) ke liye hijack kiya gaya, jiske liye clear/clearfix hacks chahiye the. Aaj layout ke liye flex/grid hain; float sirf image-text wrapping ke liye reh gaya.

@container queries size components by their container, not the viewport — true component responsiveness. How do container queries differ from media queries? Why are they a big deal for design systems? Container query @container (min-width: 400px) — component apne container ki width dekh kar style badalta hai. container-type Parent ko 'container' banana: container-type: inline-size . cqw / cqi Container query units — container width ka 1%. Definition: Media query viewport dekhti hai; container query component ka apna parent. Parent par container-type: inline-size lagao aur child mein @container likho.

min-width/max-width breakpoints, feature queries, orientation, prefers-color-scheme / reduced-motion. How do media queries work? What does prefers-reduced-motion let you do? Breakpoint Viewport width jis par layout badalta hai — content decide kare, device nahi. Feature query @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) , (prefers-reduced-motion) , (hover: hover) . @supports Browser support check — media query nahi, feature query. Definition: @media conditional CSS hai: viewport width ( min-width / max-width ), orientation, aur user preferences (dark mode, reduced motion, contrast) ke hisaab se rules lagate hain. Modern syntax: @media (400px <= width <= 900px) .

Base styles for small screens, layer up with min-width; why it produces simpler, faster CSS. What does mobile-first mean in practice? Why is it preferred over desktop-first? Mobile-first Base CSS chhoti screen ke liye, phir min-width se bade screens par layer. Progressive enhancement Basic experience sab ko, behtar features capable devices ko. Desktop-first Base bade screen ke liye, max-width se chhote par override — zyada overrides. Definition: Pehle sabse chhoti screen ka layout likho (default CSS, bina media query ke), phir jaise jagah badhe @media (min-width) se complexity add karo.

clamp(min, preferred, max) for fluid font sizes and spacing without breakpoints. How does clamp() work? Write a fluid font-size that scales between 16px and 24px. clamp(min, val, max) Value ko min aur max ke beech rakhta hai; val viewport ke saath badhta hai. Fluid scale Font/spacing continuously scale hote hain, breakpoints par jump nahi. Accessibility Sirf vw ki font-size zoom ko tod deti hai — rem ke saath mix karo. Definition: clamp(1rem, 0.8rem + 1vw, 1.5rem) font ko viewport ke saath smoothly scale karta hai, par kabhi 1rem se chhota ya 1.5rem se bada nahi hone deta.

Serving right-sized images per viewport/DPR, sizes attribute, for art direction, aspect-ratio. How do you avoid shipping a 2000px image to a phone? Explain srcset + sizes. srcset w-descriptor Har candidate ki real width: img-800.jpg 800w . sizes Browser ko batata hai image layout mein kitni wide dikhegi, taaki wo sahi candidate chune. aspect-ratio aspect-ratio: 16/9 se image load hone se pehle jagah reserve (CLS se bachav). Definition: srcset + sizes se browser viewport aur DPR ke hisaab se best image chunta hai; <picture> alag crop ya format deta hai; CSS mein max-width:100%; height:auto aur aspect-ratio image ko fluid rakhte hain.

vw/vh/vmin/vmax, the mobile 100vh address-bar problem, dvh/svh/lvh dynamic units. Why does 100vh behave badly on mobile browsers, and how do dvh/svh fix it? vh / vw Viewport height/width ka 1%. svh / lvh / dvh Small / large / dynamic viewport height — mobile address bar ke hisaab se. vmin / vmax Chhoti ya badi dimension ka 1%. Definition: vw/vh viewport relative hain. Mobile par address bar scroll par chhupti-dikhti hai to 100vh ek fixed (large) viewport maanta hai aur content bar ke neeche chhup sakta hai. Fix: dvh (dynamic, bar ke saath badalta), svh (hamesha safe, chhota), lvh (bar hata kar).

font shorthand, line-height, letter-spacing, font stacks/fallbacks, web-safe fonts, text-wrap: balance. What makes body text readable? Talk about line-height, measure, and font fallbacks. font stack Fallback list: font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif . line-height Unitless value (1.5) best — font-size ke saath scale hoti hai. text-wrap: balance Headings ki lines ko barabar balance karta hai (widows kam). Definition: Readable typography ke levers: font-family stack, font-size , line-height (body text ~1.5), letter-spacing , max-width in ch (45–75 chars), aur text-wrap ( balance headings ke liye, pretty paragraphs ke liye).

overflow visible/hidden/scroll/auto, single-line ellipsis, multi-line line-clamp. How do you truncate a single line of text with an ellipsis? What about multi-line? overflow visible (default), hidden , scroll , auto , clip . text-overflow: ellipsis Kata hua text '…' ke saath; nowrap + overflow:hidden ke saath chahiye. line-clamp Multi-line truncation: -webkit-line-clamp: 3 + display:-webkit-box . Definition: Single-line ellipsis ke liye teen properties ek saath: white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis . Multi-line ke liye line-clamp .

State selectors, structural pseudo-classes, :focus-visible vs :focus, :not(), functional pseudo-classes. What is the difference between :focus and :focus-visible? Why does it matter for accessibility? :focus-visible Focus ring sirf keyboard navigation par — mouse click par nahi. :nth-child() Position ke basis par: :nth-child(2n) , :first-child . :not() / :has() Exclude karna; :has() parent selector jaisa kaam karta hai. Definition: Pseudo-classes element ki state ya position select karte hain: :hover , :focus-visible , :checked , :disabled , :nth-child() , :not() , :has() .

Generated content, the content property, decorative shapes, icons, and layout tricks. What is the difference between a pseudo-class and a pseudo-element? ::before / ::after Element ke andar ka generated content; content property zaroori hai. ::placeholder / ::selection Input placeholder aur selected text ko style karte hain. content: "" Decorative shape ke liye khaali string de ke box banao. Definition: ::before / ::after element ke content se pehle/baad ek virtual child banate hain. Isme content dena zaroori hai (khaali ho to "" ). Decorative icons, underline effects, clearfix, overlays me use hote hain.

background shorthand, multiple backgrounds, linear/radial/conic gradients, background-size/position. How do you layer multiple backgrounds? What is the difference between cover and contain? background-size cover (poora bhare, crop ho sakta hai) vs contain (poora dikhe). linear/radial/conic-gradient Image ki jagah CSS-generated gradients. Multiple backgrounds Comma se kai layers: background: url(a), linear-gradient(...) . Definition: background shorthand mein color, image, position, size, repeat. Gradients background-image hote hain. Multiple backgrounds upar se neeche stack hote hain (pehla sabse upar).

border-radius, box-shadow (inset, spread), drop-shadow filter vs box-shadow, outline vs border. What is the difference between box-shadow and filter: drop-shadow? When does each matter? box-shadow x y blur spread color ; inset andar ki shadow. filter: drop-shadow Element ke actual shape (transparent PNG/SVG) ke hisaab se shadow. outline vs border Outline layout space nahi leta aur focus ring ke liye hai. Definition: border-radius corners round karta hai ( 50% = circle). box-shadow element ke box ke peeche shadow banata hai; multiple shadows comma se. outline border jaisa hai par layout nahi badalta.

transition-property/duration/timing-function/delay, which properties are animatable, easing curves. How does a CSS transition work? Which properties are cheap to animate and which are expensive? transition Property ki value badalne par smooth interpolation: transition: opacity .2s ease . timing-function Easing curve: ease , ease-out , cubic-bezier() , linear() . Animatable property Jiski value continuous ho (color, transform, opacity). display normally nahi. Definition: Transition property ki value ek state se doosri par jaate waqt beech ke frames khud banata hai. Trigger state change se hota hai (hover, class toggle). Syntax: property duration timing-function delay .

@keyframes, animation shorthand, iteration, direction, fill-mode, play-state. How do @keyframes differ from transitions? When would you reach for each? @keyframes Animation ke steps define karta hai: from / to ya percentages. animation-fill-mode forwards = end state rukti hai; backwards = delay mein start state. animation-iteration-count Kitni baar: number ya infinite . Definition: @keyframes name { 0% {...} 100% {...} } se multi-step animation banti hai; element par animation: name 1s ease-in-out infinite alternate lagate hain. Ye trigger ke bina apne aap chal sakti hai.

2D/3D transforms, transform-origin, why transforms do not trigger layout, will-change. Why is animating transform smoother than animating top/left? translate / scale / rotate 2D transforms; ab individual properties bhi hain: translate: 10px . transform-origin Jis point ke around rotate/scale ho (default center). will-change Browser ko hint ki ye property badlegi — layer promote ho sakti hai. Definition: transform element ko visually move/scale/rotate/skew karta hai bina layout badle (doosre elements ki jagah wahi rehti hai). Order matter karta hai: translate() rotate() aur rotate() translate() alag result dete hain.

Animate only transform & opacity to stay on the compositor; avoid layout/paint thrash; will-change budget. Which two properties can you animate without triggering layout or paint, and why? Compositor-only transform aur opacity main thread ke bina GPU par animate hote hain. Layout / paint thrash width , top , box-shadow animate karna har frame par layout/paint karwata hai. will-change budget Sirf jaha zarurat ho tabhi; bahut layers memory khate hain. Definition: Smooth animation ke liye sirf transform aur opacity animate karo. Ye properties layout aur paint skip karke compositor par chalti hain, jabki width/height/top/left layout, aur background/box-shadow paint trigger karte hain.

DOM + CSSOM → render tree → layout → paint → composite; render-blocking CSS/JS; how the browser paints. Walk me through how the browser turns HTML and CSS into pixels on screen. Render tree DOM + CSSOM ka combine; sirf visible nodes. Render-blocking CSS (aur sync JS) page ka first paint rok dete hain. Layout → Paint → Composite Geometry nikalna, pixels bharna, layers ko GPU par jodna. Definition: Browser HTML se DOM, CSS se CSSOM banata hai, dono se render tree, phir layout (positions/sizes), paint (pixels), composite (layers). CSS render-blocking hai; sync JS parser-blocking aur CSSOM par bhi wait karta hai.

Layout (reflow) recalculates geometry; paint fills pixels; composite layers GPU-blend. Which props trigger which. What is the difference between reflow, repaint, and composite? Which is most expensive? Reflow (layout) Elements ki geometry dobara calculate — mehenga. Repaint Pixels dobara bharna (color/shadow badla, geometry nahi). Composite Layers ko GPU par jodna — sabse sasta. Definition: Property badalne par browser kitna kaam karta hai: layout ( width , margin , font-size , top ) → paint → composite. Paint-only : color , background , box-shadow . Composite-only : transform , opacity . Layout badle to paint aur composite bhi hote hain.

Forced synchronous layout from read-after-write in JS; batching reads then writes; requestAnimationFrame. What is layout thrashing? How do you avoid forced synchronous layout in a loop? Forced synchronous layout Style badalne ke turant baad layout property padhna — browser ko layout turant karna padta hai. Batching Pehle saare reads, phir saare writes. requestAnimationFrame Visual updates ko next frame se pehle schedule karna. Definition: Layout thrashing tab hoti hai jab loop mein read ( offsetHeight ) aur write ( style.height = ... ) alternate hote hain — har read par browser layout recompute karta hai.

Largest Contentful Paint, Cumulative Layout Shift, Interaction to Next Paint; targets and common fixes. What are the Core Web Vitals and what causes a poor score in each? LCP Largest Contentful Paint — sabse bada content kab dikha (target ≤ 2.5s). CLS Cumulative Layout Shift — layout kitna hila (target ≤ 0.1). INP Interaction to Next Paint — click/tap ke baad screen kitni jaldi update hui (target ≤ 200ms). Definition: Core Web Vitals real-user experience ke 3 metrics hain: LCP (loading), CLS (visual stability), INP (responsiveness; FID ki jagah aaya). Fixes: LCP image preload/optimize, CLS ke liye image width/height aur font fallback, INP ke liye long tasks todna.

font-display swap/optional, preloading fonts, fallback metrics, layout shift from font swaps. What is the difference between FOUT and FOIT? How does font-display control it? FOUT Flash of Unstyled Text — fallback font dikhta hai, phir swap. FOIT Flash of Invisible Text — font aane tak text chhupta hai. font-display swap , optional , fallback — loading behaviour control karta hai. Definition: Web font load hone tak browser text ko ya to chhupata hai (FOIT) ya fallback se dikhata hai (FOUT). font-display: swap fallback turant dikhata hai aur font aane par swap karta hai; optional sirf cache mein ho to use karta hai (shift nahi).

contain property, content-visibility: auto to skip offscreen rendering, performance isolation. What does content-visibility: auto do for a long page? contain Browser ko batana ki subtree ke changes bahar affect nahi karte: layout , paint , size , style . content-visibility: auto Offscreen content ka rendering skip, scroll par render. contain-intrinsic-size Skip kiye hue content ki placeholder size (scrollbar jump rokne ke liye). Definition: contain se browser ko hint milta hai ki element ke andar ke changes bahar layout/paint ko affect nahi karenge, to wo kaam ko isolate kar sakta hai. content-visibility: auto offscreen sections ka layout/paint skip kar deta hai.

BEM block__element--modifier, why naming conventions fight specificity and scale in large codebases. What problem does BEM solve? How does it keep specificity flat? Block Independent component: .card . Element Block ka hissa: .card__title (double underscore). Modifier Variant/state: .card--featured (double hyphen). Definition: BEM (Block__Element--Modifier) ek naming convention hai: .block__element--modifier . Isse class ka naam hi batata hai ki wo kis component ka hissa hai.

Locally scoped class names, hashing, composition; solving the global namespace problem. How do CSS Modules prevent class-name collisions? What does the build step do? Local scope Class names file ke andar local; build tool unhe unique hash banata hai. composes Ek class mein doosri class ke styles reuse karna. Global escape :global(.x) jab global class chahiye. Definition: *.module.css file import karne par har class name ek unique generated name ban jata hai ( card_3xK9a ), isliye collision possible nahi. Aap styles.card se use karte ho.

Runtime vs zero-runtime CSS-in-JS, dynamic styling from props, SSR concerns, performance trade-offs. What are the pros and cons of CSS-in-JS? What is the runtime cost? Runtime CSS-in-JS styled-components/emotion: JS mein styles, runtime par CSS inject hota hai. Zero-runtime Linaria/vanilla-extract/Panda: build time par static CSS. Props-based style Component ke props se dynamic styles. Definition: CSS-in-JS styles ko component ke saath JS mein likhta hai (template literals ya objects). Runtime libraries render ke dauran CSS inject karti hain; zero-runtime tools build time par static CSS nikaal dete hain.

Utility classes, design tokens via config, purge/JIT, when utility-first helps or hurts maintainability. What is the case for and against Tailwind / utility-first CSS? Utility class Ek hi kaam wali class: p-4 , flex , text-center . Design tokens Spacing/colors config mein tay; utilities unse bante hain. JIT / purge Sirf use hui classes ka CSS generate hota hai. Definition: Utility-first (Tailwind) mein HTML par chhoti single-purpose classes lagake style karte hain, custom CSS likhne ke bajay. Config (theme tokens) se consistent spacing/colors milte hain.

Token layers, CSS variables for theming, prefers-color-scheme, per-component theming without JS. How would you architect a themeable design system that supports light/dark and brand themes? Design token Naam wali design decision: --color-bg , --space-4 . Semantic token Purpose-based naam ( --color-surface ) vs raw value ( --gray-900 ). prefers-color-scheme User ka OS-level dark/light preference. Definition: Tokens ko do layers mein rakho: primitive ( --blue-600 ) aur semantic ( --color-primary: var(--blue-600) ). Theme badalna matlab semantic tokens ko re-map karna; components sirf semantic tokens use karte hain.

Sass nesting/mixins/functions, native CSS nesting, cascade layers (@layer) for predictable ordering. What do preprocessors still offer now that CSS has variables and nesting? Sass Variables, nesting, mixins, functions — compile hoke CSS banta hai. Native CSS nesting .card { &:hover {...} } — ab browsers mein built-in. @layer Cascade layers: pehle declare kiye layers ka order specificity se upar hota hai. Definition: Sass jaise preprocessors CSS ko features dete the jo native nahi the (variables, nesting, mixins). Aaj CSS variables, nesting, @layer , color-mix() native ho gaye hain, isliye preprocessor ki zarurat kam hai. @layer reset, base, components, utilities; se ordering specificity ke b

Props interface, naming conventions, required vs optional, TypeScript generics for component APIs API surface component ke wo saare props jo bahar wale use karte hain Escape hatch ek prop jo user ko default behaviour se bahar nikalne deta hai (className, render) Prop explosion har nayi zaroorat pe naya prop — 20 props ka component Definition: Component API design ka matlab hai — component ka public contract tay karna: kaunse props, kya naam, kya required, kya default, aur kya nahi dena. Design round mein interviewer sabse pehle yahi poochta hai — "iska API kya hoga?" Tumhara jawab props ki list nahi, ek soch honi chahiye: kau

When each fits, forwardRef, useImperativeHandle, ref forwarding patterns Controlled value parent ke state se aati hai Uncontrolled component apni value khud rakhta hai Hybrid dono support karna — value diya to controlled, nahi to internal Definition: Design round mein sirf "controlled vs uncontrolled" batana kaafi nahi — dono support karo . Production component ka standard yahi hai: value prop diya to controlled, nahi diya to component apna state rakh le ( defaultValue se shuru). Ye pattern har achhi library mein hai — Radix, MUI, Re

Implicit state sharing via Context, flexible composition, dot notation API (Tabs.Panel etc.) Compound kai components jo milkar ek widget banate hain Implicit state parent ka state jo children ko Context se apne aap milta hai Slot wo jagah jahan user apna content daal sakta hai Definition: Ek parent state rakhta hai aur Context se apne bacchon ko deta hai. User HTML jaisa likhta hai — <Tabs><Tabs.List><Tabs.Tab/></Tabs.List><Tabs.Panel/></Tabs> . Design round mein ye flexibility ka jawab hai — jab interviewer poochta hai "agar client tab

children pattern, render props, slot pattern — avoiding prop explosion Composition chhote pieces jodkar bada banana Configuration ek component ko props se sab kuch batana Slot pattern named prop jisme JSX aata hai — header, footer, actions Definition: Do rasta hai flexibility dene ka: Configuration — <Card title icon actions showBorder /> . Simple, par har naya case naya prop. Composition — <Card><Card.Header/><Card.Body/></Card> . Zyada likhna, par unlimited flexibility. Beech ka rasta: slots — <Card

Keep state as close to usage as possible — lifting vs drilling vs context vs global store Colocation state ko usi jagah ke paas rakhna jahan wo use hota hai Lifting state up state ko common parent tak upar le jaana Prop drilling props ko 4-5 level neeche pass karte jaana Definition: State ko utna hi upar rakho jitna zaroori hai — ek level bhi zyada nahi. Default sabse neeche; jab do bhaiyon ko chahiye tabhi upar uthao. Design round mein ye performance ka sabse pehla jawab hai — memo se pehle.

ARIA roles/states/properties, keyboard navigation, focus management, screen reader testing ARIA Accessible Rich Internet Applications — screen reader ke liye extra info Roving tabindex group mein sirf ek element tab-focusable, baaki arrow keys se Focus trap modal ke andar focus ko band rakhna Definition: Accessibility ko baad mein "add" nahi kiya jaata — component ke design mein hi aata hai. Char cheezein har widget mein chahiye: Semantic HTML — <button> , <nav> , <dialog> (div pe onClick nahi) Keyboard — Tab, Enter/Space, Arrow, Escape, Home/End ARIA — role, state ( ar

Only render visible rows — react-window, TanStack Virtual, overscan, dynamic row heights Windowing sirf visible items ka DOM banana Overscan window ke thoda bahar extra rows — scroll smooth rakhne ko Variable height har row ki alag height — sabse mushkil case Definition: 10,000 rows ka DOM browser ko maar dalta hai. Bulk endpoints accept arrays of operations (/users/batch) to avoid N+1 request overhead. For slow operations, return 202 Accepted with a status URL the client polls for completion. How do you design batch endpoints and async processing patterns? When would you use 202 Accepted? Bulk operations Batch of items in one request — POST /batch, arrays. Async processing Long tasks: 202 Accepted + job status endpoint. Idempotency keys Bulk/async retry-safe. Polling Client GET /jobs/{id} to track. Bulk : multiple resources ek request mein (POST /orders/batch with array, or 2000 rows upload). Saves round-trips; response per-item results. Async : slow work (video transcode, report gen) — accept quickly

Clients retry on 429/5xx with exponential backoff (delay = base * 2^n + jitter). Circuit breakers stop calling failing services after N failures and probe periodically for recovery. What is exponential backoff with jitter? How does a circuit breaker differ from simple retries? Retry Transient failure pe request repeat. Backoff Wait time badhaana retries ke beech. Jitter Random add — thundering herd se bachat. Max retries 3-5 typically — sirf idempotent par. Exponential 2x wait each attempt: 1s, 2s, 4s... CORS lets server say "is origin ko access hai". Simple requests (GET/header basic) directly; others preflight OPTIONS pehle, then main request. Config: Access-Control-Allow-Origin

n: Primary Key — uniquely identifies every row

What properties must it satisfy? Primary Key Har row ki unique pehchaan — duplicate nahi, NULL nahi. Unique Constraint — koi value ek baar se zyada na aaye. Surrogate key Banaayi hui key (auto-increment id, UUID) — koi asli matlab nahi. Natural key Data se aayi key — jaise Aadhaar number, email. Index PK par DB khud index banata hai — fast lookup. n: Foreign Key — links rows across tables

Referential integrity Rule: FK value us parent table mein honi hi chahiye. ON DELETE CASCADE Parent delete to child bhi delete. ON DELETE SET NULL Parent delete to child ka ref NULL ho jaye. n: Filtering rows — WHERE, AND, OR, NOT
x: WHERE filters which rows are returned. Supports comparisons (=, !=, ), logical operators (AND, OR, NOT), pattern matching (LIKE), set membership (IN), range (BETWEEN), and null checks. How does WHERE filter rows? What operators does it support? WHERE Row filter — only jo condition match, wahi aage jaaye. AND / OR / NOT Logical combine: sab / koi ek / ulta. IN Kisi set mein membership — IN (1,2,3). BETWEEN Range check — age BETWEEN 18 AND 30. LIKE Pattern match — name LIKE 'A%'. WHERE rows ko chhaanta hai. Operators: = , != , < , > , LIKE (pattern), IN (membership), BETWEEN (range), IS NULL (null check), aur AND / OR / NOT se combine. Classic trap: WHERE email = NULL kabhi nahi chalegi

CRUD = Create, Read, Update, Delete. INSERT INTO creates rows, SELECT reads, UPDATE modifies, DELETE removes. Always use WHERE with UPDATE/DELETE or you affect every row. n: What is an Index? — when to add one, B-tree vs hash (concept)
x: An index is a data structure that speeds up row lookups at the cost of slower writes. Without an index, the database scans every row (sequential scan). With an index, it jumps directly to the matching rows. Think of a book index — instead of reading every page, you look up the topic and go straight there. What is a database index? When should you add one and when should you not? Index Data structure jo lookups ko fast karta — book index jaisa. Seq scan Bina index — har row padho (slow pada large table). B-tree index Sorted tree — range + equality dono. Hash index Hash function — sirf equality, O(1). Write cost Har insert/update par index update bhi hota — writes slow. Index = book ka index.

n: B-Tree & B+Tree — structure, fanout, range scans
x: B+ Trees are the default index in most databases. Self-balancing trees with data only in leaf nodes, which are linked for fast range scans. Height is 3-4 for billions of rows — very few disk seeks. How does a B+ Tree index work? Why is it efficient for both lookups and range scans? B+ Tree Default index — sorted tree; data sirf leaves mein, leaves linked. Fanout Har node mein kitne children — bada = tree chhota. Range scan Leaf linked list se aage-piche walk — fast. Height Root se leaf tak levels — billions rows par 3-4. B-Tree vs B+Tree B-tree: data har node mein. B+: sirf leaf mein. B+ range scan behtar. B+ Tree relaional DB ka default index hai. LSM-Trees make writes super fast by writing to memory first (memtable), then flushing sorted files (SSTables) to disk. Background compaction merges SSTables. Trade-off: reads check multiple files. How does an LSM-Tree optimize write performance? What is the write path? LSM-Tree Write-optimized structure — memory pehle, phir sorted files. Memtable RAM mein sorted collection — writes yahan. n: Buffer pool — LRU, dirty pages, checkpoints
x: The buffer pool is the database RAM cache. Reads check memory first (cache hit = instant). On miss, reads from disk, stores in pool. When full, evicts least recently used page. Target: 95%+ hit rate. What is a buffer pool? How does it improve database performance? Buffer pool DB ka RAM cache — pages yaad rahne. Cache hit Page RAM mein mil gaya — no disk read. Dirty page RAM mein change hua par disk par likha nahi. LRU Least Recently Used — kam use wala page nikalo. Checkpoint Dirty pages ko disk par bolna — jhank jhank ke. Buffer pool database ki RAM cache hai. Har read pehle RAM mein dekhta hai ( hit = instant, miss = disk). Full hone par allocation kam use ( LRU ) page ko nikaalta hai. Dir

DB-per-tenant: fully isolated (highest cost, easiest to customize). Row-Level Security (RLS) enforces tenant isolation at DB level. What are the tradeoffs between shared DB, schema-per-tenant, and DB-per-tenant? Multi-tenancy Ek software kai customers (tenants) — data alag se. Isolation models Pooled (shared DB, tenant_id), Schema-per-tenant, Separate DB. tenant_id Pooled model ka apna address — har query mein. Schema-per-tenant Alag schema per customer — clean boundary, ops moderate. RLS PG Row-Level Security — tenant_id a

Monitoring tracks key health signals. Most important metrics: query latency p95/p99, active connections, cache hit rate (>95% target), disk I/O, replication lag. PostgreSQL built-in views expose all of this. What are the most important database metrics to monitor in production? Monitoring DB health visibility — metrics, logs, dashboards. Key metrics CPU, connections, cache hit, slow queries, replication lag, disk. Slow query log Kitne ms se upar wale — tuning targets. PgBouncer / pool Connection churning kam karta. Alerting Rules par notifications — pings, thresholds. DB monitoring = duniya ki nadi visible rakho. Metrics: CPU , connections (pool chahiye), cache hit ratio (>95%), slow quer

Opening a new DB connection takes 5-100ms and PostgreSQL spawns a process. Connection pooling keeps a fixed number of connections open and reuses them. Optimal pool size is ~2x CPU cores. Why is connection pooling necessary? What happens without it? Connection pool DB connections ka reusable set — har request naya na bane. Overhead TCP handshake + auth + memory — new conn expensive. Pool size CPU ke aas-paas — (core*2)+disk; hazaaron conn = thrash. PgBouncer PG connection pooler — transaction pooling mode. HikariCP Java default — sane defaults + fast borrow. Har query ke liye nayi DB connection banana = TCP + auth + worker + memory ka kharcha. Connection pool ready-made connections ka bucket

n: Backup & recovery — PITR via WAL, RPO/RTO
x: PITR (Point-in-Time Recovery) restores to any specific moment using a base backup + archived WAL files. RPO = max data loss. RTO = recovery time. Test your backups by actually restoring them. How does Point-in-Time Recovery work in PostgreSQL? Backup Data ko alag jagah copy — restore ke liye. PITR Point-in-Time Recovery — kisi bhi moment tak restore. WAL archiving Har WAL segment S3 par — continuous log. Full + incremental Base snapshot + changes — storage/time balance. RPO / RTO Kitna data loss tolerance / kitni der mein up. Backup = disaster ke liye copy. PITR (PostgreSQL): base backup + WAL archiving — kisi bhi moment par restore (ghalti se delete hua data bachta hai). Full base + increme

Schema migrations in production are dangerous. Safe strategy: Expand (add new column), Migrate (backfill in batches), Contract (drop old column). Tools like gh-ost and pgroll do online migrations with no locking. What is the Expand-Migrate-Contract pattern? Why is it safer than direct ALTER TABLE? Expand & Contract Additive first, deploy, remove old later — zero downtime. Shadow writes Naya column bhi write — old readers still fine. Online DDL tools gh-ost, pt-online-schema-change — copy + swap, bina lock. Lock storm Direct ALTER on big table = table lock = downtime. Backfill Naye column ko purana data — batched jobs. Zero-downtime schema change = Expand & Contract : 1) expand — additive col

SQL injection is the #1 database attack. ALWAYS use parameterized queries. RBAC gives minimum required privileges. Row-Level Security in PostgreSQL enforces which rows each user can see at the database level. How do you prevent SQL injection? Why are parameterized queries essential? SQL injection App ke SQL mein attacker ka chhupa code ghusana. Prepared statement Query ka skeleton + params alag — SQL parse fixed. Parameterized Values bind, kabhi string concat nahi. RBAC Role-Based Access Control — role → permissions. RLS Row Level Security — row visibility per policy. Least privilege Sirf utna access jitna kaam ka. SQL injection = SQL ke andar attacker ka chhupa code: WHERE email = 'admin' O

n: N+1 problem — detection, eager loading, DataLoader
x: The N+1 problem: load a list (1 query) then load details for each item (N queries). 100 posts + comments = 101 queries. Fix: eager loading with JOINs or batch loading with DataLoader. What is the N+1 query problem? How do you detect and fix it? N+1 problem 1 query root + N queries children — kaafi network hops. Eager loading Pehle se children le aao — ORM joins/with. JOIN fetch Ek query mein parent + children (ORM). Batch window IN (ids...) — children ko ek query mein. DataLoader GraphQL/Node — request mein batching + cache. N+1 : root ke 1 record ke liye ek query, phir 100 records ke liye 100 queries — slow. Example: SELECT posts + har post ke liye SELECT comments . Fixes: JOIN (rows flat —

n: URL Shortener DB — sharding, caching, pre-generated keys
x: URL shortener maps short codes to long URLs. Read-heavy (99% reads). Shard by short code hash. Cache hot URLs in Redis. Pre-generate codes to avoid uniqueness checks on each write. How would you design the database layer for a URL shortener at scale? URL shortener Long URL → chhota code → redirect. Encode id → base62 (a-zA-Z0-9) — chhota code. Collision Alag URLs same short code — unique row pehle. Redirect 301 (permanent, cache) vs 302 (temporary). Bloom filter Sab used codes ka set — collision check fast. Expiry TTL per short URL — cleanup. URL shortener design (tinyurl): POST long URL → return abc123 ; GET /abc123 → 301 Location redirect. Storage: short_code PK + long_url + created_at + c

Chat needs message ordering per conversation, low latency delivery. Shard by conversation ID so all messages in one chat stay together. Use sequence numbers per conversation for ordering. How do you ensure message ordering in a distributed chat system? Chat system DM + group — messages, presence, unread. Real-time WebSocket push — bade scale par LB + fan-out. Message model conversation_id, sender_id, ts, content — index. Fan-out Ek message kai receivers ko — queues/read replicas. Presence Online status — Redis + heartbeats. Unread counters Redis incremented per conversation. Chat system design : send message → store (Postgres/Cassandra) + push via WebSocket . conversation_id fixed slot; mess

n: News Feed DB — push vs pull, celebrity handling
x: Push (fan-out on write): copy post to all follower feeds — fast reads, expensive for celebrities. Pull (on read): fetch from followed users — expensive reads. Hybrid: push for normal users, pull for celebrities. What is the difference between fan-out-on-write and fan-out-on-read? News feed Har user ka personalized timeline — posts from followed. Fan-out on write Post time hi followers ke feeds mein daal do — read cheap. Fan-out on read Serve samay merge — hot users ok, celebs bhi fine. Hybrid Normal users write-fanout, celebrities read-merge. Feed cache Redis list per user — precomputed timeline. Ranking Recency/engagement score — feed reorder. News feed design = har user ka personal timelin

An OS is software that manages computer hardware and provides services to programs. Without it, every app would need to talk to hardware directly. Examples: Linux, Windows, macOS, Android, iOS. What is an operating system and why do we need one? Operating System (OS) Wo software jo computer ke hardware (CPU, memory, disk) aur aapke programs ke beech setu ka kaam karta hai. Resource Computer ki wo cheez jo kaam aati hai — CPU ka time, memory, disk, keyboard, screen. User space Jahan aapke programs chalti hain. Kernel space Jahan OS khud chalta hai — hardware par poori pakad. Computer ka asli badan (hardware) hai — CPU, RAM, disk. Par aap jaise chrome kholte ho, wo directly CPU/disk se baat na

Batch OS (jobs queued, no interaction), Time-sharing OS (multiple users share CPU, e.g. Linux), Real-time OS (hard deadlines, e.g. flight systems), Distributed OS (across machines), Mobile OS (Android, iOS). What are the different types of operating systems? Give a real-world example of each. Batch OS Kaam pehle jama kar, phir ek saath process karo — koi interaction nahi. Time-sharing OS Ek CPU ko kai users mein chhota-chhota time dekar sabko "apna" lagwana. Real-time OS (RTOS) Pakki deadline — agar miss hui to disaster. Distributed OS Kai computer milkar ek saath kaam karein, user ko lage ek hi ho. Mobile OS Chhota-device (phone/tablet) ke liye bana OS — Android, iOS. OS alag-alag kaamo ke

n: Kernel — The Core of the OS
x: The kernel is the core program that runs at all times. It manages CPU, memory, devices, and files. User space = where your apps run. Kernel space = where the OS runs. Apps cannot touch hardware directly — they ask the kernel. What is the kernel? What is the difference between user space and kernel space? Kernel OS ka dil — hardware se seedha baat karta hai, har waqt memory mein rahta hai. User space Jahan aapke apps chalti hain (Internet browser, games). Kernel space Jahan OS chalti hai — hardware par full control. Privilege level CPU ka batawara — kaun kitni taaqat use kar sakta hai (Ring 0 = OS, Ring 3 = app). OS poori koi ek cheez nahi — uske beech ka dil hai kernel . Restaurant ke staff

n: System Calls — How Programs Talk to the OS
x: A system call is how a user program requests a service from the kernel. Examples: open() (open a file), read() (read data), write() (write data), fork() (create a process), exit() (terminate). Every file operation, network call, or memory allocation goes through a syscall. What is a system call? Why do we need them — why can't programs access hardware directly? System call App ka kernel se request — "ye hardware ka kaam karke do". Syscall System call ka chhota naam. Trap Wo hardware-darwaaza jisme app kernel ke paas jaata hai (Ring 3 se Ring 0). Context switch (syscall wala) App ka data save, kernel ka load, phir wapas. Jab app ko koi OS ka kaam karna hai — file kholo, data padho, naya proce

Power on → BIOS/UEFI (hardware check, find boot device) → Bootloader (GRUB loads kernel) → Kernel (initializes drivers, mounts filesystem) → Init/systemd (starts system services) → Login shell / Desktop. This is what happens before you see the login screen. Explain what happens from the moment you press the power button to when the OS is ready. BIOS/UEFI Computer ke "jaag-te" ka pahla software — abhi OS nahi chala. Bootloader Chhoti program jo kernel ko memory me load karke chalati hai (GRUB). Kernel init Kernel jab chalta hai — drivers, filesystem, memory set karta hai. init/systemd OS pehli service — baaki saare background processes isi ke bachchhe. A process is an independent program with its own memory. A thread is a lightweight execution unit within a process sharing memory. What is the difference between a process and a thread? What resources does each own? Process Ek program jo memory mein chal raha hai. Uska apna ghar (memory), apna kagaz (files), apna sab kuch. Thread Process ke andar ka ek kaam-gunda. Ek process ke andar kai threads, sab ek hi ghar mein rehte hain. Thread-safe Jab kai threads ek hi cheez ko chhoo rahe hon, phir bhi sab theek chale. Process = ek chhota sa "ghar" jisme program rehta hai. Agar do programs chalao to do alag ghar — ek ko pata nahi doosre ke ghar mein kya hai. Thread = usi ghar ke andar ka kaam karne

Data structure the OS maintains for each process — PID, state, CPU registers, memory maps, open files. What information is stored in a Process Control Block? Why does the OS need it? PID Har process ka apna number (ID card number jaisa). PCB Process Control Block — OS ka register jisme har process ki poori history likhi rehti hai. Registers CPU ke andar ke chhote dabbe jahan abhi chalke hua data rehta hai. OS ko har process ki poori jankari rakhni padti hai — naam nahi, sab. Ye jankari ek packed file mein rehti hai, usi ko PCB kehte hain. Jab koi process banta hai (app khulta hai), OS use ek PCB deta hai — jaise school mein admission par ek file banti hai.

The OS saves the current process state and loads another process state — enables multitasking but has overhead. Explain context switching. What is its cost and how can it be minimized? Context switch CPU ka ek process chhod ke doosre par jaana — aur wapas aane ka rasta yaad rakhna. Context Wo "kahaan hain" — save ki hui state jahan se resume karna hai. Overhead Switch karne mein jo extra mehnat/time lagta hai. CPU ek waqt mein ek hi kaam karta hai. Par computer ko "sab ek saath chalta hai" dikhana hai. Iski trick ye hai: CPU bahut tezi se ek process chhod, doosra pakad, phir pehla pakad. Har baar "chhodne" par wo note likhta hai — main yahan tak tha . Is note ko likhna aur doosre ka note pad

New → Ready → Running → Waiting → Terminated. Understanding state transitions is key to debugging hung processes. Describe the lifecycle of a process. Draw the state diagram and explain each transition. Ready Kaam ke liye taiyar, par CPU abhi maujood nahi. Running CPU iska kaam kar raha hai — iski baari. Waiting/Blocked Kisi cheez ka wait — input ya I/O ka. CPU ise chhod chuka hai. Har process ka ek chhota sa "jeevan" hota hai — kaafi phase jo ek ke baad ek aata hai: New (bana) → Ready (taiyar, par number) → Running (CPU mila) → Waiting (kisi cheez ka wait) → Running wapas → Terminated (khatam). Sabse zaroori transition: Running ⇄ Waiting . Jab process I/O ka wait karta hai (j

User threads managed by runtime library (fast, no syscall). Kernel threads managed by OS (can use multiple cores). What is the difference between user-level and kernel-level threads? What are green threads? Kernel thread OS khud banati hai — CPU cores taak jaa sakta hai. Bhaari, par matter hai. User thread Program ke andar ka thread — OS par nirbhar (diesel). Green thread User thread jo runtime khud manage karti hai (JS/Python wale). Do thread ke do prakaar: Kernel thread — OS khud banati hai. Use asli CPU core milta hai, kai cores par saath mein chalta hai. Banaane (syscall) ka thoda time lagta hai. User thread — program ke andar ka, runtime sambhalta hai. fork() duplicates a process; exec() replaces process image with a new program. Together: spawn a child process. Explain fork() and exec(). What is copy-on-write and how does it make fork() efficient? fork() Process ki ek nayi copy banana — doosra process banna jaisi same program ki. exec() Us nayi copy ke andar purana program hata kar naya program daalna. Copy-on-write Sasta tariqa: copy sirf naam ki hoti hai, asli copying tabhi hogi jab kuch badala jaaye. Process ko naya kaam karna hai (jaise koi badhiya program chalana hai). Do kaam karne padte hain: 1. fork() — apni ek "game ki copy" banaana (naya process). Ab do same program hain — parent aur child. 2. exec() — us nayi copy ke andar pura

Stack: LIFO, fast, automatic, limited size. Heap: dynamic, manual (or GC), large, slower allocation. Explain stack vs heap memory. What goes on each? What causes a stack overflow? Stack Memory ka fast hissa — LIFO, automatic. Function call, local variables. Chhota (fixed size). Heap Memory ka bada hissa — dynamic, aap khud mangaate ho. Slow, par bada. Stack overflow Stack khatam ho gaya — zyada deep recursion → crash. Fragmentation Heap mein chhote-chhote khaali tukkde bikhre — naya bada block nahi milta. Ek program chalti hai to use memory do hisson mein milti hai: Stack — sabse fast. Har function call par ek "tikki" (frame) upar rakha jaata hai, wapas hote hi hata deta hai. LIFO (last in,

Each process sees its own private address space. OS maps virtual addresses to physical RAM using page tables. What is virtual memory? How does it enable process isolation and allow programs larger than physical RAM? Virtual address Jo pata program ko dikhta hai (jaise 0x4000) — real nahi. Physical address Asli RAM ka pata — jo hardware par hota hai. Page tables Chhoti book — har virtual pata ko physical bata-ti hai. Isolation Har program ka apna alag area — doosra nahi chhoo sakta. Har program ko lagta hai ki uski poori RAM sirf usi ki hai — jaise 0 se 4GB tak, sab uska. Par ye jhooth hai. OS virtual address space banata hai — ek fake, safe, bada space jahan program khelta hai. Physical memory divided into fixed-size frames. Virtual memory divided into pages. Page table maps pages to frames. Explain paging. What is a page fault and how is it handled? Page Virtual memory ka chhota hissa (fixed, e.g. 4KB). Frame Asli RAM ka utna hi chhota hissa. Page table Map: page → frame. Page fault Wanted page RAM mein nahi — disk se uthana pada (slow). TLB Chhoti fast cache of page table — recent translations. Memory ko chhote-chhote same-size blocks mein kato (jaise book ke pages). Virtual side ke block ko page kehte hain, physical (RAM) side ke block ko frame . Page table bata-ti hai ki kaunsa page kaunse frame mein padi hai. Jab program kisi page ko chhoo-ta hai jo RAM mein n

Memory divided into logical segments (code, data, stack). Each segment has base + limit registers. What is segmentation? How does it differ from paging? What are its advantages and problems? Segment Memory ka logical hissa — code, data, stack, etc. (koi ek hissa). Base Segment ka shuru hone ka pata (RAM). Limit Segment ki lambai — kitna bada hai. External fragmentation Bikhri khaali jagah — nayi segment ke liye ek saath badi jagah nahi milti. Paging ne memory ko fixed blocks mein kato, par segmentation logical hisson mein kato — code, data, stack alag-alag segment. Har segment apna base (kahaan shuru) aur limit (kitna lamba) rakhta hai. Program ka pata aisa likha hota hai: (segmentNo, offset

When RAM is full and a new page is needed, the OS must evict one. FIFO, LRU, LFU, Clock algorithm. Explain LRU page replacement. What is Belady's anomaly? Page fault Wanted page RAM mein nahi — uthana pada. FIFO Sabse pehle aaya wala hatao. Simple, par galat ho sakta hai. LRU Least Recently Used — sabse kam time pe use hua hatao. Best, par mehenga. Belady anomaly FIFO mein frames badhane par bhi zyada faults — ulta! Clock LRU ka sasta approximation — hardware friendly. Jab RAM bhar jaati hai aur naya page chahiye, OS ko ek purana page hata kar nikaalna padta hai. Kaunsa nikale? Yahi page replacement strategy hai. FIFO — sabse pehle bhar aaya wala hatao. Simple par achha nahi. LRU — sabse kam

A memory leak is heap memory that is allocated but never freed. GC automates deallocation via reference counting or mark-and-sweep. How do memory leaks happen in languages with and without GC? How do you detect them? Memory leak Heap ki memory jo khud li gayi par kabhi free nahi hoti — program aage use ho raha hai. GC (Garbage Collector) Jo objects ab use nahi ho rahe, wo khud free kar deta. Mark & sweep GC ka tarika: root se jo sab reachable use mark karo; jo mark na hue wo free. Stop-the-world GC chalte waqt program ruk jaata — pause se latency. Reference counting Har object ke use-count; 0 hote hi free. (Cycles mein fail.) Leak = memory tumne li (allocate), par kabhi wapas nahi di jab wo

Maximize CPU utilization and throughput. Minimize turnaround time, waiting time, and response time. What are the goals of CPU scheduling? What trade-offs exist between throughput and latency? CPU utilization CPU kitna time busy rehta hai — kam khali na rahe. Throughput Ek second mein kitne processes khatam hote hain. Turnaround time Process shuru hone se khatam hone tak ka pura time. Response time Input dene se pehla output aane tak ka time — interactive systems mein important. Preemptive OS beech mein rok kar kisi aur ko CPU de sakta hai. Scheduler ka kaam: kaun sa process kab CPU chalaye . Par "best" ka matlab cheez-par-nirbhar hai — isliye goals define karte hain. System goals: CPU busy r

First-Come-First-Served: simple, convoy effect. Shortest Job First: optimal avg wait, needs future knowledge. Compare FCFS and SJF. What is the convoy effect? Why is SJF optimal but impractical? FCFS First Come First Served — jo pehle aaya wo pehle (queue jaisa). Convoy effect Ek lamba process sab ko piche rokh deta hai — traffic jam. SJF Shortest Job First — sabse chhota kaam pehle. Optimal avg wait. SRTF Shortest Remaining Time First — preemptive SJF. Starvation Chote processes aate rahein to lamba kabhi nahi chattas — bhuka reh jaata. Aging Purane processes ki priority badhao taaki bhuke na rahein. FCFS — sabse simple. Jo process pehle bazaar aayi usi ko CPU. Order = arrival order. Dikkt:

Each process gets a fixed time quantum in a circular queue. Good for time-sharing systems. Explain Round Robin scheduling. How does quantum size affect performance and response time? Time quantum Har process ko utna samay (ek "slice") CPU milta hai. Ready queue Circular queue — process time khatam hote hi piche lag jata. Preemptive Quantum khatam ho to OS rok kar agla laga deta. Context switch overhead Har switch par state save/restore ka time — overhead. Round Robin — har process ko ek fixed time quantum diya jaata hai, phir agla. Order circular hai — aakhri ke baad pehle wapas. Har process ko barabar time milta hai — koi bhuka nahi rehta. Isliye interactive/time-sharing ke liye best. Par q

Higher priority processes run first. Multilevel feedback queues adapt priority dynamically. Explain priority scheduling with aging. What is a multilevel feedback queue? Priority Har process ko ek number — zyada wala pehle. Aging Wait badhne par priority badhao — starvation rokne ke liye. Multilevel feedback queue Kai queues (alag priority); process behaviour se queue badal sakta. Completely Fair Scheduler (CFS) Linux ka scheduler — sabko fair CPU time (vruntime). nice value Linux mein priority adjust karne ka user-level knob (-20 to 19). Priority scheduling — har process ki ek priority hoti hai; sabse zyada priority wala pehle. Par risk: low-priority process kabhi CPU na paaye → starvation .

Hard real-time: must meet deadlines (EDF, RMS). Soft real-time: best effort (multimedia, UI). What is the difference between hard and soft real-time systems? What is Earliest Deadline First? Hard real-time Deadline pakki — miss hui to disaster (safety-critical). Soft real-time Deadline best-effort — miss hui to quality girti, disaster nahi. RMS Rate Monotonic — chhoti period wala high priority. EDF Earliest Deadline First — sabse jaldi deadline wala pehle. Optimal. PREEMPT_RT Linux ka real-time patch — preemption zyada, latency kam. Real-time = har kaam ki ek deadline hoti hai. Hard : deadline miss hui to fail (brake system, pacemaker). Soft : miss hui to quality girti (video call, game) — p

Files are named byte sequences. Directories are files that map names to inodes. Everything in Unix is a file. How does a file system organize data on disk? What is the difference between a file, inode, and directory? File Bytes ka ek named sequence — data ko naam se rakho. Directory (folder) Khud bhi ek file — jo naam→inode ka map rakhta hai. Inode File ka "identity card" — metadata (size, permissions, data blocks). Everything is a file Unix ka funda — file, disk, device, pipe sab file jaisa behave karta. Path Root se file tak ka rasta — /home/user/a.txt. Disk par data raw bytes ki tarah pda hota hai. File system usko organise karta hai — files (named byte sequences) aur directories (jo file

An inode stores metadata about a file (size, permissions, timestamps, data block pointers) but NOT the filename. What is an inode? What information does it store? What is the inode table? Inode File ka metadata — size, perms, owner, timestamps, data-block pointers. Inode number File ka unique ID filesystem ke andar. Inode table Saari inodes ka area — disk par fix hota. Link count Kitne names is inode ko point karte hain. Direct/indirect blocks Chhote data direct pointer; lamba data indirect blocks se (multi-level). Inode file ka metadata card hai — usme file ka content nahi, par file ke baare mein sab: size, owner, permissions, timestamps aur data blocks kahan hain . File ka naam yahan Nahi

An integer that represents an open file in a process. 0=stdin, 1=stdout, 2=stderr. File descriptor table per process. What is a file descriptor? What happens when you open() a file? File descriptor (fd) Ek integer jo process ke andar kholi hui file/device/socket ko represent karta. File table OS-level — global open files ka record (offset, inode). FD table Per-process — kitne open fds hain, kis global file ko point karta. stdin/stdout/stderr 0,1,2 — default open fds (input, output, error). Too many open files FD limit khatam — ulimit -n se dekh/barha sakte. File descriptor ek integer hai — process apni kholi hui file ko is number se pehchanta hai. open() par OS ek naya fd deta hai (har proce

Log changes before applying them to ensure consistency after crash. Write-ahead logging. Used in ext4, NTFS, HFS+. What is a journaling file system? How does it protect against corruption after a crash? Journal (log) Pehle "kya badalne wala hai" log karo, phir file system par lagao. Write-ahead logging Badlav apply karne se pehle usko log karna. Crash consistency Achanak power cut par file system corrupt na ho. ext4/NTFS/HFS+ Journaling file systems — data/metadata log. Metadata journaling Sirf metadata (directory/inode) log; data blocks nahi. File system par kai writes ek saath honi hoti hain (inode + data block + directory). Agar power beech mein gayi, to kuch likha kuch nahi → corruption

FCFS, SSTF (shortest seek time), SCAN (elevator), C-SCAN. Minimize disk seek time. Explain SCAN (elevator) disk scheduling. Why is it better than FCFS for HDDs? Seek time Read/write head ko correct track tak jaane ka time — HDD ka sabse bada cost. FCFS Jo request pehle aayi turant serve — simple par seek zyada. SSTF Shortest Seek Time First — sabse paas wala pehle. SCAN (elevator) Head ek side se doosri side jaata, raste ke requests serve. C-SCAN Sirf ek direction mein serve, head wapas turant (uniform wait). HDD mein read/write head ek track se doosre tak jaana hai — isi ko seek kahte hain aur ye sabse slow. Disk scheduler requests ka order isi tarah lagata hai ki head kam ghoome. FCFS — aa

Pipes: unidirectional byte stream between related processes. Named pipes (FIFOs): persist in filesystem, any two processes. How do pipes work? What is the difference between anonymous and named pipes? Pipe Unidirectional byte stream — ek process likhta, doosra padhta. Anonymous pipe Related processes (parent-child) ke beech — shell 's | . Named pipe (FIFO) Filesystem mein naam se — koi bhi do process. Buffer Pipe mein kernel ka temporary storage; agar bhar to writer block. Reader/Writer Ek side data daalta (in), doosri side nikalta (out). Pipe ek ek-disha (one-way) byte stream hai — ek process andar likhta hai, doosra bahar padhta hai. Order maintain hota (FIFO). Anonymous pipe : parent-chil

Fastest IPC — two processes map the same physical memory pages. Requires synchronization (semaphores/mutexes). How does shared memory IPC work? Why is it the fastest IPC mechanism? Shared memory Do (ya zyada) processes ek hi physical memory pages map karein. mmap / shm mmap ya shmget se shared region banaya. Synchronization Data hi share hai to races rokne ke liye mutex/semaphore chahiye. Race condition Dono ek saath likhein to galat data — sync ke bina. Fastest IPC Kernel copy nahi — seedha memory, isliye sabse tez. Shared memory — do processes ek hi physical memory pages ko apni virtual space mein map karte hain. Jo ek likhta, doosra turant dekh sakta — bina kernel copy ke . Isliye yahi fa

Message queues: asynchronous, typed messages. Sockets: network or Unix domain, bidirectional, flexible. Compare message queues, shared memory, and sockets for IPC. When would you choose each? n: Distributed Systems Networking — gossip protocols, consistent hashing
x: Gossip protocol: nodes periodically exchange state with random peers — converges without central coordination. Consistent hashing maps keys to nodes with minimal reshuffling on topology changes. How do gossip protocols work and where are they used? What problem does consistent hashing solve? Gossip protocol Info nodes ke beech viral (eventually consistent). Consistent hashing Nodes par hash-ring se data distribution. Virtual nodes Uneven distribution se bachne ke liye. Membership Kaunse nodes upar hain — gossip se detect hota hai. Gossip protocol — information nodes ke beech viral tarah spread hoti hai: har node apni jaankari friends ko batata hai, chain reaction se sab jaante hain. Clusters

n: Rate Limiting — token bucket, leaky bucket, sliding window
x: Token bucket refills tokens at steady rate — burst up to bucket size. Leaky bucket processes at steady rate — excess queued/dropped. Sliding window counters over recent time window. Compare token bucket, leaky bucket, and sliding window rate limiting algorithms. When would you use each? Token bucket Tokens bucket mein, fixed rate refresh — burst allow. Leaky bucket Fixed rate output queue — smooth, no burst. Sliding window Recent exact window count — precise. Redis counter Distributed rate limiting ke liye Lua/atomic. Rate limiting kisi client ya service ke requests ki sankhya ko rokna hai. Algorithms: token bucket — bucket tokens se bhara, har request ek token consume, fixed rate par tokens

n: Backpressure & Flow Control — TCP, HTTP, reactive streams
x: Backpressure prevents a fast producer from overwhelming a slow consumer. TCP flow control (receiver window). HTTP/2 flow control (per-stream WINDOW_UPDATE). Reactive Streams demand-based push. What is backpressure and why is it critical in distributed systems? How do TCP and HTTP/2 implement flow control? Backpressure Producer ko slow kar dena jab consumer overburdened. Flow control TCP window — receiver buffer capacity. Reactive streams Publisher/Subscriber with demand signal. HOL blocking Slow stream piche wale ko rokna. Backpressure & flow control system ko overrun hone se rokta hai jab producer consumer se fast ho. TCP window size se flow control karta hai — receiver buffer bharne pa

n: Network Performance — latency, bandwidth, throughput, jitter
x: Latency: time for a packet to travel (one-way or RTT). Bandwidth: max data rate (bits/sec). Throughput: actual achieved rate. Jitter: variance in latency. Explain the four key network performance metrics. How do they interact and which one matters most for different applications? Latency Ek request ka time (RTT / ms). Bandwidth Max data rate (bps). Throughput Actual data rate (with overhead). Jitter Latency ka variation. Latency ek chhote packet ke round-trip ka time (ms). Bandwidth channel ki max capacity (bps). Throughput actual data jo safely transfer hota hai (with protocol overhead). Jitter latency ki variation — real-time apps (VoIP, gaming) ke liye killer. Relation: latency × bandwidt

n: Cloud Networking — VPC design, multi-region, hybrid cloud
x: Cloud VPC design: large CIDR (/16) with subnets per tier (public, private-app, private-data) across 3 AZs. Multi-region: active-active or active-passive. Hybrid: Direct Connect + VPN to on-prem. How do you design a VPC for production workloads? What considerations drive CIDR ranges and subnet layout? VPC design Subnets + route tables + gateways ka layout. Multi-region Availability + low latency across regions. Hybrid cloud On-premise + cloud mix. AZ Availability Zone — datacenter group. Cloud networking — VPC design se shuru: public subnets (web), private subnets (app/db), NAT gw, route tables, NACL/SG. Multi-region — data ko multiple regions mein replicate karna (geo redundancy, low latency

n: Network Observability — tracing, metrics, packet capture, eBPF
x: Network observability includes flow logs (VPC Flow Logs), packet capture (tcpdump, Wireshark), distributed tracing (trace_id across services), eBPF (in-kernel programmable observation). What tools and techniques do you use for network observability in production? How do you debug a network issue? Tracing Request ko services ke paar follow karna (span graph). Metrics Counters/gauges — latency, QPS, error rate. Packet capture tcpdump/Wireshark — raw packets dekho. eBPF Kernel mein program — observability bina instrument. pcap Packet capture format. Network observability — samjho ki network kya kar raha hai. Tracing (Jaeger/Zipkin) ek request ko multiple services ke paar follow karta hai (spans

n: Kubernetes Networking — CNI, service mesh, ingress, network policies
x: Pod networking: CNI plugins assign IPs and route traffic. Service: kube-proxy handles cluster IP via iptables/IPVS. Ingress: L7 routing. NetworkPolicy: pod-level firewall. How does networking work in Kubernetes? Explain the roles of CNI, kube-proxy, and Ingress. CNI Container Network Interface — pod networking plugin. Service Pods ka stable virtual IP + DNS. Ingress Cluster ke andar HTTP L7 routing. kube-proxy Service IP -> pod IP forwarding rules. Kubernetes networking — pods ko ek flat network milta hai (har pod apna IP). CNI (Calico, Cilium) pod-to-pod networking + policies provide karta hai. Service pods ka stable virtual IP + DNS — pod churn se IP badalta hai par service constant. Ingre

n: Network Resiliency — retry, circuit breaker, timeout, bulkhead
x: Retry: resend on transient failures (with backoff). Circuit breaker: fail fast when downstream is unhealthy. Timeout: bound wait time. Bulkhead: isolate connection pools per dependency. What are the four essential network resiliency patterns? How do retry and circuit breaker interact? Retry Fail par request dobara — idempotency required. Circuit breaker Fail repeatedly par circuit open (fast fail). Timeout Kitna der wait karna; deadline boundary. Bulkhead Resources partition — ek failure doosre ko na rokaye. Network resiliency failures ko handle karta hai: retries (transient fail par dobara, bina blast radius), circuit breaker (repeated failure par circuit open — fast fail, bina wait), timeo

n: BGP — Border Gateway Protocol, AS routing, route propagation
x: BGP is the routing protocol of the internet. Autonomous Systems (AS) exchange routes via BGP. eBGP between ASes, iBGP within an AS. BGP selects routes based on AS-path length, local preference, MED. Route propagation is incremental — not periodic like OSPF. What is BGP and how does it differ from OSPF? Why is BGP called a path vector protocol? BGP Border Gateway Protocol — internet routing. AS Autonomous System — ek org ka network block. eBGP/iBGP eBGP between ASes, iBGP within AS. Prefix Announced route block (CIDR). AS path Route ka hop list — loop prevention. BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) internet ka routing protocol hai — different Autonomous Systems (AS) ke beech paise wale routers ko r

n: Ethernet — frames, MAC addresses, ARP, VLANs, switching
x: Ethernet frames: preamble, destination MAC, source MAC, type, payload, FCS. MAC addresses are 48-bit hardware addresses. ARP resolves IP→MAC. VLANs (802.1Q tag) segment broadcast domains. Switches learn MACs by source address, flood unknown unicast. What is the structure of an Ethernet frame? How does ARP resolve an IP to a MAC address? Ethernet Layer-2 LAN technology — frames, MAC. MAC address 48-bit physical unique address. ARP IP -> MAC resolution. VLAN Ek switch ko logical segments mein baantna (802.1Q). Frame L2 PDU: MAC hdr | payload | FCS. Ethernet Layer-2 LAN technology hai — devices ko MAC address se identify karta hai aur frames mein data bhejta hai. Switch MAC table se flooding in

n: ICMP & Diagnostic Tools — ping, traceroute, path MTU discovery
x: ICMP echoes (ping) test reachability and measure RTT. traceroute sends TTL=1,2,3... packets, receives ICMP time exceeded. Path MTU Discovery: send DF (Don't Fragment) bit, receive ICMP 'fragmentation needed' to find max MTU. Used for network diagnostics. How does traceroute work? What is the difference between ping and traceroute? ICMP Internet Control Message Protocol — diagnostics. ping Host reachability + RTT. traceroute Path ka har hop + latency. Path MTU Path par smallest MTU — fragmentation. Echo/Reply ICMP type 8 / 0. ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) diagnostics ke liye hai — jaise ping (echo request/reply — host reachable hai aur RTT kya hai) aur traceroute (path ke har hop k

802.11 defines WiFi. Standards: 802.11n (WiFi 4), 802.11ac (WiFi 5), 802.11ax (WiFi 6/6E). Association: scan → authenticate → associate. Encryption: WPA3 (SAE handshake, protected management frames). WPA2 vulnerable to KRACK attack. Channel contention via CSMA/CA. What is the difference between WiFi 5 (802.11ac) and WiFi 6 (802.11ax)? 802.11 IEEE WiFi standard family. WPA3 Latest WiFi security (SAE, forward secrecy). SSID Network name. Channel/band 2.4GHz, 5GHz, 6GHz bands. WPA2/WPA3-PSK Personal security modes. WiFi IEEE 802.11 standard par chalta hai — versions: 802.11n (WiFi 4), ac (WiFi 5), ax (WiFi 6), be (WiFi 7). WPA3 latest security — SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals) dicti

t: Start Here — Processes, Threads & Why They Exist
x: A process is a running program. When you open Chrome, the OS creates a process for it — gives it its own memory space, CPU time, and resources. Each process is isolated; one crashing process cannot corrupt another. What is a process? What resources does the OS give to each process? Process Running program ka instance — apna address space, file descriptors, PID. Address space Har process ko OS virtual memory deta hai; dusre process ki memory dikhti nahi. PCB Process Control Block — OS ka record: PID, state, registers, memory maps. Definition: Process = disk par pada program jab OS use memory mein load karke chalata hai. OS use code, heap, stack, open files aur ek PID deta hai. Isolation hardw

t: Start Here — Processes, Threads & Why They Exist
x: A thread is a single sequence of execution inside a process. One process can have many threads — they share the same memory (heap, code, files) but each has its own stack and CPU registers. Threads are "lightweight processes" — much cheaper to create. What is a thread? How is it different from a process? Thread Process ke andar execution ka ek sequence — apna stack aur registers. TID Thread ID; OS thread ko schedule karta hai. Shared heap Same process ke saare threads same heap/globals dekhte hain. Definition: Thread CPU scheduling ki sabse chhoti unit hai. Ek process mein ek ya zyada threads hote hain jo code, heap aur file descriptors share karte hain, par stack aur program counter alag ra

n: Why Do We Need Multiple Threads?
t: Start Here — Processes, Threads & Why They Exist
x: Two reasons: (1) Responsiveness — while one thread waits for a disk read, another thread can keep the UI running. (2) Performance — on a multi-core CPU, threads can truly run in parallel, speeding up computation. Without threads, a web server could only handle one request at a time. Why do we use multiple threads? Give a real example of a program that benefits from threading. Responsiveness Slow kaam background mein, UI/main flow block nahi hota. Throughput Multi-core par ek saath zyada kaam. I/O overlap Ek thread I/O par wait kare to dusra CPU use kare. Definition: Multiple threads ke do bade fayde hain: (1) responsiveness — blocking kaam alag thread mein, (2) parallelism — multi-core CPU k

t: Start Here — Processes, Threads & Why They Exist
x: Process: own code, own heap, own stack, own file descriptors — fully isolated. Thread: shared code, shared heap, shared file descriptors — but own stack and own registers. This shared heap is the source of all concurrency bugs. Draw the memory layout of a process with 3 threads. What is shared? What is private? Isolation Process alag memory; thread shared memory. Context switch cost Process switch mein address-space switch + TLB flush, thread mein kam. IPC Process ke beech communication ke liye pipes/sockets/shared mem. Definition: Process ke paas apna code, heap, stack, file descriptors hote hain (poora isolated). Thread ek process ke andar rehta hai — code, heap, globals share karta hai, s

n: How the CPU Runs Multiple Threads — Scheduling & Context Switch
t: Start Here — Processes, Threads & Why They Exist
x: A CPU core can only run one thread at a time. The OS scheduler rapidly switches between threads (context switch) — saving one thread's registers and loading another's. This happens so fast (milliseconds) it feels simultaneous. Multi-core CPUs can truly run threads in parallel. How does a single-core CPU appear to run multiple programs at once? Scheduler OS ka part jo tay karta hai ab kaunsa thread CPU par chalega. Context switch Chalte thread ka state save karke dusre ka load karna. Time slice Thread ko ek baar mein milne wala CPU time (ms). Definition: Ek core ek samay mein ek hi thread chalata hai. Scheduler time-slice khatam hone par (preemption) ya thread ke block hone par state (registe

Concurrency: multiple tasks make progress (interleaving). Parallelism: multiple tasks run simultaneously (multi-core). What is the difference between concurrency and parallelism? Give a real-world analogy. Concurrency Kai tasks ek saath progress karte hain — interleaving, ek core par bhi. Parallelism Kai tasks literally ek hi time par chalte hain — multi-core. Rob Pike 'Concurrency is about dealing with lots of things at once; parallelism is about doing lots of things at once.' Definition: Concurrency ek structure/design property hai — program ko independent tasks mein todna. Parallelism execution property hai — un tasks ko multiple cores par ek saath chalana. Concurrent program single core

When two threads access shared data concurrently and at least one writes — result depends on execution order. What is a race condition? Write a code example that demonstrates one. Race condition Result thread scheduling ke order par depend kare. Read-modify-write count++ asal mein read, add, write — 3 steps. Heisenbug Debug karte hi gayab hone wala non-deterministic bug. Definition: Jab do ya zyada threads shared data ko ek saath access karein aur kam se kam ek write kare, aur outcome timing par depend kare. count++ atomic nahi hai: read → add → write. Do threads dono ne 5 padha, dono ne 6 likha — ek update kho gaya (lost update).

A code region accessing shared resources. Must be executed by only one thread at a time (mutual exclusion). What is a critical section? What are the 4 requirements for a correct mutual exclusion solution? Critical section Code ka hissa jo shared resource chhuta hai. Mutual exclusion Ek samay par sirf ek thread andar. Progress & bounded wait Koi thread hamesha ke liye bahar na rahe. Definition: Critical section wo code region hai jahan shared data access hota hai. Sahi solution ke teen gun: mutual exclusion, progress (koi andar nahi to doosre ko ghusne do), bounded waiting (starvation nahi). Lock ya mutex se ise protect karte hain; section jitna chhota, utna better concurrency.

An operation that appears to happen instantaneously — no intermediate state is observable to other threads. What does atomic mean? Is i++ atomic? What about a read-modify-write on a 64-bit int on a 32-bit system? Atomic Operation poora hota hai ya bilkul nahi; beech ki state koi nahi dekhta. Indivisible Beech mein interrupt nahi ho sakta. Atomic types AtomicInteger, std::atomic, Atomics (JS). Definition: Atomic operation ek instant mein hota hua dikhta hai. Hardware kuch operations (aligned read/write, CAS, fetch-add) ko atomic banata hai; baaki ke liye lock ya atomic library chahiye. x++ , x = x + 1 normally atomic nahi hain.

CPUs have private caches — writes by one thread may not be visible to others without synchronization. Why can a thread read stale data even without a race condition? What is the volatile keyword for? CPU cache Har core ka private L1/L2 — writes turant dusre core ko nahi dikhte. Visibility Ek thread ki write kab dusre thread ko dikhe. Happens-before Ordering rule jo visibility guarantee karta hai. Definition: Modern CPU aur compiler reorder/cache karte hain. Ek thread ne flag = true likha, par dusra thread purani value cache se padhta reh sakta hai — bina synchronization ke guarantee nahi. Lock, volatile, atomics visibility ke liye memory barriers lagate hain.

A lock that only one thread can hold at a time. Thread acquires lock, enters critical section, releases lock. How does a mutex work? What is a spinlock and when is it better than a blocking mutex? Mutex Ek samay mein ek hi owner wala lock. Lock / unlock Acquire karo, kaam, release. Reentrant Same thread dobara lock le sake bina deadlock. Definition: Mutex critical section ko protect karta hai. Jo thread lock leta hai wahi chhodta hai (ownership). Lock mila hua ho to dusre thread block (sleep) ho jaate hain. Reentrant mutex ek hi thread ko baar-baar lene deta hai (count rakhta hai).

A counter-based synchronization primitive. Binary semaphore = mutex. Counting semaphore = limit concurrent access. What is a semaphore? How does it differ from a mutex? Implement a bounded buffer using semaphores. Counting semaphore N permits; acquire se ghatta, release se badhta. Binary semaphore 0/1 — mutex jaisa par ownership nahi. P / V wait() / signal() — Dijkstra ke operations. Definition: Semaphore ek counter hai. acquire() counter ghatata hai (0 ho to block), release() badhata hai. Isse N threads tak ko resource access de sakte ho. Mutex se fark: semaphore ko koi bhi thread release kar sakta hai, isliye signaling ke liye bhi use hota hai.

A monitor combines a mutex + condition variables. A thread can wait() until a condition is true, then be signal()ed. What is a monitor? How do condition variables work?
