Why must you always check conditions in a while loop? Monitor Mutex + condition variables ka bundle. wait() Lock chhod ke sleep; signal par wapas lock lekar jaagta hai. Spurious wakeup Bina signal ke bhi jaag sakta hai. Definition: Monitor mein lock ke andar thread kisi condition ka wait kar sakta hai ( wait ), aur dusra thread condition badal kar notify/signal kar deta hai. wait atomic roop se lock release karke sleep karta hai.

Multiple readers can hold simultaneously. Only one writer — exclusive. Perfect for read-heavy workloads. When would you use a Read-Write Lock over a plain mutex? What are its trade-offs? Shared lock Kai readers ek saath. Exclusive lock Writer akela. Writer starvation Readers lagatar aate rahein to writer ruka rahe. Definition: ReadWriteLock multiple readers ya ek writer allow karta hai. Read-heavy workload (95% reads) mein mutex se behtar throughput deta hai.

Barrier: all threads must reach it before any proceeds. Latch: countdown to zero then releases all waiters. What is a CyclicBarrier? What is a CountDownLatch? When would you use each? Barrier N threads wait karte hain jab tak sab pahunch na jayein. Latch Count 0 hone par ek baar sab release; reuse nahi. Phase Parallel algorithm ke steps jo sync maangte hain. Definition: CyclicBarrier reusable hai — har phase ke baad sab ek saath aage badhte hain. CountDownLatch ek-baar: main thread tab tak wait karta hai jab tak workers countDown() na kar dein.

Coffman conditions: Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait. All 4 must hold. What are the four necessary conditions for deadlock? To prevent deadlock, which one would you eliminate? Mutual exclusion Resource ek hi holder. Hold & wait Ek hold karke dusra maange. No preemption Zabardasti nahi chheeni ja sakti. Circular wait A→B→A cycle. Definition: Deadlock tab hota hai jab Coffman ki chaaron conditions ek saath hon. Inme se ek bhi tod do to deadlock nahi ho sakta. Classic: Thread 1 ne lock A liya, B maanga; Thread 2 ne B liya, A maanga.

Prevention: eliminate one Coffman condition. Avoidance: Banker's algorithm. Detection: find cycles in RAG. Compare deadlock prevention, avoidance (Banker's algorithm), and detection. What does each cost? Prevention Ek Coffman condition tod do. Avoidance Banker's algorithm — safe state mein hi allocate. Detection Wait-for graph mein cycle dhoondho, phir recover. Definition: Prevention: lock ordering (circular wait), sab locks ek saath lena (hold & wait), tryLock+timeout (no preemption). Avoidance system-state dekh kar decide karta hai. Detection+recovery: cycle mile to ek victim abort.

Livelock: threads keep responding to each other but make no progress. Starvation: a thread never gets CPU time. What is the difference between deadlock, livelock, and starvation? Give a real-world analogy for each. Livelock Threads active hain par progress zero. Starvation Ek thread ko resource kabhi nahi milta. Backoff Random wait se symmetry todna. Definition: Deadlock mein threads block hote hain; livelock mein wo chalte rehte hain par kuch kaam nahi hota. Starvation mein scheduler/lock policy ki wajah se ek thread hamesha peeche reh jaata hai.

Acquire locks in a consistent global order across all threads — the most practical deadlock prevention technique. How does consistent lock ordering prevent deadlock? What is tryLock with timeout? Global order Saare locks ka ek fixed rank. Ordered acquire Hamesha chhote rank se bade. Identity hash Ordering ke liye id/address. Definition: Agar har thread locks ek hi order mein le (jaise account id ke ascending order mein), to circular wait possible nahi, isliye deadlock nahi.

Pre-created pool of threads that pick up tasks from a queue. Avoids thread creation overhead, controls resource usage. Why use a thread pool instead of creating a new thread per task? How do you size a thread pool? Worker threads Pehle se bane, reuse hote hain. Task queue Pending tasks ka buffer. Rejection policy Queue bhar jaye to kya karna hai. Definition: Thread pool fixed/bounded threads rakhta hai jo queue se tasks uthate hain. Thread creation cost bachta hai aur concurrency limit hoti hai. Sizing: CPU-bound ≈ cores; I/O-bound ≈ cores × (1 + wait/compute).

Hardware-supported instruction: atomically compare memory location to expected value and swap if equal. No lock needed. How does CAS work? Implement an atomic counter using CAS. What is the ABA problem? CAS compareAndSwap(addr, expected, new) atomically. Retry loop CAS fail ho to phir se padho aur try karo. ABA problem Value A→B→A ho gayi, CAS ko pata nahi. Definition: CAS CPU instruction hai: memory mein value expected ke barabar ho to nayi value likho, warna fail. Is par lock-free counters/stacks bante hain.

Lock-free: system-wide progress guaranteed (at least one thread progresses). Wait-free: every thread progresses. What is a lock-free data structure? Why is it hard to implement? When would you use one? Lock-free Kam se kam ek thread hamesha aage badhta hai. Wait-free Har thread bounded steps mein khatam. Obstruction-free Akela chale to khatam. Definition: Lock-free algorithms mutex ki jagah CAS use karte hain, isliye ek thread ka stall/suspension baakiyon ko block nahi karta. Wait-free sabse strong guarantee hai par likhna bahut mushkil.

A Future represents a value not yet computed. Promise resolves it later. Async/await is syntactic sugar over Futures. What is the difference between a Future and a Promise? How does CompletableFuture in Java work? Future Abhi na mili value ka placeholder. Promise Value set karne wala writable side. async/await Future par sequential-looking syntax. Definition: Future ek pending result hai jo baad mein resolve ya reject hota hai. async/await compiler/runtime state machine banata hai jo await par thread chhod deta hai (block nahi karta).

Concurrency without shared state — actors communicate via message passing only. Used in Erlang, Akka, Go channels. Explain the Actor model. How does it avoid race conditions without locks? Actor Private state + mailbox; ek time par ek message. Message passing Shared memory nahi, sirf messages. Supervision Parent actor child ke fail par restart tay karta hai (Erlang). Definition: Actor model mein har actor apni state ka akela maalik hai; doosre actor sirf message bhej sakte hain. Mailbox ke messages ek-ek karke process hote hain, isliye locks ki zaroorat nahi. Go ka mantra: 'share memory by communicating'.

n: Memory Ordering — sequential consistency, acquire-release, relaxed
x: Memory ordering defines the order in which memory operations become visible to other threads. Sequential consistency: all threads see the same order. Acquire-release: release on write, acquire on read (synchronizes). Relaxed: no ordering guarantees (fastest). x86 is mostly TSO (Total Store Order). ARM/POWER are weakly ordered. What is the difference between sequential consistency and relaxed memory ordering? Sequential consistency Saare threads ek hi global order dekhte hain. Acquire/release Release se pehle ki writes acquire karne wale ko dikhengi. Relaxed Sirf atomicity, koi ordering nahi. Definition: CPU/compiler instructions reorder karte hain. Memory model tay karta hai kaun si ordering

n: volatile keyword — Java, C++, JavaScript differences
x: Java volatile: visibility guarantee (no caching) + happens-before ordering. C++ volatile: prevents compiler optimization (NOT thread-safe, use std::atomic). JavaScript: no volatile (single-threaded). Common misconception: volatile does NOT provide atomicity in Java. What does volatile guarantee in Java? Why is it NOT sufficient for thread safety? Java volatile Visibility + happens-before; atomicity nahi. C++ volatile Compiler optimization roke; thread-safety nahi. JS volatile nahi hota; Atomics use karo. Definition: Java mein volatile variable ki write turant sab threads ko dikhti hai aur reordering rokti hai. Par volatile int x; x++ atomic nahi. C++ mein volatile threading ke liye nahi hai

n: Thread Interruption — cooperative cancellation, InterruptedException, flags
x: Thread interruption is cooperative: interrupt sets a flag, the thread must check and respond. Java: Thread.interrupt() + InterruptedException. Python: threading.Event. Go: context.Context with cancel. Never ignore InterruptedException — either rethrow or restore interrupt flag. How does cooperative thread cancellation work? Why is it preferred over forceful termination? Cooperative Thread ko khud check karke ruk-na hota hai. InterruptedException Blocking call interrupt par throw karta hai. Cancellation token JS/C#/Go (context) ka equivalent. Definition: Thread ko zabardasti maarna unsafe hai (locks leak). Isliye interrupt sirf flag set karta hai; thread blocking calls par ya isInterrupted()

n: Green Threads vs OS Threads — fibers, coroutines, M:N scheduling
x: Green threads (goroutines, Kotlin coroutines, Python asyncio tasks) are multiplexed onto OS threads by a runtime. M:N model: M green threads on N OS threads. Lightweight (~2KB stack for goroutines vs ~1MB for OS threads). Scheduled by runtime, not OS. Blocked green thread yields OS thread. What is the difference between green threads and OS threads? How does M:N scheduling work? Goroutine Go ka lightweight thread (~2KB stack). M:N scheduling M green threads N OS threads par. Virtual threads Java 21 ke lightweight threads. Definition: Green threads runtime ke scheduler se chalte hain, OS ke nahi. Blocking I/O par runtime thread ko park karke OS thread dusre green thread ko de deta hai. Isliye

JS is single-threaded but non-blocking via event loop: call stack + task queue + microtask queue + libuv. Explain the JS event loop in detail. What is the difference between microtasks and macrotasks? Call stack Abhi chalta sync code. Microtask queue Promise.then, queueMicrotask — pehle chalti hai. Macrotask setTimeout, I/O callbacks. Definition: Loop: stack khali ho → saari microtasks drain → ek macrotask → repeat. Node mein libuv phases hain (timers, poll, check) aur process.nextTick microtasks se bhi pehle.

Node.js Worker Threads enable true parallelism for CPU-bound work. Each worker has its own V8 and event loop. When would you use Worker Threads in Node.js? How do you communicate between them? Worker Alag V8 isolate + event loop. postMessage Structured clone se data copy. SharedArrayBuffer Zero-copy shared memory + Atomics. Definition: worker_threads CPU-heavy kaam main loop se hata deta hai. Workers memory share nahi karte (default) — messages copy hote hain; SharedArrayBuffer se share kar sakte ho.

Promises implement the microtask queue. Unhandled promise rejections can crash Node.js in newer versions. How do Promises work internally? What is Promise chaining vs async/await? What are the error propagation rules? States pending → fulfilled / rejected (settled, immutable). then chain Har then naya promise return karta hai. unhandledRejection Node 15+ default: process crash. Definition: Promise ke callbacks microtask queue mein chalte hain. then ka return value agle promise ko resolve karta hai; throw rejection mein badal jaata hai.

Node Cluster forks multiple worker processes (one per CPU core) sharing the same port — achieves parallelism. How does Node.js Cluster module work? How does the master process distribute connections to workers? Primary/worker Master fork karta hai, workers port share karte hain. Round-robin Linux par default distribution. PM2 Cluster manager. Definition: cluster module har CPU core par ek Node process chalata hai, sab ek hi port par. Memory share nahi hoti, isliye in-memory session/cache workers ke beech consistent nahi.

Producers add items to a bounded buffer; consumers remove items. Synchronize to avoid overflow and underflow. Implement the Producer-Consumer problem using semaphores. Then solve it with a BlockingQueue. Bounded buffer Fixed size queue — backpressure deta hai. empty/full Consumer empty par, producer full par wait. BlockingQueue Built-in thread-safe implementation. Definition: Producers queue mein items daalte hain, consumers nikalte hain. Bounded buffer producers ko slow karta hai jab consumers peeche hon (backpressure).

Multiple readers can read simultaneously. Writers need exclusive access. Variants: reader-first vs writer-first. Solve the Readers-Writers problem. Which variant prevents starvation and how? Reader-preference Readers ko priority — writer starve ho sakta hai. Writer-preference Writer wait mein ho to naye readers rokte hain. Fair Arrival order. Definition: Shared data par kai readers ek saath, writer exclusive. Variants fairness tay karte hain. Solution: ReadWriteLock ya semaphores + reader count.

N philosophers alternate eating/thinking, sharing N forks. Demonstrates deadlock and starvation challenges. Explain the Dining Philosophers problem. Give two different solutions to avoid deadlock. Forks Shared resources (N). Circular wait Sab ne left fork utha li → deadlock. Resource hierarchy Forks ko number do, chhota pehle. Definition: N philosophers ko khane ke liye do forks chahiye. Sab ek saath left fork uthayein to deadlock. Fixes: fork ordering, max N−1 philosophers table par (semaphore), ya odd/even alag order.

Creating a singleton in a multi-threaded environment — naive lazy initialization is not thread-safe. What is wrong with double-checked locking for Singleton? How do you implement it correctly? Double-checked locking Pehle bina lock check, phir lock mein. Holder idiom Static inner class lazy + thread-safe. Enum singleton Java mein simplest safe. Definition: Naive if (inst==null) inst=new X() do threads mein do instances bana sakta hai. Safe options: eager static, holder class, enum, ya volatile + double-checked locking.

Token bucket or leaky bucket algorithm implemented with atomic operations or locks for concurrent requests. Design a thread-safe rate limiter that allows 100 req/sec. Implement it in code. Token bucket Tokens refill hote hain, burst allow. Leaky bucket Fixed rate se output. Sliding window Time window mein count. Definition: Token bucket: capacity C, refill rate r. Har request ek token leti hai. Thread-safe banane ke liye lock ya CAS par (tokens, lastRefill) ko ek unit mein update karo.

LRU cache with concurrent reads/writes — naive locking kills throughput. Segmented locking is the solution. Implement a thread-safe LRU cache. How do you handle concurrent reads without a write lock? LRU HashMap + doubly linked list. Lock striping Segments par alag locks. Read-through Miss par load aur store. Definition: Ek global lock throughput maar deta hai. Options: segmented/striped locks, ya Caffeine jaisa library; get par bhi list reorder hoti hai isliye read-lock kaafi nahi.

Race conditions and deadlocks are non-deterministic — hardest bugs to reproduce and fix. How do you debug a deadlock in production? What tools and techniques do you use? Thread dump Sab threads ka stack snapshot. Race detector Go -race, ThreadSanitizer. Stress test Zyada threads, repeat runs. Definition: Approach: logs mein thread-id + timestamp, thread dump (jstack) se deadlock cycle, TSan/ go test -race , stress + randomized delays, aur minimal repro.

Thread-per-request vs thread pool vs async event-driven. Each has different performance characteristics. Compare multi-threaded vs event-driven concurrency models for a web server. When does each excel? Thread-per-request Simple, blocking, memory heavy. Thread pool Bounded threads + queue. Event-driven Kam threads, non-blocking (nginx, Node). Definition: Thread-per-request (Apache prefork) simple par 10k connections par fail (C10K). Pool resource bound karta hai. Event loop I/O-bound par best par CPU kaam block karta hai. Hybrid: event loop + worker pool.

n: Python GIL — what it is, why it exists, when it matters
x: The Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) is a mutex in CPython that allows only one thread to execute Python bytecode at a time. It exists because CPython's reference counting is not thread-safe. It affects CPU-bound code but not I/O-bound code. Removed in Python 3.13+ (free-threaded mode, opt-in). What is the Python GIL? Why does it exist and when does it matter? GIL CPython mein ek time par ek thread bytecode chalata hai. CPU-bound Threads se fayda nahi. I/O-bound I/O par GIL release hota hai — threads kaam karte hain. Definition: GIL CPython ke reference counting ko safe rakhta hai. CPU-bound threads parallel nahi chalte; I/O (sockets, files) ya C extensions (NumPy) GIL release karte hain. Pytho

n: Threading in Python — threading module, daemon threads, Thread(target=)
x: Python's threading module creates OS threads. Due to the GIL, threads don't help CPU-bound tasks but do help I/O-bound tasks (network, file I/O). Daemon threads die when the main thread exits. join() waits for thread completion. When would you use Python threading? Why doesn't it help with CPU-bound work? threading.Thread OS thread wrapper. daemon Main exit par band, bina wait ke. Lock / Event Sync primitives. Definition: threading I/O-bound concurrency ke liye. Thread(target=fn, args=...) , start() , join() . Daemon threads program exit nahi rokte.

n: asyncio — event loop, coroutines, await, asyncio.gather()
x: asyncio provides single-threaded concurrency via an event loop. async/await defines coroutines. asyncio.gather() runs multiple coroutines concurrently. asyncio creates tasks that interleave during I/O waits. No GIL contention because single-threaded. How does asyncio work? What is the difference between asyncio.gather() and asyncio.create_task()? Coroutine async def function. await Control event loop ko wapas. gather Kai coroutines saath chalao. Definition: asyncio single thread par cooperative multitasking karta hai. await par task suspend hota hai aur loop dusra chalata hai. Blocking call (time.sleep, requests) poora loop rok deta hai.

n: multiprocessing — bypassing the GIL, shared memory, Process(target=)
x: multiprocessing spawns separate processes, each with its own Python interpreter and GIL. Bypasses the GIL for CPU-bound work. Communicate via Queue, Pipe, or shared memory (Value, Array, Manager). Overhead of process creation and IPC. How does multiprocessing bypass the GIL? What are the tradeoffs vs threading? Process Alag interpreter + GIL. Pool Worker processes ka pool. Pickling Args/results serialize hote hain. Definition: multiprocessing alag processes chalata hai, isliye CPU-bound kaam true parallel hota hai. Data pickling se jaata hai (overhead); shared_memory se zero-copy sharing possible.

n: Encapsulation — bundling data + methods, access modifiers
x: Encapsulation binds data and methods that operate on that data together, restricting direct access to internal state. Access modifiers (private, protected, public) enforce boundaries. Why does encapsulation protect object invariants and reduce coupling? How do access modifiers enforce boundaries? State Object ka apna internal data ya variables Behavior Object ke methods ya functions jo us state ke saath kaam karte hain Access Modifiers private, public, protected jaise keywords jo ye decide karte hain ki kaun data dekh/change kar sakta hai Encapsulation ka seedha sa matlab hai data (variables) aur behavior (methods) ko ek hi dabbe (class) mein band karna, aur us dabbe ko bahar se direct modif

n: Inheritance — IS-A relationships, super/sub classes, method overriding
x: Inheritance creates an IS-A hierarchy where a subclass inherits fields and methods from a parent class. Method overriding allows subclasses to provide specialized behavior. Why does inheritance create tight coupling and when should you prefer composition over inheritance? Superclass (Parent) Wo class jiski khoobiyan inherit ki jaa rahi hain Subclass (Child) Wo nayi class jo parent ki khoobiyan le rahi hai IS-A Relationship Ye relationship batata hai ki child actually parent ka hi ek type hai (e.g. Car IS-A Vehicle) Inheritance ka matlab hai ek nayi class banana jo ek existing class ki properties (state) aur methods (behavior) ko automatically le leti hai. Ye "IS-A" (yah-ek) relationship esta

Polymorphism means "many forms". Compile-time polymorphism (method overloading) vs runtime polymorphism (method overriding, virtual dispatch). How does polymorphism enable treating objects of different types uniformly through a common interface? Poly Bohot saare (Many) Morph Roop ya aakar (Forms) Method Overloading Ek hi class mein same naam ke multiple methods, par parameters alag (Compile-time) Method Overriding Child class apne parent ke method ko replace kar deti hai (Run-time) Polymorphism ka seedha sa matlab hai "Bohot saare roop". Ek hi function ya method alag-alag objects ke liye alag tarike se behave kar sakta hai.

n: Abstraction — abstract classes vs interfaces, hiding complexity
x: Abstraction hides implementation details and exposes only essential features. Achieved via abstract classes (partial impl + abstract methods) and interfaces (pure contracts). How does abstraction reduce complexity for the caller and isolate change? What is the difference between abstract classes and interfaces? Abstract Class Aadhi-adhuri class jiska object (instance) nahi banaya jaa sakta Interface Sirf ek contract (rules) jisme koi implementation nahi hoti Abstraction ka matlab hai zaroori details dikhana aur baaki ki complexity (background ka mess) chhupa lena.

n: Association, Aggregation, Composition — has-a vs owns-a differences
x: Association (uses-a), Aggregation (has-a, independent lifecycle), Composition (owns-a, dependent lifecycle). These define relationships with different ownership semantics. What is the difference between association, aggregation, and composition? How does ownership affect lifecycle management? Ye teeno HAS-A relationships ke alag alag levels (strength) hain.

n: SRP — Single Responsibility: one class, one reason to change
x: A class should have one, and only one, reason to change. Every class should be responsible for a single part of the system functionality. Why do SRP classes lead to more cohesive, focused, and testable code? What is the God Object anti-pattern? Responsibility Class ke change hone ki wajah (Reason to change) God Object Wo dheet class jo system ka aada kaam khud akele karti hai Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) kehta hai ki ek class ke paas badalne (change hone) ki bas ek hi wajah honi chahiye. Matlab ek class ko system ka sirf ek hi kaam sambhalna chahiye.

n: OCP — Open/Closed: open for extension, closed for modification
x: Software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification. Add new behavior through new code, not by changing existing code. How does the Strategy pattern exemplify the Open/Closed Principle? Why prevents modifying tested code? Open for Extension Nayi features aasani se add ho sakein Closed for Modification Purana tested code na chhedna pade Open/Closed Principle (OCP) kehta hai ki code aisa hona chahiye jismein nayi functionality add karna aasan ho (Open), par uske liye purana likha hua code na change karna pade (Closed).

n: LSP — Liskov Substitution: subtypes must replace base types
x: Objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of a subclass without affecting correctness. Subtypes must satisfy the base type contract. Why is the Square-Rectangle problem the classic example of violating LSP? How do preconditions and postconditions relate? Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) kehta hai ki agar Class B, Class A se inherit karti hai, toh program mein jahan bhi Class A use ho rahi ho, wahan Class B ko rakh dene se program fatna nahi chahiye.

n: ISP — Interface Segregation: small focused interfaces
x: Clients should not be forced to depend on methods they do not use. Large interfaces should be split into smaller, more specific ones. How does Interface Segregation reduce coupling and prevent dummy method implementations? Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) kehta hai ki clients ko un methods pe depend karne ke liye majboor mat karo jo wo use nahi karte. Ek bade (fat) interface se behtar hai chhote-chhote specific interfaces banana.

n: DIP — Dependency Inversion: depend on abstractions, not concretions
x: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions. Abstractions should not depend on details. How does Dependency Injection implement the Dependency Inversion Principle? What problem does it solve? High-level modules Tumhara main business logic (e.g. OrderProcessing) Low-level modules Chhote utilities ya tools (e.g. MySQLDatabase, SmtpEmail) Abstraction Interface ya base class Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP) kehta hai ki High-level classes ko Low-level classes pe direct depend nahi karna chahiye. Dono ko abstractions (interfaces) pe depend karna chahiye.

n: Composition over Inheritance — prefer has-a over is-a when possible
x: Favor has-a relationships over is-a relationships. Achieve reuse by composing objects, not by inheriting from a base class. Why does composition provide more flexibility than inheritance at runtime? How does the Decorator pattern demonstrate this? Inheritance (IS-A) Ek class se extend karke nayi class banana Composition (HAS-A) Chhote-chhote parts (objects) ko jod kar ek bada object banana Composition over Inheritance ek rule of thumb hai jo kehta hai ki code reuse karne ke liye objects ko aapas mein jodna (compose karna) better hota hai, bjaye ek base class se inherit karne ke.

n: Law of Demeter (Principle of Least Knowledge) — talk only to immediate friends
x: A method should only call methods on: itself, its parameters, objects it creates, its own fields. Dont talk to strangers (method chaining like a.getB().getC().do()). Why does the Law of Demeter reduce coupling? What is the trade-off of following it too strictly? Law of Demeter (Principle of Least Knowledge) kehta hai ki ek object ko apne aas-paas ki duniya (dusre objects ke internals) ke baare mein kam se kam pata hona chahiye.

n: DRY, KISS, YAGNI — dont repeat, keep simple, avoid over-engineering
x: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself), KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid), YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It). Three principles guiding pragmatic software design. How can over-applying DRY lead to premature abstraction? When does YAGNI apply to design patterns? Teen basic rules jo har developer ko pata hone chahiye: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself): Code copy-paste mat karo. Same logic 2 jagah hai toh usko ek function mein dalo. KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid): Code ko over-engineer mat karo. Aasan code likho jo kal ko padh sako. YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It):

n: Coupling & Cohesion — low coupling, high cohesion
x: Coupling measures how dependent one module is on another. Cohesion measures how focused the responsibilities within a module are. Aim for low coupling, high cohesion. Why is low coupling and high cohesion the sweet spot for software maintainability and testability? Coupling: Do classes ek dusre pe kitna depend karti hain. (Aim: Low Coupling - Classes azaad honi chahiye). Cohesion: Ek class ke methods aur variables ka aapas mein kitna lena-dena hai. (Aim: High Cohesion - Class ka ek hi focus hona chahiye, SRP jaisa).

n: Tell-Dont-Ask — command objects what to do, dont query state
x: Tell objects what to do rather than asking about their state and then deciding. Encapsulate behavior with data. How does Tell-Dont-Ask preserve encapsulation and eliminate anemic domain models? Give a code example. Tell-Don't-Ask ka principle kehta hai ki object se data maang (ask) kar khud decision lene ke bjaye, object ko apna kaam khud karne ko bolo (tell).

n: Singleton — ensure one instance, global access point. Thread-safety considerations.
x: Singleton ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access. Thread-safety through eager initialization, synchronized getInstance, or Bill Pugh inner class. How do you implement a thread-safe Singleton in Java? Why is enum Singleton considered the most robust approach? Instance Class ka ek object Global Access Point Kahi se bhi us object ko access karne ka tareeqa Singleton Pattern ye ensure karta hai ki ek class ka pure application mein sirf aur sirf ek hi instance (object) banega, aur usko access karne ka ek global tareeqa hoga.

n: Factory Method — define interface for creating objects, subclasses decide instantiation
x: Factory Method defines an interface for creating an object, but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate. The Creator class defers instantiation to subclasses. How does Factory Method decouple clients from concrete types and enable the Open/Closed Principle? Creator Wo class jisme factory method hota hai Product Wo object jo factory method banata hai Factory Method ek creational pattern hai jo object create karne ka logic ek separate method mein daal deta hai. Subclasses us method ko override karke decide kar sakti hain ki kis type ka object banana hai.

n: Abstract Factory — create families of related objects without concrete classes
x: Abstract Factory provides an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying their concrete classes. A "factory of factories". When would you use Abstract Factory over Factory Method? How does it ensure product compatibility? Abstract Factory patterns ka ek level up hai. Ye ek factory of factories hai. Ye tumhe related objects ki poori "Family" (theme) banane deta hai bina unki concrete classes specify kiye.

n: Builder — separate construction of complex objects from representation
x: Builder separates the construction of a complex object from its representation. The same construction process can create different representations via a director + builder interface. How does Builder solve the telescoping constructor problem? What makes it different from Factory? Builder Pattern complex objects ko step-by-step banane (construct) mein madad karta hai. Constructor mein 10 parameters pass karne ki jagah (Telescoping Constructor Anti-pattern), hum ek Builder object use karte hain.

n: Prototype — clone existing objects instead of creating new from scratch
x: Prototype creates new objects by cloning/copying an existing instance (the prototype). Avoids costly creation from scratch, especially when object initialization is expensive. What is the difference between shallow copy and deep copy in the Prototype pattern? When is it useful?

n: Object Pool — reuse objects that are expensive to create (connections, threads)
x: Object Pool manages a reusable set of initialized objects. Clients borrow from the pool and return objects instead of creating/destroying them. What problems does Object Pool solve beyond performance? How do you handle stale/broken objects in the pool?

n: Adapter — convert interface of a class to another interface clients expect
x: Adapter converts the interface of a class into another interface that clients expect. Lets classes work together that couldn't otherwise due to incompatible interfaces. What is the difference between class adapter and object adapter? Why is composition preferred? Adapter Pattern ek structural design pattern hai jo do aisi classes ko saath mein kaam karne deta hai jinke interfaces aapas mein match nahi hote (incompatible interfaces).

n: Bridge — decouple abstraction from implementation so they vary independently
x: Bridge decouples an abstraction from its implementation so the two can vary independently. Avoids permanent binding between abstraction and implementation at compile time. How does Bridge prevent the Cartesian product explosion of subclasses? Give a real-world example.

n: Composite — compose objects into tree structures, treat individuals uniformly
x: Composite composes objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies. Clients treat individual objects and compositions uniformly via a common interface. How does Composite simplify client code when dealing with tree structures like file systems or UI components?

n: Decorator — attach responsibilities to objects dynamically (wrapper)
x: Decorator attaches additional responsibilities to an object dynamically. Provides a flexible alternative to subclassing for extending functionality. How is Decorator more flexible than inheritance for adding behavior? How do decorators stack? Decorator Pattern ek structural pattern hai jo objects mein runtime par nayi behaviors (features) add karne deta hai, bina unki class ko modify kiye ya subclass banaye.

n: Facade — provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem
x: Facade provides a unified, simplified interface to a set of interfaces in a subsystem. Defines a higher-level interface that makes the subsystem easier to use. How does Facade differ from Mediator? Does Facade hide the subsystem or just simplify access? Facade Pattern (Padho: Fa-saad) ek library, framework ya complex system ko access karne ke liye ek bohot hi simplified interface (ya front-face) deta hai.

n: Flyweight — share fine-grained objects to support large numbers efficiently
x: Flyweight minimizes memory usage by sharing as much data as possible with similar objects. Intrinsic state (shared) vs extrinsic state (passed in context). How do you decide what goes into intrinsic vs extrinsic state in the Flyweight pattern? Give an example.

n: Proxy — provide a surrogate or placeholder to control access
x: Proxy provides a surrogate or placeholder for another object to control access. Variants: virtual proxy (lazy load), protection proxy (access control), remote proxy. What are the four variants of Proxy and what problem does each solve? How does Proxy differ from Decorator? Proxy Pattern kisi dusre object ke liye ek surrogate (ya substitute) provide karta hai, taaki us object ke access ko control kiya ja sake.

n: Chain of Responsibility — pass requests along a chain of handlers
x: Chain of Responsibility passes a request along a chain of handlers. Each handler decides to process the request or pass it to the next handler. How does Chain of Responsibility decouple the sender from the receiver? What happens if no handler processes the request?

n: Command — encapsulate a request as an object (undo/redo, queue, log)
x: Command encapsulates a request as an object, allowing parameterization, queuing, logging, undo/redo. Contains all info needed to perform an action. How does Command enable undo/redo functionality? What is the relationship between Command and Memento?

n: Interpreter — define grammar + interpreter for language sentences
x: Interpreter defines a grammar for a language and an interpreter that uses the representation to interpret sentences in the language. When is Interpreter appropriate vs using a parser generator? What are the trade-offs?

n: Iterator — provide sequential access to elements without exposing internals
x: Iterator provides a way to access elements of a collection sequentially without exposing the underlying representation. How does Iterator separate traversal logic from the collection? Why is it useful for different collection types?

n: Mediator — reduce chaotic coupling by centralizing communication
x: Mediator reduces chaotic communication between multiple objects by introducing a mediator object that centralizes interactions. What is the trade-off of Mediator? How does it risk becoming a God Object and how do you prevent that?

n: Memento — capture and restore object state without violating encapsulation
x: Memento captures and externalizes an object's internal state so it can be restored later without violating encapsulation. How does Memento preserve encapsulation while enabling undo/checkpoint functionality? What are the three roles?

n: Observer — define one-to-many dependency; when one changes, all dependents notified
x: Observer defines a one-to-many dependency between objects. When the subject changes state, all its dependents (observers) are notified and updated automatically. What is the difference between push model and pull model in Observer? When would you use each?

n: State — alter behavior when internal state changes (state machine)
x: State allows an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes. The object appears to change its class. Each state is a separate class. How does State eliminate complex if/else switch statements? How does it differ from Strategy?

n: Strategy — define family of algorithms, make them interchangeable
x: Strategy defines a family of algorithms, encapsulates each one, and makes them interchangeable. The algorithm can vary independently from clients that use it. How does Strategy enable selecting algorithms at runtime? Give an example where it replaces complex conditional logic.

n: Template Method — define skeleton of algorithm, subclasses override steps
x: Template Method defines the skeleton of an algorithm in a method, deferring some steps to subclasses. Subclasses redefine certain steps without changing the algorithm's structure. What is the Hollywood Principle and how does Template Method embody it? What are hook methods?

n: Visitor — separate algorithm from object structure (Double Dispatch)
x: Visitor lets you define a new operation without changing the classes of the elements on which it operates. Separates algorithm from object structure via Double Dispatch. What is Double Dispatch and how does Visitor achieve it? When is Visitor appropriate vs when does it become a maintenance burden?

n: Active Object — decouple method execution from invocation (async + scheduler)
x: Active Object decouples method execution from method invocation. Each object has its own thread of control and a scheduler that queues invocation requests. How does Active Object enable asynchronous processing without explicit thread management? How does it relate to the Actor model?

n: Balking — only execute action if object is in appropriate state
x: Balking Pattern prevents an action if the object is in an inappropriate state. If the guard condition fails, the method returns immediately (bails out). How does Balking provide a simple alternative to blocking for handling race conditions? Give a real-world example.

n: Barrier — synchronize a group of threads at a common point
x: Barrier synchronizes multiple threads at a common point. All threads must arrive at the barrier before any can proceed past it. How does CyclicBarrier differ from CountDownLatch? When would you use a barrier for parallel algorithms?

n: Double-Checked Locking — reduce lock overhead by checking before acquiring
x: Double-Checked Locking reduces the overhead of acquiring a lock by first testing the locking criterion without acquiring the lock. Why does Double-Checked Locking require the volatile keyword in Java? What problem occurs without it?

n: Future / Promise — placeholder for async result (CompletableFuture)
x: Future/Promise represents a placeholder for a result that hasn't been computed yet. The future is returned immediately; the caller can check, block, or attach callbacks. How does CompletableFuture enable non-blocking asynchronous composition without callback nesting?

n: Producer-Consumer — decouple producers from consumers via a buffer
x: Producer-Consumer decouples producers (create data) from consumers (process data) using a shared buffer/queue. How does BlockingQueue simplify Producer-Consumer? What happens if the buffer is full or empty?

n: Read-Write Lock — allow concurrent reads, exclusive writes
x: Read-Write Lock allows multiple threads to read simultaneously but requires exclusive access for writes. Improves concurrency for read-heavy workloads. Why is Read-Write Lock better than a regular mutex for read-heavy workloads? What is the risk of writer starvation?

n: Thread Pool — manage reusable threads for executing tasks
x: Thread Pool manages a reusable pool of worker threads. Tasks are submitted to a queue, and idle workers pick up tasks. What are the different types of thread pools (fixed, cached, scheduled)? What is a rejection policy?

n: Thread-Local Storage — isolate data per thread (no synchronization needed)
x: Thread-Local Storage provides each thread with its own copy of a variable. No synchronization needed because each thread has exclusive access to its own copy. How does ThreadLocal eliminate contention for per-thread data? What is the memory leak risk in thread pools?

n: MVC — Model-View-Controller: separate data, UI, and input handling
x: MVC separates an application into three components: Model (data + business logic), View (UI presentation), Controller (handles input and updates Model/View). How does MVC enable multiple views of the same model and testable business logic independent of UI?

n: MVP / MVVM — presentation patterns for testable UIs
x: MVP/MVVM are presentation patterns for testable UIs. MVP: View is passive, Presenter contains logic. MVVM: View binds to ViewModel via data binding. Compare MVP and MVVM. When would you choose one over the other for testability and boilerplate?

n: Layered Architecture — horizontal layers (presentation, business, persistence)
x: Layered Architecture organizes code into horizontal layers (presentation, business, persistence). Each layer has a specific responsibility and communicates only with adjacent layers. What is the sinkhole anti-pattern in Layered Architecture? When does layered architecture become a monolithic problem?

n: Microservices — decompose by business capability, independently deployable
x: Microservices decomposes an application into small, independently deployable services organized around business capabilities. What are the trade-offs of microservices vs monoliths? How do you handle distributed transactions?

n: Event-Driven Architecture — components communicate via events (pub/sub)
x: Event-Driven Architecture components communicate through events. Producers emit events, consumers react. Can use message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ). What are the challenges of event-driven architecture in terms of tracing and debugging? Compare pub/sub to point-to-point.

n: CQRS — separate command (write) and query (read) models
x: CQRS separates read operations (queries) from write operations (commands). They may use different models and even different data stores. How does CQRS optimize reads and writes independently? Why is it often paired with Event Sourcing?

n: Event Sourcing — store state changes as sequence of events
x: Event Sourcing stores state changes as a sequence of events. Current state is derived by replaying all events. Events are the single source of truth. How does Event Sourcing provide a complete audit trail? What is the snapshot optimization for large event streams?

n: Hexagonal / Ports & Adapters — core logic isolated from external systems
x: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters) isolates core business logic from external systems. Core defines ports (interfaces); adapters implement them. How does Hexagonal Architecture make core logic testable without infrastructure? What are driving vs driven adapters?

n: Domain-Driven Design — ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, aggregates
x: Domain-Driven Design focuses on modeling the domain first. Uses ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, aggregates, entities, value objects. What is a bounded context and an aggregate in DDD? How does ubiquitous language bridge domain experts and developers?

n: Repository Pattern — mediate between domain and data mapping layers
x: Repository Pattern mediates between the domain and data mapping layers. Acts like an in-memory collection of domain objects. How does Repository abstract persistence details away from domain code? How does it simplify unit testing?

n: Unit of Work — maintain list of changed objects, commit as transaction
x: Unit of Work maintains a list of objects affected by a business transaction. Coordinates writing changes and resolves concurrency problems. How does Unit of Work ensure transactional consistency? What is the relationship with Repository?

Design a multi-level parking lot handling vehicle entry/exit, spot assignment, fee calculation. Patterns: Singleton, Factory, Strategy. LLD Problem: Design a parking lot system. Model different vehicle types, spot assignment, and fee calculation.

Design elevator logic with request handling, direction strategy, door operations. Patterns: State, Command, Observer. LLD Problem: Design an elevator control system. Handle concurrent requests from multiple floors.

Design product selection, payment processing, change calculation, and inventory management. Patterns: State, Factory. LLD Problem: Design a vending machine with product selection, payment, and change calculation.

Model pieces with movement rules, board state, player turns, check/checkmate detection. Patterns: Composite, Command, Strategy, Memento. LLD Problem: Design a chess game system with move validation, undo/redo, and AI opponents.

Design books, members, borrowing/returning, fines management. Patterns: Repository, Singleton, Factory. LLD Problem: Design a library management system with borrowing, returns, reservations, and fine calculation.

Design a flexible logging system with multiple appenders, log levels, formatting. Patterns: Singleton, Chain of Resp, Factory. LLD Problem: Design a logging framework with configurable log levels, appenders, and formatting.
Design a topic-based publish/subscribe system. Patterns: Observer, Singleton, Thread Pool. LLD Problem: Design a pub-sub message queue with topics, subscribers, and async delivery.

Model card authentication, account types, transactions. Patterns: State, Command, Chain of Resp. LLD Problem: Design an ATM system with card authentication, PIN verification, and transaction processing.
Design the board, players, win condition checking. Patterns: Strategy, Factory. LLD Problem: Design a Tic Tac Toe game supporting human vs human and human vs computer modes.

Create stories/tasks, assign, transition through workflow states. Patterns: State, Command, Observer, Composite. LLD Problem: Design a task management system with workflow states, assignments, and notifications.
Limit API requests per client within time windows. Patterns: Strategy, Proxy, Factory. LLD Problem: Design a rate limiter supporting multiple algorithms (Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket, Sliding Window).

Design real-time messaging with rooms, private messages, user status. Patterns: Observer, Mediator, Command, Singleton. LLD Problem: Design a real-time chat system with rooms, private messaging, and presence tracking.

n: God Object — one class knows/does too much (violates SRP)
x: God Object — a single class that knows too much or does too much. It has too many responsibilities and becomes extremely hard to maintain. How does the God Object violate SRP? What refactoring steps would you take to fix one?

n: Spaghetti Code — no clear structure, GOTO-like logic
x: Spaghetti Code — code with no clear structure, characterized by excessive nesting, and unpredictable control flow. How does deep nesting and scattered state mutations create spaghetti code? How do design patterns help?

n: Golden Hammer — applying a favorite pattern everywhere
x: Golden Hammer — treating every problem as a nail because you have a favorite pattern. Over-applying a pattern that worked well elsewhere. When does using a design pattern become over-engineering? How does YAGNI relate to the Golden Hammer?

n: Callback Hell — deeply nested callbacks, use Promises/async patterns
x: Callback Hell (Pyramid of Doom) — deeply nested callbacks that make code hard to read, reason about, and debug. How do Promises and async/await solve Callback Hell? What design pattern can help organize callback chains?

n: Singleton Abuse — overusing global state, testing difficulties
x: Singleton Abuse — overusing the Singleton pattern leads to global state that is hard to test, reason about, and maintain. Why are Singletons considered an anti-pattern in many contexts? What is the preferred alternative?

n: Yo-Yo Problem — deep inheritance hierarchies making code hard to follow
x: Yo-Yo Problem — deep inheritance hierarchies where understanding behavior requires jumping up and down the hierarchy repeatedly. How does deep inheritance create the fragile base class problem? How does composition over inheritance solve this?

n: Premature Optimization — optimizing before understanding the real bottleneck
x: Premature Optimization — optimizing code before understanding the actual bottleneck. Knuth: "Premature optimization is the root of all evil." Why is premature optimization problematic even when the optimization seems obvious? What is the correct approach?

n: "Design a system to support multiple notification channels" (Strategy + Observer)
x: Design a system that sends notifications via email, SMS, push, and in-app. Strategy (channel algorithms), Observer (trigger events), Factory (channel creation). Design a notification system that supports email, SMS, push, and in-app notifications. How do you add a new channel?

n: "Design a document editor with undo/redo" (Command + Memento)
x: Design text operations as Command objects. Each command stores state for undo (Memento). Command history stack enables undo/redo navigation. Design a document editor with full undo/redo capability. How do you handle large document memory for undo history?

n: "Design a cache with eviction policies" (Strategy + Proxy)
x: Design a cache with pluggable eviction algorithms. Strategy (LRU, LFU, FIFO), Proxy (wrap data source), Singleton (cache manager). Design a thread-safe cache with pluggable eviction policies. How would you implement LRU efficiently?

n: "Design a workflow engine" (Chain of Resp + Command + State)
x: Design a system that executes a series of steps with branching, parallel execution, and state persistence. Design a workflow engine that supports sequential steps, branching, parallel execution, and state persistence.

Architecture for loading third-party extensions at runtime. Strategy (plugin interface), Factory (discovery/instantiation), Proxy (sandboxed wrapper). Design a plugin system that loads third-party extensions at runtime with security isolation.

n: "Design a UI component library" (Composite + Decorator + Strategy)
x: Design a reusable component system. Composite (component tree), Decorator (add styling/behavior), Strategy (rendering for themes). Design a UI component library that supports theming and composable component trees.

n: Strategy vs State — same structure, different intent (algorithm vs state machine)
x: Strategy vs State — both have identical class structures (Context + interface + concrete classes). Difference is intent: Strategy selects algorithm, State manages behavior transitions. Strategy and State have identical UML. How do you distinguish them by intent and usage?

n: Decorator vs Proxy — both wrap, but intent differs (add features vs control access)
x: Decorator vs Proxy — both wrap an object and forward calls. Intent differs: Decorator adds new behavior, Proxy controls access. How is the intent different between Decorator and Proxy when they both wrap objects? Give examples.

n: Factory vs Builder — Factory creates in one step, Builder in multiple steps
x: Factory vs Builder — Factory creates in one step (single method call). Builder creates in multiple steps, allowing different configurations. When would you choose Builder over Factory? What problem does each solve?

n: Observer vs Mediator — Observer is distributed, Mediator is centralized
x: Observer vs Mediator — both handle communication. Observer distributes (one-to-many notification). Mediator centralizes (many-to-many through coordinator). When does Observer's distributed communication become a problem, and how does Mediator solve it?

n: Adapter vs Facade — Adapter changes interface, Facade simplifies
x: Adapter vs Facade — both wrap something existing. Adapter converts one interface to another (interface transformation). Facade provides simplified interface (simplification). What is the key difference in motivation between Adapter and Facade? Compare their level of abstraction.

n: Command vs Strategy — Command has undo/redo, Strategy is interchangeable algorithms
x: Command vs Strategy — both encapsulate behavior in objects. Command represents a request (action + parameters) with undo support. Strategy represents interchangeable algorithms. How does Command's undo/redo capability distinguish it from Strategy which also encapsulates behavior?

A Null Object implements the interface with no-op behavior. Client code works with real and null objects identically — no null checks needed. Common in UI trees (no-op component), logging (null logger), and caching (null cache that just doesn't cache). How does the Null Object pattern eliminate null checks and where is it commonly used?

Specification pattern encapsulates business rules as composable objects. Each specification tests an object against a rule. Compose with AND, OR, NOT to build complex queries. Separates business logic from data access. How does the Specification pattern encapsulate and compose business rules? How does it fit with the Repository pattern?

A monolith is a single application where ALL the code runs in one process and deploys as one unit. Login, ordering, payments, emails — one codebase, one server, one deploy command. What is a monolith? Why is it the correct starting architecture for most products? Monolith Ek codebase, ek process, ek deploy. In-process call Function call, network nahi. Single DB Ek shared database. Definition: Saari functionality (login, orders, payments, emails) ek hi application mein, ek hi process mein deploy hoti hai. Modules aapas mein function calls se baat karte hain.

Monoliths are simpler in every dimension: function calls instead of network calls (microseconds vs milliseconds), one database transaction covers everything, you can read all code in one place. Why are monoliths simpler than microservices? What advantages do they have in the early stages? Modular monolith Ek deploy, andar clear module boundaries. Local transaction Ek DB transaction. Low ops Kam infra complexity. Definition: Monolith har dimension mein simple hai: network calls ki jagah function calls, ek hi debugger, ek hi deploy, easy refactoring aur transactions.

Monoliths break at scale in four concrete ways: independent scaling becomes impossible, deployments become risky, teams block each other, and one crash takes down everything. What are the four concrete ways a monolith breaks at scale? Independent scaling Sirf hot module ko scale karna. Deploy coupling Ek change = poora redeploy. Team contention Same codebase mein conflicts. Definition: Scale par monolith ke 4 pain points: (1) independent scaling nahi, (2) ek bug sab giraye, (3) deploys slow aur risky, (4) bade teams mein merge conflicts aur ownership unclear.

A microservice is a small, independently deployable process that owns one business domain. Each service has its OWN codebase, database, and deployment pipeline. What is a microservice? How does it differ from a monolith architecturally? Independently deployable Alag deploy bina baaki ko chhue. Owns its data Apna database. Single business capability Ek kaam achhe se. Definition: Microservice chhota, independent process hai jo ek business capability own karta hai — apna code, apna data, apna deploy. Dusre services se network (HTTP/gRPC/events) par baat karta hai.

Microservices require Docker, Kubernetes, a service registry, distributed tracing, a message broker, and engineers who know all of it. A 3-person team using microservices spends more time on infrastructure than on product. When should you NOT use microservices? What is the team size test? Distributed monolith Microservices ki cost, monolith ki coupling. Operational overhead K8s, tracing, discovery, CI per service. Premature split Boundaries galat guess. Definition: Chhoti team, unclear domain, early product, ya strong ops skills ke bina microservices mat lo. Galat boundaries ko baad mein badalna monolith se zyada mahanga hota hai.

Organizations design systems that mirror their own communication structure. A company with 5 engineering teams will inevitably build 5 services. Amazon applied this deliberately with the two-pizza team rule. What is Conway's Law and how does it influence service boundary decisions? Conway's Law System org ke communication structure ko mirror karta hai. Inverse Conway Pehle team structure design karo. Team Topologies Stream-aligned teams. Definition: 'Jo organization system design karti hai, wo aisa design banati hai jo uske communication structure ki copy ho.' Teen teams = teen modules.

Architectural style where app is a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services. Each owns its domain, data, and lifecycle. What are the core characteristics of microservices? What tradeoffs do they introduce? Loose coupling Ek ka change dusre ko na tode. High cohesion Related cheezein saath. Polyglot Har service alag tech. Definition: Application chhoti independent services ka collection, har ek business capability par focused, apna data aur lifecycle, lightweight communication.

Domain-driven design defines bounded contexts — each service owns a subdomain. Strangler Fig pattern for incremental migration. Vertical slicing over horizontal. How do you decide where to draw service boundaries? What is a Bounded Context? Bounded context DDD ka boundary jahan model consistent. By business capability Orders, Payments, Shipping. Strangler Fig Monolith se dheere extract. Definition: Services ko business capability ya bounded context se decompose karo, technical layers se nahi. Existing monolith ke liye Strangler Fig: naye features nayi service mein, purane dheere migrate.

Synchronous (HTTP/gRPC) for request-response. Asynchronous (messages/events) for decoupling. gRPC uses protobuf, HTTP/2, streaming — preferred for internal service-to-service. Compare synchronous and asynchronous inter-service communication. When would you use each? Sync HTTP/gRPC request-response. Async Events/messages. Coupling Temporal coupling sync mein zyada. Definition: Sync simple par caller callee ke availability par depend karta hai. Async decouple karta hai par eventual consistency aur complexity laata hai. Mix: queries sync, workflows async.

Single entry point for all clients — routes, aggregates, transforms. BFF (Backend For Frontend): separate gateway per client type (mobile, web, IoT). What is an API Gateway and why is it necessary in a microservices architecture? API Gateway Single entry, routing, auth, rate limit. BFF Backend-for-frontend per client type. Aggregation Multiple calls ek response mein. Definition: Gateway clients ko services ke internal structure se bachata hai. BFF web/mobile ke liye alag tailored APIs deta hai.

How services find each other's network locations. Client-side: service registry + client load balancing. Server-side: load balancer in front (K8s Service, AWS ALB). How do services discover each other in a dynamic environment like Kubernetes? Registry Service instances ki list. Client-side Client registry se choose kare. Server-side LB/Kubernetes DNS. Definition: Instances dynamically aate-jaate hain, IPs badalte hain. Discovery: Kubernetes DNS/Services, Consul, Eureka. Health checks se unhealthy remove.

Each service owns its data exclusively — no direct DB sharing. Polyglot persistence: choose the right DB per service (SQL for orders, document for catalog, graph for recommendations). Why must each microservice own its own database? What happens when services share a DB? Database per service Har service ka private data store. Polyglot persistence Use-case ke hisaab se DB. No shared tables Dusri service ka DB direct nahi. Definition: Service ka data sirf uski API se access hota hai. Isse schema changes independent hote hain. Cross-service queries API composition ya CQRS views se.

Sequence of local transactions with compensating rollbacks. Choreography: each service listens for events and acts. Orchestration: central coordinator tells each service what to do. How do you handle a transaction that spans multiple services? Explain the Saga pattern. Saga Local transactions ka sequence + compensation. Choreography Events se, central controller nahi. Orchestration Central orchestrator steps chalata hai. Definition: Distributed transaction ki jagah har service local transaction karti hai; fail hone par compensating actions (refund, release stock) chalte hain.

CQRS separates read models (queries) from write models (commands). Event sourcing stores all state changes as an append-only event log — current state is derived by replaying events. What is CQRS and when does it make sense in a microservices architecture? CQRS Read aur write models alag. Event sourcing State = events ka sequence. Projection Events se read model. Definition: CQRS commands (writes) aur queries (reads) alag models mein. Event sourcing state ki jagah events store karta hai — poora history, replay possible.

Services communicate through events — producers emit facts, consumers react. Message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ) provide durability, ordering, and routing. What is event-driven architecture? How does it decouple services? Event Jo ho chuka (past tense) fact. Producer/Consumer Emit / react. Event vs command Event notification; command instruction. Definition: Services facts emit karti hain (OrderPlaced); interested services subscribe karti hain. Producer ko consumers ka pata nahi — loose coupling.

No distributed transactions across services. Embrace eventual consistency. CAP theorem in practice: partition tolerance is non-negotiable, choose consistency (CP) or availability (AP). What is eventual consistency and how does it differ from strong consistency? Eventual consistency Thodi der baad sab sync. Idempotency Duplicate processing safe. Outbox DB transaction mein event save. Definition: Services ke beech strong consistency nahi; eventual consistency accept karo. Tools: sagas, outbox, idempotency keys, reconciliation jobs.

Request-response over HTTP/REST or gRPC. Client waits for response. Simple, familiar, but couples availability — if downstream is down, caller is down too. Compare REST and gRPC for inter-service communication. What are the tradeoffs? REST Resource HTTP/JSON. gRPC HTTP/2 + protobuf, fast, typed. Timeout Har call par. Definition: Sync request-response simple hai. REST public/compatible; gRPC internal low-latency. Resilience: timeout, retry, circuit breaker.

Producer sends message to broker → consumer processes later. Decouples sender and receiver in time and space. Message vs event: message has a specific consumer, event is a fact anyone can react to. How does asynchronous messaging decouple services? What guarantees do brokers provide? Broker Kafka/RabbitMQ/SQS. At-least-once Duplicates possible. DLQ Failed messages. Definition: Producer broker ko message deta hai, consumer baad mein process karta hai. Temporal decoupling, buffering, retry, fan-out.

How services agree on data format. Protobuf (compact, typed, schema evolution), Avro (Hadoop-native, schema on read), JSON (human-readable, no schema). Why is schema management important in event-driven systems? Compare JSON, Protobuf, and Avro. Protobuf/Avro Compact typed schemas. Schema registry Central schema versions. Compatibility Backward/forward. Definition: Services ke beech data format agreement. Schema registry compatibility enforce karti hai taaki producer change consumers ko na tode. JSON flexible par untyped.

When a single operation spans multiple services. Two-phase commit (2PC) for short-lived ACID. Outbox pattern for reliable publishing. Saga for long-lived transactions. How does the Outbox Pattern ensure reliable event publishing alongside database writes? 2PC Prepare + commit, blocking. Saga Compensation based. TCC Try-Confirm-Cancel. Definition: Ek operation kai services span kare to 2PC (strong consistency, coordinator SPOF, lock holding) ya Saga/TCC (eventual). Microservices mein saga prefer hota hai.

Federated GraphQL: multiple services (subgraphs) each own a piece of a unified graph. Gateway (router) composes schemas and routes queries to correct subgraph. What is GraphQL Federation and how does it differ from a monolithic GraphQL API? Subgraph Service ka GraphQL schema part. Supergraph/Router Combined schema. Entity @key se services ke beech shared type. Definition: Federation mein har service apna subgraph own karti hai; router unhe ek unified graph mein jodta hai. Clients ek query se multiple services ka data lete hain.

Wraps remote call with state machine: CLOSED (normal) → OPEN (failing, fast-fail) → HALF-OPEN (test recovery). Prevents cascading failures and lets downstream recover. Explain the Circuit Breaker pattern. What are its three states and when does it trip? Closed Normal, calls pass. Open Fail fast, call nahi jaati. Half-open Kuch trial calls se recovery check. Definition: Circuit breaker failures count karta hai; threshold cross hone par OPEN — calls turant fail (ya fallback). Timeout ke baad HALF-OPEN mein test requests; success par CLOSED.

Retry transient failures with exponential backoff + jitter. Timeouts prevent waiting forever. Never retry on the critical path without circuit breaker. How should you implement retries safely? What is exponential backoff with jitter? Backoff Retry delay badhta hai. Jitter Random delay — thundering herd roke. Timeout Har call par. Definition: Transient failures par retry (exponential backoff + jitter, max attempts). Sirf idempotent operations retry karo. Retry budget rakho.

Isolate resources into pools so failure in one pool doesn't drain shared resources. Thread pool isolation (each service gets its own thread pool) or semaphore isolation (limit concurrent calls). What is the Bulkhead pattern? How does it prevent one slow service from affecting others? Bulkhead Resource pools alag. Thread/connection pool Per-dependency limit. Isolation Ek slow dependency baaki ko na khaye. Definition: Ship ke compartments ki tarah — har dependency ka alag pool/semaphore. Slow service sirf apna pool bharegi, poora app nahi.

Control how many requests a client can make in a window. Protects services from abuse, misconfiguration, or traffic spikes. Token bucket, leaky bucket, sliding window. What are the main rate limiting algorithms? Compare token bucket and sliding window. Rate limit Max requests / window. Throttling Excess ko slow ya reject. 429 Too Many Requests + Retry-After. Definition: Per-client limits service ko overload se bachate hain. Algorithms: token bucket, sliding window. Gateway ya service level par; distributed ho to Redis.

When a dependency fails, degrade the feature instead of breaking the user. Show cached data, hide the widget, serve a fallback response. Fail-open vs fail-closed. What is graceful degradation? How do you decide between fail-open and fail-closed? Graceful degradation Feature kam, system up. Fallback Cache/default response. Load shedding Non-critical requests drop. Definition: Recommendation service down ho to popular items dikhao, error nahi. Critical vs non-critical features classify karo.

Trace a single request across multiple services. Each request gets a traceId propagated in headers. Spans represent units of work. OpenTelemetry is the standard. How does distributed tracing work? What is the role of traceId and spans? Trace Poori request journey. Span Ek service ka step. Context propagation Trace ID headers mein forward. Definition: Har request ko trace ID milta hai jo services ke beech propagate hota hai (W3C traceparent). Backends: Jaeger, Tempo; instrumentation: OpenTelemetry.

All services send logs to a central platform (ELK, Loki, CloudWatch). Correlation IDs tie logs across services. Structured logging (JSON) for machine parsing. Why is centralized logging essential in microservices? What is a correlation ID? Structured logs JSON with fields. Correlation ID Request ko logs mein jodna. ELK/Loki Central search. Definition: Har service stdout par JSON logs likhe; agent unhe central system mein bheje. Fields: timestamp, level, service, traceId, userId (no PII/secrets).

RED method: Rate (requests/sec), Errors (failed requests/sec), Duration (latency percentiles). Four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors, saturation. What is the RED method? How do you use it to monitor microservice health? RED Rate, Errors, Duration. USE Utilization, Saturation, Errors. Percentiles p95/p99 latency. Definition: Services ke liye RED, resources ke liye USE. Prometheus + Grafana. SLO-based alerts (burn rate) symptom par, cause par nahi.

Consumer-driven contract tests: consumer defines expectations, provider validates them against its API. Pact framework. Ensures compatibility without full integration tests. What is contract testing and why is it preferred over full integration tests in microservices? Consumer-driven contract Consumer expectations define. Pact Popular tool. Provider verification Provider contract verify karta hai. Definition: Consumer apni expectations (request/response) contract mein likhta hai; provider CI mein verify karta hai. Breaking change deploy se pehle pakda jaata hai — full E2E ki jagah.

Test services together with real dependencies. Testcontainers for DB/message broker in tests. WireMock for external API stubs. Focus on critical paths. How do you test microservices with real dependencies? What is Testcontainers? Testcontainers Docker se real DB/broker tests. Test pyramid Unit > integration > E2E. Test data Isolated, repeatable. Definition: Service ko real dependencies (DB, Kafka) ke saath test karo — mocks se behtar confidence. Testcontainers har test run ke liye disposable containers deta hai.

Monorepo (single repo, many services) vs polyrepo (repo per service). Monorepo: unified tooling, atomic cross-service changes, but harder to scale CI. Compare monorepo and polyrepo strategies for microservices. What are the tradeoffs? Monorepo Ek repo, kai services. Polyrepo Repo per service. Path filters Sirf changed service build. Definition: Har service ki apni independent pipeline: build → test → image → deploy. Monorepo mein path-based triggers; polyrepo mein shared libs versioning.

Kubernetes: declarative deployment, auto-scaling, self-healing, service discovery, load balancing, secrets, and config management. What are the core Kubernetes objects for running microservices? How does K8s enable self-healing? Orchestrator Kubernetes. Self-healing Restart/reschedule. Declarative Desired state. Definition: Kubernetes containers schedule, scale, heal aur service discovery handle karta hai. Rolling updates, resource limits, probes.

Blue/Green: two identical environments, switch traffic at once. Canary: gradually shift traffic (1% → 5% → 50% → 100%) — monitor metrics, rollback if needed. Compare blue/green and canary deployment strategies. When would you choose each? Blue/Green Instant switch. Canary Gradual %. Rollback Previous version. Definition: Blue/Green fast rollback par double capacity. Canary real traffic ke chhote hisse par metrics dekh kar rollout. Mesh/ingress traffic split.

Externalize config from code — environment-specific values, feature flags, and secrets. Tools: K8s ConfigMaps/Secrets, HashiCorp Vault, AWS Parameter Store. How should you manage configuration and secrets in a microservices deployment? 12-factor config Env mein config. Secrets manager Vault/AWS SM. Dynamic config Runtime change. Definition: Config code se alag (env-specific), secrets encrypted store se, rotation, per-environment values. Feature flags runtime behaviour ke liye.

n: Why Microservices — monolith first, when to split, Conway's Law
x: Start with monolith, split when team size or deployment frequency demands it. Conway's Law: system design mirrors org structure. Microservices add operational complexity (networking, data consistency, deployment). Split by business domain, not technical layer. When should you move from a monolith to microservices? What are the hidden costs? Monolith first Pehle monolith, phir split. Split triggers Team size, deploy frequency, scale needs. Conway Team boundaries. Definition: Microservices tab jab team size, independent scaling ya release cadence demand kare. Martin Fowler: 'MonolithFirst'. Split data-driven ho, trend-driven nahi.

n: Domain-Driven Design — bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language
x: DDD aligns software with business domains. Bounded Context: autonomous domain with its own model. Aggregate: cluster of entities with a root (consistency boundary). Ubiquitous Language: shared vocabulary between devs and domain experts. Context Maps define inter-domain relationships. What is a Bounded Context in DDD? How do you identify service boundaries? Bounded context Model ka boundary. Aggregate Consistency boundary. Ubiquitous language Dev + business shared vocabulary. Definition: DDD business domain ko model karta hai. Aggregate (Order + OrderLines) ek transaction boundary; dusre aggregates IDs se reference. Context map contexts ke relationship batata hai.

n: Kafka — event sourcing, CQRS, exactly-once semantics, consumer groups
x: Kafka: distributed append-only log. Topics partitioned for parallelism. Consumer groups for load balancing. Exactly-once requires idempotent producers + transactional consumers. Event sourcing: store events, derive state. CQRS: separate read/write models. How does Kafka achieve exactly-once delivery? What is the difference between at-least-once and exactly-once? Partition Parallelism + ordering unit. Consumer group Partitions share karte hain. Offset Log position. Definition: Kafka distributed append-only log. Key se partition → same key ka order guaranteed. Consumer group scale-out. Exactly-once (idempotent producer + transactions) limited scope mein.

n: Service Mesh — Istio, Envoy sidecar, mTLS, traffic management
x: Service mesh handles cross-cutting concerns (observability, security, traffic) via sidecar proxies. Istio uses Envoy sidecars. mTLS between services automatically. Traffic management: canary deployments, circuit breaking, retries. Adds latency (~1-2ms per hop). What is a service mesh? When does the overhead justify the benefits? Sidecar Har pod ke saath proxy (Envoy). mTLS Service-to-service encryption. Traffic management Retries, splits, timeouts. Definition: Mesh cross-cutting concerns (mTLS, retries, observability, traffic shifting) application code se nikal ke proxies mein daalta hai. Istio/Linkerd.

n: Chaos Engineering — game days, fault injection, Netflix Chaos Monkey
x: Chaos Engineering: deliberately inject failures to find weaknesses before they cause outages. Chaos Monkey kills random instances. Game days: coordinated failure scenarios. Steady state hypothesis: define expected behavior, then break things. Tools: Chaos Monkey, Litmus, Gremlin. What is Chaos Engineering? How do you run a chaos experiment safely? Hypothesis Steady state expectation. Blast radius Limit scope. Chaos Monkey Random instance kill. Definition: Production-like environment mein failures inject karke resilience verify. Latency, pod kill, dependency down, AZ failure. GameDays teams ko practice dete hain.

n: Event Storming — collaborative design, domain events, aggregates
x: Event Storming is a workshop format for exploring complex domains. Participants map domain events (orange stickies) on a timeline. Commands (yellow), aggregates (blue), policies (purple), read models (green). Big Picture → Process Modeling → Software Design. What is Event Storming and how do you facilitate one? What are the different types of stickies? Domain event Orange sticky: OrderPlaced. Command / Aggregate Blue / yellow stickies. Bounded context Clusters se milte hain. Definition: Workshop jahan dev + domain experts wall par events timeline banate hain. Phir commands, aggregates, policies, hotspots; clusters bounded contexts suggest karte hain.

n: What is DevOps — Culture, Principles, CALMS Framework
x: DevOps is a cultural and technical movement that breaks down silos between development and operations. CALMS: Culture, Automation, Lean, Measurement, Sharing. Explain the CALMS framework and how it applies to DevOps adoption. CALMS Culture, Automation, Lean, Measurement, Sharing. You build it, you run it Dev team production ki ownership leti hai. Silo Dev aur Ops ke beech deewar. Definition: DevOps ek culture + practices ka set hai jo development aur operations ko jodta hai taaki software tez, safe aur baar-baar deliver ho. CALMS framework adoption ko check karne ka tareeka hai. Purane model mein dev code 'deewar ke upar se phenk' deta tha aur ops ko sambhalna padta tha.

n: DevOps vs SRE vs Platform Engineering
x: DevOps is the philosophy. SRE applies software engineering to operations. Platform Engineering builds internal developer platforms (IDPs) for self-service. What is the difference between DevOps, SRE, and Platform Engineering? DevOps Philosophy/culture. SRE Ops ko software engineering se; SLOs, error budgets. Platform Engineering Internal developer platform (self-service). Definition: DevOps 'kya aur kyun', SRE 'reliability ko measurable bana kar kaise' (SLI/SLO/error budget), Platform Engineering 'developers ke liye golden paths/portal' hai.

The software delivery lifecycle: plan → code → build → test → release → deploy → operate → monitor. Automation at every stage reduces lead time and errors. Walk through the SDLC pipeline from commit to production. What metrics define elite performance? Pipeline Automated build→test→release stages. Shift left Testing/security pehle. Fast feedback Fail early. Definition: Plan → code → build → test → release → deploy → operate. Har stage automate; fast tests pehle, slow tests baad mein.

Trunk-based development: short-lived branches merged to main frequently. Feature flags decouple deployment from release — merge dark code, turn on later. What is trunk-based development and how do feature flags enable it? Trunk-based Short-lived branches, main par frequent merge. Feature flag Code deploy, feature hidden. Long-lived branch Merge hell. Definition: Developers din mein kai baar main mein merge karte hain; incomplete features flags ke peeche. Release = flag on, deploy = code shipping — dono alag.

DORA identifies four key metrics: Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Change Failure Rate, Time to Restore Service. What are the four DORA metrics and what benchmarks define elite performance? Deployment Frequency Kitni baar prod deploy. Lead Time Commit → prod time. Change Failure Rate / MTTR Kitne deploys fail; recover kitne time mein. Definition: DORA ke 4 metrics: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, time to restore. Elite teams speed aur stability dono mein achhi hoti hain.

n: CI/CD Pipeline Design — Stages, Gates, Artifact Promotion
x: CI (Continuous Integration): merge frequently, build and test every change. CD (Continuous Delivery): every change is deployable but release is manual. Design a CI/CD pipeline from scratch. What are the key stages and gates? CI Frequent merge + automated build/test. Continuous Delivery Hamesha deployable; manual approval. Continuous Deployment Auto prod deploy. Definition: Build once, promote same artifact across environments (dev→staging→prod). Gates: tests, scans, approvals. Artifact immutable.

n: GitHub Actions — Workflows, Runners, Matrix Builds
x: GitHub Actions is CI/CD natively integrated with GitHub. Workflows are YAML with triggers, jobs, steps. Runners can be GitHub-hosted or self-hosted. How do you design an efficient GitHub Actions workflow? Explain matrix builds and caching. Workflow YAML in .github/workflows. Runner Job chalane wali machine. Matrix Multiple versions/OS parallel. Definition: Events (push, PR) par jobs/steps chalte hain. Matrix builds, caching, secrets, reusable workflows, environments with approvals.

n: Deployment Strategies — Blue/Green, Canary, Rolling, A/B
