x: Blue/green: two identical environments, switch traffic. Canary: percentage of traffic to new version. Rolling: gradually replace instances. Compare blue/green, canary, and rolling deployment strategies. When would you choose each? Blue/Green Do envs, traffic switch. Canary Chhota % pehle. Rolling Instances dheere replace. Definition: Blue/green instant rollback deta hai par double capacity. Canary real traffic par risk kam karta hai. Rolling default K8s strategy. A/B experiments ke liye.

Artifacts are versioned, signed, and stored in registries. Immutability: once tagged/pushed, artifact never changes. Why is artifact immutability critical for reproducible deployments? How do you enforce it? Registry Artifacts store (ECR, Nexus, npm). Immutability Tag overwrite nahi. Semver / SHA Version identify. Definition: Har build ek versioned artifact (image digest/SHA). Immutable tags, signed, retention policy, vulnerability scan registry mein.

n: Pipeline Security — SAST, DAST, SBOM, Supply Chain
x: SAST scans source code. DAST scans running app. SBOM catalogs dependencies. Supply chain security ensures trusted artifacts. How do you build security into a CI/CD pipeline? Explain SAST, DAST, and SCA. SAST Source scan. DAST Running app scan. SBOM Components inventory. Definition: Pipeline mein secrets scan, SAST, SCA, container scan, DAST, signing aur provenance (SLSA). Pipeline khud bhi attack target hai — least privilege tokens.

n: Docker Architecture — Images, Layers, Union FS, Overlay2
x: Docker images are read-only layers built from a Dockerfile. Each instruction creates a layer. Union filesystem (overlay2) merges layers. Explain Docker image layers and how the overlay2 filesystem works. Image Read-only layered template. Layer Har Dockerfile instruction ek layer. Overlay2 Union filesystem — layers stack + writable top layer. Definition: Image layers ka stack hai, container = image + writable layer. Layers cache aur share hote hain. Containers namespaces (isolation) aur cgroups (resource limits) use karte hain.

n: Dockerfile Best Practices — Multi-stage, Cache, Minimal Images
x: Multi-stage builds: use one image to build and a separate minimal image to run. Result: tiny production images without build tools. How do you write an optimized Dockerfile? Explain multi-stage builds and layer caching. Multi-stage Build stage alag, runtime stage chhota. Layer cache Kam badalne wali cheezein upar. Minimal base alpine/distroless. Definition: Dependencies pehle copy+install, phir source — cache hit zyada. Multi-stage se compilers final image mein nahi. .dockerignore, non-root user, pinned versions.

n: Container Networking — Bridge, Host, Overlay, CNI
x: Bridge: default network. Host: shares host network stack. Overlay: multi-host networking via VXLAN. CNI: standard interface for container networking. Compare bridge, host, and overlay networking in Docker. When would you use each? Bridge Default private network on host. Host Container host network share karta hai. Overlay Multi-host networking. Definition: Bridge network par containers apas mein naam se baat karte hain (user-defined bridge). Ports publish karke bahar. K8s mein CNI plugins pod networking dete hain.

n: Container Security — Non-root, Read-only FS, Seccomp, AppArmor
x: Run containers as non-root user. Mount filesystem read-only where possible. Seccomp restricts syscalls. AppArmor/SELinux Mandatory Access Control. List the key container security hardening techniques and why each matters. Non-root USER directive. Seccomp Syscalls filter. AppArmor MAC profile. Definition: Root user, privileged mode, docker.sock mount avoid. Read-only rootfs, capabilities drop, seccomp default profile, resource limits.

Docker Compose defines multi-container applications in YAML. Services, networks, volumes, environment variables configured in docker-compose.yml. How do you set up a reproducible local development environment with Docker Compose? Service Container definition. depends_on Start order (readiness nahi). Volumes Persistent data. Definition: docker-compose.yml mein app + DB + cache ek command se. Local dev aur integration tests ke liye perfect; production orchestration nahi.

n: K8s Architecture — Control Plane, Nodes, etcd, Scheduler
x: Control plane: API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager. Workers: kubelet, kube-proxy, container runtime (containerd). Explain the Kubernetes control plane components and their responsibilities. API server Cluster ka front door. etcd Cluster state store. Scheduler/Controllers Pod placement / desired state reconcile. Definition: Control plane: API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager. Nodes: kubelet, container runtime, kube-proxy. Declarative model: desired state likho, controllers actual ko match karte hain.

Pod: smallest deployable unit. Deployment: declarative updates for Pods. Service: stable network endpoint for a set of Pods. Explain the relationship between Pods, Deployments, and Services in Kubernetes. Pod Smallest unit; containers share network. Deployment Replicas + rolling updates. Service Stable virtual IP/DNS for pods. Definition: Deployment ReplicaSet ke through pods manage karta hai. Service label selector se pods ko load-balance karta hai. ConfigMap config, Secret sensitive (base64, encrypted nahi by default).

n: K8s Networking — Ingress, CNI, Service Mesh
x: Ingress: L7 load balancing with path/host-based routing. CNI: pod networking and network policies. Service mesh: mTLS, traffic management. How does Kubernetes handle networking? Compare Ingress, CNI, and service mesh. Ingress L7 routing host/path. CNI Pod network plugin (Calico, Cilium). Service mesh Sidecar proxies. Definition: Service types: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer. Ingress controller (nginx) HTTP routing deta hai. Har pod ka apna IP; CNI pod-to-pod connectivity deta hai.

Helm: Kubernetes package manager — Charts bundle templates + values. CRD: extends K8s API. Operator: controller that watches CRDs and reconciles state. What are Helm Charts, CRDs, and Operators? How do they work together? Helm chart Templates + values package. CRD Custom resource definition. Operator CRD + controller automation. Definition: Helm templating se same manifests alag environments mein; Operators (jaise Postgres operator) domain knowledge (backup, failover) automate karte hain.

n: K8s Security — RBAC, Pod Security, Network Policies
x: RBAC: Role-based access control for API operations. Pod Security Standards: privileged, baseline, restricted. NetworkPolicies: pod-level firewall. How do you secure a Kubernetes cluster? Explain RBAC, Pod Security, and NetworkPolicies. RBAC Roles + bindings. NetworkPolicy Pod traffic firewall. Pod Security Restricted/baseline standards. Definition: Least-privilege RBAC, default-deny NetworkPolicy, Pod Security Admission, secrets encryption/external secrets, image policies, audit logs.

Terraform declares infrastructure in HCL. State file maps config to real resources. Modules encapsulate reusable infrastructure. Workspaces isolate environments. Explain Terraform state management, modules, and workspaces. State Config aur real resources ka mapping. Module Reusable infra block. Provider AWS/GCP plugin. Definition: Terraform HCL mein desired infra declare karta hai. plan diff dikhata hai, apply change karta hai, state file track karti hai.

n: Terraform Advanced — Remote State, Locking, Drift Detection
x: Remote state stores terraform.tfstate in S3/GCS with DynamoDB locking. Plan detects drift between declared state and real infrastructure. What is infrastructure drift and how does Terraform detect and handle it? Remote state S3/GCS backend. Locking DynamoDB lock — concurrent apply roke. Drift Real infra config se alag. Definition: Team ke liye state remote + locked + encrypted. Drift detection scheduled terraform plan se. State split per environment/component.

n: Configuration Management — Ansible vs Chef vs Puppet
x: Ansible: agentless, push-based, YAML playbooks. Chef: agent-based, Ruby DSL, pull-based. Puppet: agent-based, declarative DSL, pull-based. Compare Ansible, Chef, and Puppet. When would you choose each? Ansible Agentless, push, YAML. Chef/Puppet Agent-based, pull. Idempotent Baar-baar chalane par same result. Definition: Config management servers ke andar software/config manage karta hai. Ansible SSH se; Terraform provisioning ke liye, Ansible configuration ke liye.

n: Immutable Infrastructure — Packer, AMIs, Golden Images
x: Immutable infrastructure: never modify running servers — replace them. Packer builds machine images with everything baked in. Golden images are versioned templates. What is immutable infrastructure and how does it eliminate configuration drift? Immutable Server replace, patch nahi. Packer Machine images build. Golden AMI Pre-baked image. Definition: Change = naya image build → naye instances launch → purane terminate. Snowflake servers aur drift khatam.

n: GitOps — ArgoCD, Flux, Declarative Continuous Delivery
x: GitOps: Git repo is the single source of truth. ArgoCD/Flux reconciles cluster state with what's in the Git repo. Syncs automatically on commit. What is GitOps and how does ArgoCD implement it for Kubernetes deployments? GitOps Git = source of truth. ArgoCD/Flux Cluster ko Git se reconcile. Pull-based Cluster khud Git se kheenchta hai. Definition: Deploy = Git commit/PR. Controller continuously desired state vs live compare karke sync karta hai. Audit trail, rollback = git revert.

n: Capacity Planning & Auto-scaling — HPA, VPA, Cluster Autoscaler
x: HPA: scales pods based on CPU/memory or custom metrics. VPA: adjusts pod resource requests. Cluster autoscaler: adds/removes nodes. Explain HPA, VPA, and cluster autoscaler. How do they work together? HPA Pods count badhao/ghatao. VPA Pod resources adjust. Cluster Autoscaler Nodes add/remove. Definition: HPA CPU/custom metrics (RPS, queue depth) par pods scale karta hai. Nodes ke liye Cluster Autoscaler/Karpenter. Load test se baseline set karo.

n: Disaster Recovery & Backup — RPO, RTO, Multi-region
x: RPO: max acceptable data loss. RTO: max acceptable downtime. Multi-region: active-active vs active-passive. Define RPO and RTO. How do you design a disaster recovery strategy for a cloud application? RPO Max data loss window. RTO Max downtime. Strategies Backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active. Definition: RPO/RTO business tay karta hai; strategy uske hisaab se (cost badhta jaata hai). Backups ka restore test karna zaroori.

Chaos engineering: proactively inject failures to build confidence in system resilience. Principles: steady state hypothesis, run experiment in production. What is chaos engineering? How do you run a safe GameDay in production? Steady state Normal behaviour hypothesis. Blast radius Experiment ka scope. GameDay Planned failure drill. Definition: Production-jaisi conditions mein controlled failures (pod kill, latency inject, AZ outage) se weaknesses dhundna. Hypothesis → experiment → learn → fix.

n: Compliance & Audit — SOC2, HIPAA, Policy-as-Code (OPA, Kyverno)
x: SOC2: security controls for service providers. HIPAA: healthcare data protection. Policy-as-code: OPA and Kyverno enforce rules as code. How do you implement policy-as-code in a Kubernetes environment using OPA or Kyverno? Policy as code OPA/Kyverno rules. SOC2 Controls audit. Admission control Cluster mein enter hone se pehle check. Definition: Policies code mein: 'koi privileged pod nahi', 'images sirf trusted registry se', 'S3 public nahi'. CI aur admission controller dono par enforce; audit evidence auto.

n: EC2 — instances, AMIs, security groups, key pairs
x: EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) provides virtual servers in the cloud. An AMI is a template for an instance (OS + software). Security groups act as virtual firewalls controlling inbound/outbound traffic. Key pairs provide SSH access. What is an EC2 instance? How do security groups differ from network ACLs? AMI Machine image. Security Group Stateful firewall. Instance types General/compute/memory optimized. Definition: EC2 virtual servers. Purchasing: On-Demand, Reserved/Savings Plans, Spot. Key pair SSH ke liye (ya SSM Session Manager better). ASG scaling.

n: S3 — buckets, lifecycle policies, presigned URLs, versioning
x: S3 (Simple Storage Service) stores objects (files) in buckets. Lifecycle policies auto-move objects between storage classes (Standard, IA, Glacier). Presigned URLs grant temporary access to private objects. Versioning keeps object history. What is S3? How do lifecycle policies reduce storage costs? Bucket/object Flat key-value storage. Lifecycle Tier/expire rules. Presigned URL Temporary access link. Definition: S3 11 9s durability. Versioning, lifecycle (IA/Glacier), SSE-KMS, Block Public Access, presigned URLs direct upload/download ke liye.

n: RDS — managed databases, Multi-AZ, read replicas, backups
x: RDS (Relational Database Service) manages PostgreSQL, MySQL, etc. Multi-AZ provides automatic failover for high availability. Read replicas scale read traffic. Automated backups enable point-in-time recovery. What is RDS? How does Multi-AZ differ from Read Replicas? Multi-AZ Standby failover (HA). Read replica Read scaling (async). PITR Point-in-time restore. Definition: RDS managed backups, patching, failover. Multi-AZ availability ke liye, read replicas performance ke liye — dono alag cheezein.

n: Lambda — serverless functions, cold starts, event sources
x: Lambda runs code without managing servers. Triggered by events (API Gateway, S3, SQS, DynamoDB streams). Cold start = first invocation delay. Provisioned concurrency eliminates cold starts at extra cost. What is AWS Lambda? What causes cold starts and how do you mitigate them? Cold start Naye execution environment ka startup delay. Event source API GW, S3, SQS, EventBridge. Concurrency Parallel executions limit. Definition: Lambda event aane par code chalata hai, per-invocation billing. Limits: 15 min, memory 10GB. Provisioned concurrency cold start kam karta hai.

n: VPC — subnets, route tables, NAT gateway, internet gateway
x: VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) is your isolated network in AWS. Public subnets have internet access via Internet Gateway. Private subnets use NAT Gateway for outbound-only internet. Route tables control traffic flow between subnets. What is a VPC? How do public and private subnets differ? Public subnet IGW route. Private subnet NAT ke through egress. Route table Traffic rules. Definition: VPC mein CIDR, subnets (multi-AZ), route tables, IGW (internet), NAT GW (private se bahar), VPC endpoints (AWS services bina internet).

n: IAM — users, roles, policies, least privilege
x: IAM (Identity and Access Management) controls who can do what. Users have long-term credentials. Roles provide temporary credentials (for EC2, Lambda, etc.). Policies are JSON documents granting/denying permissions. Least privilege = only grant what is needed. What is IAM? What is the difference between an IAM user and an IAM role? Role Temporary credentials assume karo. Policy JSON permissions. Least privilege Sirf zaroori actions. Definition: Users ke liye SSO/MFA, workloads ke liye roles (instance profile, IRSA), long-lived access keys avoid. Explicit Deny > Allow. Access Analyzer unused permissions batata hai.

CloudWatch collects metrics (CPU, memory, request count), logs (Lambda, EC2, RDS), and alarms (notify when threshold breached). Dashboards visualize metrics. CloudWatch Events/EventBridge route events between services. How do you set up an alarm for high CPU on an EC2 instance using CloudWatch? Metrics Time series (CPU, requests). Logs Insights Log query. Alarm Threshold → SNS/action. Definition: CloudWatch metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards. Custom metrics, composite alarms. Memory/disk ke liye agent chahiye.

n: ALB & ELB — load balancing, health checks, target groups
x: ALB (Application Load Balancer) routes HTTP/HTTPS traffic to targets (EC2, Lambda, IP). ELB is the umbrella name. Health checks ensure traffic only goes to healthy targets. Target groups define which instances receive traffic. What is the difference between ALB and NLB? When would you use each? ALB L7 HTTP routing. NLB L4, high performance. Target group + health check Healthy targets. Definition: ALB path/host routing, WebSocket, WAF integration. Health checks unhealthy targets nikalte hain. Connection draining deployments mein.

n: Serverless — Lambda, API Gateway, event-driven architecture
x: Serverless = no server management. AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, GCP Cloud Run. API Gateway routes HTTP to Lambda. Event-driven: S3, SQS, DynamoDB streams trigger functions. Cold starts, execution limits (15min Lambda), vendor lock-in. What are the limitations of serverless? When should you NOT use serverless? FaaS Function as a service. Event-driven Triggers par execution. Pay-per-use Idle par cost zero. Definition: Serverless mein infra management provider ka; auto-scale, per-ms billing. Patterns: API GW+Lambda, S3→Lambda, queue workers, step functions.

n: Cloud Networking — VPC, subnets, security groups, load balancers
x: VPC isolates your cloud network. Public subnets have internet access. Private subnets are internal only. Security groups are stateful firewalls. NACLs are stateless. ALB for HTTP routing. NLB for TCP/UDP. NAT Gateway for private subnet internet access. What is the difference between a security group and a NACL? Subnet/VPC Isolated network. Security group Stateful instance-level. Load balancer Traffic distribute. Definition: Public/private subnets, SG vs NACL, LB layers (L4/L7), DNS (Route53), CDN, VPN/peering/Transit Gateway.

n: Cloud Cost Optimization — Reserved Instances, Spot, right-sizing
x: Reserved Instances: 1-3 year commitments for 30-60% discount. Spot Instances: up to 90% discount but can be terminated. Right-sizing: match instance type to workload. Savings Plans: flexible commitment. Cost allocation tags for per-team billing. How do you reduce AWS costs by 50%? What is the difference between Reserved Instances and Savings Plans? Right-sizing Instance size usage ke hisaab se. Savings Plans/RI Commitment discount. Spot Interruptible cheap capacity. Definition: Pehle visibility (tags, Cost Explorer), phir right-size, idle resources delete, commitment discounts steady load par, spot fault-tolerant workloads par, storage tiering, data transfer kam.

n: Feature Flags — progressive delivery, A/B testing, kill switches
x: Feature flags control feature visibility without deployment. Progressive delivery: gradual rollout (1% → 10% → 100%). A/B testing: split traffic between variants. Kill switches: instantly disable broken features. Tools: LaunchDarkly, Unleash, Flagsmith. How do feature flags enable progressive delivery? What is the difference between release flags and experiment flags? Progressive delivery Percentage rollout. Kill switch Turant feature band. Targeting User/segment rules. Definition: Flags runtime par behaviour badalte hain bina deploy. Use: gradual rollout, A/B, kill switch, ops toggles. Flag ka lifecycle: create → rollout → cleanup.

Confidentiality, integrity, availability — the three pillars every security control maps back to. Includes defense in depth, least privilege, and fail secure. Explain the CIA triad. How does each principle apply to a real-world system you have designed? Confidentiality Sirf authorized log data dekh sakein (encryption, access control). Integrity Data unauthorized change na ho (hash, signature, checksums). Availability Service jab chahiye tab chale (redundancy, DDoS protection). Definition: CIA triad security ke teen stambh hain. Har control inme se kisi ek ko protect karta hai. Saath mein: defense in depth (kai layers), least privilege (minimum access), fail secure (fail ho to deny).

Authentication verifies identity ("who you are"). Authorization determines access ("what you can do"). Factors: something you know, have, are. Common failure: checking AuthN but forgetting AuthZ. What is the difference between authentication and authorization? Why do engineers confuse them? Authentication (AuthN) Tum kaun ho — identity verify. Authorization (AuthZ) Tum kya kar sakte ho — permissions. 401 vs 403 401 = identity nahi pata; 403 = pata hai par allowed nahi. Definition: AuthN pehle (password, MFA, token), AuthZ uske baad har request par (RBAC, ABAC, ownership check). Dono alag layers par implement hote hain.

Symmetric (AES-256-GCM), asymmetric (ECDSA, Ed25519), hashing (SHA-256, bcrypt), and digital signatures. AEAD encrypts and verifies integrity together. Compare symmetric and asymmetric cryptography. When would you use AES-256-GCM vs RSA? Symmetric Ek hi key: AES-256-GCM (fast, bulk data). Asymmetric Public/private key: RSA, ECDSA, Ed25519. Hash vs encrypt Hash one-way; encryption reversible. Definition: Symmetric data encrypt karta hai; asymmetric key exchange aur signatures ke liye; hash integrity ke liye. Passwords ke liye slow hash (bcrypt/argon2) aur salt, SHA-256 nahi.

Hierarchy of Certificate Authorities (CAs) that trust each other up to a root CA. TLS certificate chain validation, CRL, OCSP, Let's Encrypt, and Certificate Transparency. Explain how the TLS certificate chain works. What happens when a certificate is revoked? CA Trusted authority jo certificate sign karti hai. Chain of trust Leaf → intermediate → root. Revocation CRL / OCSP se cert cancel. Definition: PKI mein browser root CAs par trust karta hai; server leaf cert + intermediates bhejta hai. Cert mein domain, public key, expiry aur CA ka signature hota hai.

STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Info disclosure, DoS, Elevation of privilege) maps threats to components. Attack trees model multi-step paths. Risk = likelihood × impact. How do you perform threat modeling on a new system? Walk through the STRIDE framework. STRIDE Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Info disclosure, DoS, Elevation. Trust boundary Jahan data ek trust level se dusre mein jaata hai. DFD Data flow diagram — threat model ka base. Definition: Threat modeling design stage par poochta hai: Hum kya bana rahe hain? Kya galat ho sakta hai? Kya karenge? Kya hum ne sahi kiya? DFD banao, trust boundaries mark karo, har element par STRIDE lagao.

The most critical web application security risks: Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, Insecure Design, Security Misconfiguration, and more. Name the current OWASP Top 10. Which three are most common in modern web applications? Broken Access Control #1 — authZ checks missing. Injection SQL/NoSQL/OS command. Security misconfiguration Default creds, debug on. Definition: OWASP Top 10 web apps ke sabse common risks ki list hai (Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, Insecure Design, Misconfiguration, Vulnerable Components, Auth Failures, Integrity Failures, Logging Failures, SSRF).

Stored XSS (saved on server), Reflected (in URL), DOM-based (client-side). CSP (Content Security Policy) prevents all three. Output encoding must be context-aware. Explain the three types of XSS. How does Content Security Policy prevent each? Stored XSS Payload DB mein save, sabko trigger. Reflected XSS URL parameter turant page mein. CSP Browser ko batata hai kaun si scripts allowed. Definition: XSS mein attacker ki JS victim ke browser mein tumhari site ke origin par chalti hai — cookies/tokens chura sakti hai. Fix: output encoding, framework auto-escape, CSP, HttpOnly cookies.

CSRF tricks a victim into performing actions on another site. Anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookie attribute (Lax, Strict, None) provide browser-level protection. How does a CSRF attack work? What defenses would you implement in a modern web app? CSRF Victim ke browser se authenticated request attacker trigger kare. SameSite Cookie cross-site requests mein nahi jaati (Lax/Strict). CSRF token Unpredictable per-session token. Definition: Browser cookies automatically bhejta hai, isliye evil.com se bank.com par POST ho sakta hai. Defense: SameSite=Lax/Strict, anti-CSRF tokens, Origin/Referer check, custom header for APIs.

SQLi injects malicious SQL through input fields — UNION-based, error-based, blind. NoSQLi targets MongoDB/Couchbase with $where and $regex. Parameterized queries are the fix. Explain blind SQL injection. How do you detect and prevent it? SQLi Input se query ka structure badal jaye. Parameterized query Data aur code alag. NoSQLi {"$ne": null} jaise operators inject. Definition: String concat se query banane par attacker ' OR 1=1 -- daal ke logic badal sakta hai. Fix: prepared statements/ORM parameters, least-privilege DB user, input validation.

SSRF makes the server fetch internal resources (cloud metadata endpoints). IDOR lets attackers access resources by changing IDs. Both require server-side validation and authorization checks. How would you exploit SSRF to steal AWS IAM credentials? How do you defend against it? SSRF Server ko attacker ke diye URL par request karwana. Metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254 — cloud credentials. IDOR ID badal ke dusre ka data. Definition: SSRF mein server internal services/metadata (AWS IMDS) tak request bhej deta hai. Fix: URL allowlist, private IP block, IMDSv2, egress filtering. IDOR: ownership check missing.

n: XXE — XML External Entity injection, XXE mitigation
x: XXE attacks exploit XML parsers that process external entities. Attacker injects XML entities to read local files, SSRF, or cause DoS. Mitigation: disable DTD processing, disable external entities. JSON APIs are not vulnerable. Only affects XML-based systems (SOAP, SAML, SVG, DOCX). What is XXE and which systems are vulnerable? How do you prevent it? External entity XML mein <!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd"> . DTD Document Type Definition jisme entities define hoti hain. Mitigation Parser mein DTD/external entities disable. Definition: XXE tab hota hai jab XML parser external entities resolve karta hai. Attacker local files padh sakta hai, SSRF kar sakta hai ya DoS (billion laugh

n: SSTI — Server-Side Template Injection, auto-escaping, sandboxing
x: SSTI occurs when user input is embedded in a template without escaping. Attacker injects template syntax to execute code server-side. Jinja2, Twig, Handlebars, FreeMarker all vulnerable. Mitigation: auto-escaping, sandbox mode, never render user input directly. What is SSTI and how do you detect it? What is the impact of SSTI in Jinja2? Template injection User input template code ban jaye. Auto-escape Output HTML-encode. Sandbox Template engine ko restricted environment. Definition: Agar user input ko template string mein concatenate karke render karo ( render_template_string("Hello " + name) ), attacker {{7*7}} bhej ke code execution tak ja sakta hai.

n: Directory Traversal — path traversal, null bytes, URL encoding
x: Directory traversal uses ../ sequences to access files outside the web root. Bypasses: URL encoding (%2e%2e%2f), null bytes (%00), double encoding. Mitigation: validate paths against whitelist, use chroot/jail, never use user input in file paths directly. What is directory traversal and what are common bypass techniques? ../ Parent directory sequence. Encoding bypass %2e%2e%2f, double encoding, null byte. Canonicalize Path resolve karke base ke andar check. Definition: /download?file=../../etc/passwd se attacker web root ke bahar ki files padh leta hai. Fix: filename ko ID se map karo, ya resolve karke base directory prefix verify karo.

n: Open Redirect — parameter manipulation, SSO bypass, phishing
x: Open redirect: application redirects user to attacker-controlled URL via manipulated parameter. Used in phishing (legitimate domain → malicious site), OAuth/SSO bypass, token theft. Mitigation: validate redirect URLs against whitelist, use callback URLs. What is an open redirect vulnerability? How is it used in phishing attacks? Open redirect ?next=https://evil.com par redirect. Phishing Trusted domain ka link, evil destination. Allowlist Sirf known paths/hosts. Definition: Login ke baad ?returnTo= par blindly redirect karna attacker ko trusted domain se phishing link banane deta hai, aur OAuth/SSO flows mein token leak ka raasta.

n: Insecure Deserialization — object injection, remote code execution
x: Insecure deserialization: untrusted data is deserialized into objects without validation. Can lead to remote code execution (Java RCE, PHP object injection). Mitigation: avoid deserializing untrusted data, use signed/encrypted serialization, integrity checks. What is insecure deserialization and how does it lead to RCE? Deserialization Bytes → object. Gadget chain Existing classes ko jod ke code execution. Safe format JSON + schema validation. Definition: Untrusted data ko native deserializer (Java ObjectInputStream, Python pickle, PHP unserialize) se load karna attacker ko object banane/methods chalane deta hai — aksar RCE.

n: Clickjacking — UI redressing, X-Frame-Options, CSP frame-ancestors
x: Clickjacking: attacker iframes victim site transparently, tricks user into clicking. Mitigation: X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN. CSP frame-ancestors directive (preferred). Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'. JavaScript frame-busting is bypassable. What is clickjacking and how do you prevent it? UI redressing Invisible iframe par click karwana. X-Frame-Options DENY / SAMEORIGIN. frame-ancestors CSP ka modern replacement. Definition: Attacker tumhari site ko transparent iframe mein load karke apne page ke button ke upar rakh deta hai; user 'free gift' click karta hai par asal mein 'delete account' dabata hai.

Sessions: server stores state, client gets cookie. Tokens (JWT): client stores claims, server validates signature. Access tokens (short-lived) vs refresh tokens (long-lived, rotated). Compare session-based and token-based authentication. What are the trade-offs for scalability and security? Session Server state + cookie mein session ID. Stateless token JWT: claims client ke paas. Revocation Session aasaan; JWT mushkil. Definition: Sessions server-side store (Redis) mein state rakhte hain, logout/revoke turant. JWT stateless hai, scale easy par revoke mushkil — short expiry + refresh token chahiye.

Three base64url segments: header, payload, signature. Common attacks: alg=none, algorithm confusion, weak HMAC secret. Always validate signature, expiry, issuer, and audience. Explain the alg=none attack on JWTs. How do you prevent algorithm confusion attacks? alg=none Signature skip attack. Algorithm confusion RS256 public key ko HS256 secret banana. exp / aud / iss Claims jo verify karne chahiye. Definition: JWT = header.payload.signature (base64url). Payload encrypted nahi, sirf signed hai. Verify karte waqt algorithm pin karo aur exp, iss, aud check karo.

OAuth 2.0: delegated authorization via access tokens. Authorization Code Flow with PKCE prevents interception. OIDC adds id_token (JWT) for authentication on top of OAuth. Walk through the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. Why is PKCE necessary? OAuth 2.0 Delegated authorization (access token). OIDC OAuth ke upar authentication (ID token). PKCE Authorization code interception se bachata hai. Definition: Authorization Code + PKCE flow: app user ko IdP par bhejti hai → code milta hai → backend/SPA code+verifier se token leta hai. OAuth authZ hai; login ke liye OIDC ID token.

XML-based SSO protocol. IdP authenticates user and sends signed SAML assertion to SP. Used by Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin. Vulnerable to XML signature wrapping and response replay. How does SP-initiated SAML SSO work? What are the security risks in SAML assertions? IdP Identity Provider (Okta, Azure AD). SP Service Provider (tumhari app). Assertion Signed XML jisme user identity hai. Definition: SAML enterprise SSO: user SP se IdP par redirect, login, IdP signed assertion bhejta hai, SP signature verify karke session banata hai.

WebAuthn/FIDO2: browser-based public key auth, no shared secret. Passkeys sync across devices via iCloud/Google. TOTP: time-based 6-digit codes. Phishing-resistant > phishable. How does WebAuthn work at a technical level? Why are passkeys considered the future of authentication? WebAuthn/FIDO2 Public-key auth browser/OS authenticator se. Passkey Synced WebAuthn credential. MFA Kuch jaante ho + kuch ho + kuch ho. Definition: WebAuthn mein private key device par rehti hai, server sirf public key rakhta hai — phishing-resistant kyunki credential origin se bound hai. TOTP/SMS kamzor, push fatigue ka risk.

SDL integrates security into every phase: design (threat model) → code (SAST) → test (DAST) → deploy (scan) → operate (monitor). A bug in design costs $100; in production, $100K+. How do you integrate security into a CI/CD pipeline? What tools do you use at each stage? Shift left Security ko early phases mein laana. SAST / DAST / SCA Code scan / running app scan / dependency scan. Security champion Team ka security point person. Definition: SDL: requirements → threat model → secure coding + SAST → DAST/pen-test → release gate → monitoring. CI mein automated checks.

Never store secrets in code, config files, or cleartext env vars. Use HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager for storage, rotation, and just-in-time access with automatic expiry. How do you manage database credentials and API keys in a microservices architecture? Vault / Secrets Manager Central encrypted secrets store. Rotation Secrets regularly badlo. Dynamic secrets Short-lived DB creds on demand. Definition: Code/git/Docker image mein secrets nahi. Runtime par vault se inject, IAM role se access, rotate, audit. Leak hone par turant revoke.

Scan images for CVEs (Trivy, Grype), run as non-root, use minimal base images (distroless). K8s: Pod Security Standards, Network Policies, OPA Gatekeeper policies. How do you secure a Kubernetes cluster from image build to runtime? Non-root Container user non-privileged. Distroless Minimal image, kam attack surface. Image scan Trivy/Grype CVE scan. Definition: Minimal base image, non-root user, read-only filesystem, capabilities drop, no privileged containers, signed images aur registry scanning.

Authenticate every request, authorize every operation, validate every input, rate limit per client. CORS restricts cross-origin access. APIs are the #1 modern attack vector. How would you secure a public REST API serving millions of requests per day? Rate limiting Request caps. Input validation Schema se strict check. Least data Response mein sirf zaroori fields. Definition: Har request authN, har operation authZ, input schema validation, rate limit, TLS, proper error messages (no stack traces), logging.

SCA scans dependencies for CVEs. SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX) inventories all components. Artifact signing (cosign) and SLSA levels secure the build pipeline against attacks like SolarWinds. How do you protect against supply chain attacks in your software development process? SCA Software Composition Analysis. SBOM Components ki list (CycloneDX/SPDX). Lockfile Exact versions pin. Definition: Dependencies mein CVEs, typosquatting, malicious updates. Defense: lockfiles, SCA, SBOM, signed artifacts (Sigstore), minimal deps, private registry.

IAM manages identities and permissions. Service accounts for machines. Policy conditions restrict by IP, time, MFA. Start minimal, add only what is needed. Never use wildcard actions. How do you design IAM policies for a multi-service cloud application? Least privilege Minimum permissions. Role vs user Services roles use karein, long-lived keys nahi. Condition IP/MFA/time based policy. Definition: IAM identities (users, roles, service accounts) ko policies deti hai. Wildcard * avoid karo, roles assume karo, MFA, permission boundaries, access review.

VPC isolates networks with public/private subnets across AZs. Security Groups (stateful), NACLs (stateless), WAF (L7 SQLi/XSS), and Shield/CloudFront for DDoS protection. Design a VPC architecture for a three-tier web application. What security controls apply at each layer? VPC/subnets Private/public network split. Security Group Stateful instance firewall. NACL Stateless subnet filter. Definition: DBs private subnet mein, sirf LB public. SG least-open, NAT egress, VPC endpoints, WAF, flow logs.

Encryption at rest (AES-256 on S3, RDS, EBS) and in transit (TLS 1.3). KMS manages keys with automatic rotation. Envelope encryption: KMS encrypts DEK, DEK encrypts data. How do you implement encryption at rest and in transit for a cloud-native application? At rest Disk/DB encryption. In transit TLS 1.2+/1.3. KMS Key management service, rotation, audit. Definition: Data classification, encryption at rest (KMS keys) aur in transit, backups encrypted, tokenization PII, retention policies.

SOC2 (5 trust criteria), HIPAA (PHI protection), GDPR (EU data rights), PCI DSS (card data). Audit logging (CloudTrail), automated evidence collection (Vanta, Drata). How do you design a system that is compliant by default for SOC2 and GDPR? SOC2 Trust criteria audit. GDPR EU data rights. PCI DSS Card data standard. Definition: Compliance frameworks controls aur evidence maangte hain: access reviews, logging, change management, incident response, data retention, right to erasure (GDPR).

IR phases: Preparation → Detection → Containment → Eradication → Recovery → Postmortem. Runbooks define steps per scenario. Blameless postmortems focus on process failures, not people. Walk through your incident response process for a suspected data breach in a cloud environment. IR phases Prepare, Detect, Contain, Eradicate, Recover, Lessons. Runbook Step-by-step playbook. Blameless postmortem System fix, blame nahi. Definition: Detect → triage severity → contain (isolate, revoke creds) → eradicate (root cause) → recover → postmortem. Evidence preserve karo, communication plan rakho.

"Never trust, always verify" — no implicit trust based on network location. Micro-segmentation per service. Continuous verification on every sensitive operation. Google BeyondCorp pioneered this. How would you implement Zero Trust architecture in an existing cloud application? Never trust, always verify Network location se trust nahi. Micro-segmentation Chhote isolated zones. Continuous verification Identity + device posture har request. Definition: Perimeter model toot gaya (remote work, cloud). Zero trust mein har request authenticate+authorize, mTLS, device health, least privilege.

Security is part of every component decision, not bolted on. Patterns: least privilege, defense in depth, fail secure, secure defaults, complete mediation, economy of mechanism. What does "Secure by Design" mean in practice? Give examples of each principle in a real system. Secure by default Safe configuration out of box. Defense in depth Multiple layers. Fail secure Error par deny. Definition: Security architecture ka hissa: minimize attack surface, least privilege, separation of duties, safe defaults, input validation boundary par.

TLS 1.3: 1-RTT handshake, 3 cipher suites only. AEAD (AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305). ECDHE for perfect forward secrecy. X25519 preferred over P-256 for key exchange. Explain the TLS 1.3 handshake. How does it improve security and performance over TLS 1.2? TLS 1.3 1-RTT handshake, forward secrecy. AEAD Encryption + integrity (GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305). HSTS HTTPS force karne ka header. Definition: TLS 1.3 sirf strong cipher suites rakhta hai, ECDHE se forward secrecy. Practical: HSTS, cert automation, mTLS internal, disable TLS 1.0/1.1.

SIEM aggregates logs from all sources, normalizes, correlates, and alerts. SOAR automates incident response. Detection engineering writes rules as code. Median dwell time without SIEM: 204 days. How do you design a security monitoring strategy for a cloud-native application? SIEM Logs aggregate, correlate, alert. SOAR Response automation. Detection rule Suspicious pattern ka alert. Definition: Auth logs, CloudTrail, app logs ek jagah; rules (impossible travel, many failed logins, new admin) alert deti hain; triage aur runbooks.

BOLA (formerly IDOR) is the #1 API vulnerability. Attacker accesses objects by manipulating IDs in API calls (e.g., /api/users/123 → /api/users/456). Server doesn't verify ownership. Most common in REST APIs. What is BOLA? How do you prevent it in a multi-tenant API? BOLA Object id badal ke dusre ka object. Ownership check Har object access par. Unpredictable IDs UUID helps par fix nahi. Definition: GET /orders/123 ko 124 karke dusre user ka order mil jaye to BOLA. Fix: har object access par user-ownership/policy check.

n: Broken Authentication — credential stuffing, session fixation, weak JWT
x: Broken Authentication encompasses weak passwords, no rate limiting on login, credential stuffing, session fixation, and weak JWT implementation (alg:none, no expiry, weak secret). How do you prevent credential stuffing attacks on a login API? What makes a JWT implementation insecure? Credential stuffing Leaked passwords ko replay. Session fixation Attacker ki session ID victim par. Rate limit login Per IP + per account. Definition: Weak passwords, no throttling, predictable tokens, long-lived JWT, no MFA. Fix: MFA, breached-password check, lockout/backoff, rotate session ID after login.

n: Broken Object Property Level Authorization — mass assignment, excessive data exposure
x: Mass assignment: API accepts all fields from request body, allowing attackers to set unintended properties (e.g., isAdmin: true). Excessive data exposure: API returns more fields than the client needs. What is mass assignment? How do you prevent it in a REST API? Mass assignment Request body ke saare fields model mein. Excessive data exposure Response mein zyada fields. DTO Allowlisted fields. Definition: User.update(req.body) se attacker isAdmin:true bhej sakta hai. Response mein password hash/internal fields chale jaate hain.

n: Unrestricted Resource Consumption — rate limiting, pagination, resource limits
x: APIs without rate limiting are vulnerable to DoS. Lack of pagination allows fetching millions of records. No file size limits enable storage abuse. No query complexity limits enable GraphQL abuse. How do you implement rate limiting for a public API? What are the tradeoffs between different rate limiting algorithms? Rate limit Time window mein max requests. Pagination limit Max page size. Cost control Timeouts, payload limits, query depth. Definition: APIs bina limits ke DoS aur bill-shock ka shikaar hote hain: huge page size, expensive queries, large uploads, SMS/email spam.

n: Broken Function Level Authorization — admin endpoints, vertical privilege escalation
x: Regular users accessing admin functions by calling admin API endpoints directly. Missing authorization checks on function-level operations. Vertical privilege escalation: low-privilege user gains admin access. How do you prevent regular users from accessing admin API endpoints? What is vertical vs horizontal privilege escalation? BFLA Function-level authZ missing. Vertical escalation User → admin functions. Deny by default Role check har function par. Definition: Normal user /api/admin/users ya DELETE method call kar leta hai kyunki sirf UI chhupaya gaya tha. Fix: server-side role/permission check central middleware mein.

Raw socket(), bind(), listen(), accept() loop — handle multiple concurrent clients without a framework. Covers TCP handshake, partial reads, goroutine-per-connection, graceful shutdown. Design a TCP echo server from raw POSIX sockets. Walk me through bind, listen, accept — and how you would handle 1000 concurrent clients without a framework.

Build HTTP/1.1 on raw TCP. Parse request line, headers, body via Content-Length. Route paths, serve responses, support keep-alive — zero stdlib http. Build an HTTP/1.1 server on raw TCP sockets. How do you parse the request line, headers, and body? What does keep-alive actually do at the wire level?

Recursive DNS resolver: parse DNS packets, walk the hierarchy from root to authoritative, cache by TTL — raw UDP sockets and binary parsing. Explain how a recursive DNS resolver walks from root servers down to authoritative answers. What does the DNS wire format look like?

Single-threaded event loop using epoll/kqueue for I/O multiplexing. Timer min-heap for setTimeout semantics. Handle 1000 concurrent connections in one thread. How does epoll work under the hood? Explain the difference between edge-triggered and level-triggered I/O notification.

on/emit/once/off, error event propagation, setMaxListeners, memory leak detection at 10+ listeners. The observer pattern backbone. Build Node.js EventEmitter from scratch. How does once() auto-remove listeners, and why is the error event special?

require() from scratch: resolution, __dirname, module.exports, caching, circular dependency handling with partial exports. Rebuild Node.js require(). How does module resolution work, and how does caching prevent redundant loads?

n: In-Memory KV Store with File Persistence
x: In-memory hash map + LRU eviction + append-only WAL for crash recovery. GET, SET, DEL, EXPIRE commands. Redis lite without the protocol. Design an in-memory key-value store with WAL for crash recovery. What does the write-ahead log look like, and how do you replay it?

Pool of persistent TCP connections with borrow/return, health check, idle timeout, overflow strategy. Amortize handshake + TLS + auth cost. Build a TCP connection pool. How do you handle borrow and return semantics, idle timeout, and health checks before lending?

HTTP upgrade handshake, WebSocket frame protocol, masking, fragmentation, ping/pong keepalive. Pub/sub broadcast across concurrent connections. Walk me through the WebSocket upgrade handshake. How do you compute the Sec-WebSocket-Accept key from the client challenge?

Signal handling (SIGTERM/SIGINT), connection drain with timeout, health check flip 200→503, worker drain, force-kill fallback. Design production-grade graceful shutdown. How do you drain in-flight requests without dropping connections?

The foundation of Node.js — build a server using only the http module. Build an HTTP server using only Node's built-in http module — GET /hello, POST /echo, 404 handling, JSON responses. Walk me through how you parse the request body from the incoming stream.

Build a command-line tool using fs and process — tests Node fundamentals. Build a CLI tool that takes a file path and prints line count, word count, character count, and the top 5 most frequent words. How do you handle a missing or unreadable file?

A building block used in every Node.js service — caching with expiry. Design an in-memory TTL cache with set/get/delete/clear and stats. Values expire after ttlMs — explain lazy expiry vs active expiry and when you would choose each.

n: Build a Logger with Log Levels
x: Every Node.js app needs a logger — build one that writes to console and file. Build a Logger class with debug/info/warn/error levels, colored console output, and newline-delimited JSON written to a file. How do you make the minimum level configurable at runtime?

Stream-friendly CSV parsing — tests string parsing and edge case handling. Build parseCSV(text) and toCSV(records) that handle quoted fields, commas and newlines inside quotes, and escaped quotes. What is the naive approach and why does it fail?

Configuration management is a real production concern. Build it properly. Build loadConfig() merging defaults → JSON file → env vars → runtime overrides, with nested keys (DB_HOST → config.db.host), type coercion, and required-field validation.

Build your own find command — tests async file system operations. Build walk(dir, options) as an async generator that lazily yields file paths, with extension filters, maxDepth, and ignore patterns. How do you avoid infinite loops with symlinks?

Real-time data push without WebSockets — the simplest live-update mechanism. Build an SSE endpoint at GET /events that pushes a counter every second, detects client disconnects, and supports Last-Event-ID resume. What headers and wire format are required?

RESP wire protocol, core commands (GET/SET/DEL/TTL/INCR/LPUSH), pub/sub fan-out, AOF + RDB persistence. redis-cli should connect and work. Build a Redis-compatible server. How does the RESP wire protocol work, and how do you implement TTL with lazy expiry plus background sweep?

Durable queue with producer/consumer, ack/nack, redelivery timer, dead-letter queue. At-least-once delivery via WAL + visibility timeout. Design a message queue with at-least-once delivery. How does visibility timeout prevent duplicate processing?

Reverse proxy distributing traffic across backends. Round-robin + least-connections, active/passive health checks, connection draining, sticky sessions. Build an HTTP load balancer. Compare round-robin and least-connections algorithms. How do health checks work?

Standalone rate limiter: token bucket + sliding window + fixed window counter. Redis + Lua for atomic distributed counting. Rate limit headers. Design a distributed rate limiter. Compare token bucket, sliding window, and fixed window counter algorithms.

Consistent hash ring with virtual nodes, LRU eviction per node, cache-aside + write-through patterns. Client routes without central coordinator. Design a distributed cache with consistent hashing. How do virtual nodes improve key distribution across nodes?

Cron expression parser, min-heap job queue, distributed lock (SETNX) for exactly-once execution, retry with exponential backoff. Build a distributed cron scheduler. How do you parse cron expressions and compute the next run time?

Protobuf-style wire format with varint + TLV encoding, TCP framing, unary + server-streaming, client stub generation from IDL. Design a minimal RPC framework. How does varint encoding work, and why is length-prefix framing necessary over TCP?

HTTP API for PUT/GET/DELETE objects, bucket management, chunked upload, range requests (206), ETag validation, metadata index. Build an object storage service. How does chunked upload work, and why are range requests important for large objects?

n: URL Shortener — Base62 encoding, collision handling, analytics
x: Generate unique short codes using Base62 (a-z, A-Z, 0-9). Store mapping in DB (short_code → long_url). Handle collisions with retry. Add click analytics (IP, user-agent, timestamp). Use cache (Redis) for hot URLs. 301 vs 302 redirect. How do you generate unique short codes for a URL shortener? How do you handle collisions?

Understand how Express works by building it — middleware chain, params, error handling. Build an Express-like framework: route registration with params (:id), middleware via app.use, next()/next(err), and a 4-argument error handler. How do you convert /users/:id into a matcher?

The backbone of background processing — build a production-grade job queue. Design a JobQueue with configurable concurrency, retry with exponential backoff, status tracking, and lifecycle events. How does a job move through pending → active → completed/failed?

Every production API has one — implement sliding window and token bucket. Build Express rate-limiting middleware with fixed-window and sliding-window strategies, 429 responses with Retry-After, and rate-limit headers. How do you key by client?

Node.js streams are heavily tested at senior level — build a real transform pipeline. Build a streaming file processing pipeline: read a large CSV as a stream, parse, transform, filter, batch into groups of 100, and write JSONL — without loading the file into memory.

Resource management pattern used in every production Node.js service. Design a database ConnectionPool with acquire/release, min/max size, acquire timeout, idle timeout, and health checks. What happens when acquire exceeds max?

Build your own prompting library — tests raw TTY control and keyboard events. Build a prompting library: text, password (masked), select via arrow keys, confirm, and checkbox — using raw-mode stdin. How do you detect arrow key presses?

Build your own chokidar-lite — recursive watching, change types, debouncing. Build watch(dir, options) emitting add/change/delete events with debounce, recursion, ignore patterns, and an initial scan. How do you distinguish add from change?

Implement the WebSocket upgrade handshake and basic framing from scratch. Implement a raw WebSocket server: the HTTP upgrade handshake, Sec-WebSocket-Accept computation, and frame parsing/construction for text messages. Walk me through the accept-key computation.

Redis-lite - a data store with append-only-file durability. Design a KV store with AOF persistence: every mutation appends to a log, replay on restart, SAVE snapshots, TTL support, and keys() wildcard matching.

Product companies run webhook infrastructure - retries, idempotency keys, and a delivery log. Design a WebhookDispatcher with HMAC-signed delivery, per-attempt timeouts, exponential backoff retries, auto-disabling flaky endpoints, and a delivery log with replay.

Payments-grade APIs need idempotency - dedupe retried POSTs by key. Build Express idempotency middleware: a client sends Idempotency-Key, duplicate keys return the stored response instead of re-executing, with a TTL and locking for concurrent duplicates.

Rebuild libuv phases: timers → pending → poll → check → close. Microtask queue, nextTick priority, I/O starvation guard. Rebuild the Node.js event loop phases. How do timers, I/O poll, setImmediate, and close callbacks interact?

Readable/Writable/Duplex/Transform with backpressure, highWaterMark, pipe(). Flowing vs paused mode, drain events. Build Node.js streams from scratch. What is backpressure, and how does highWaterMark control data flow?

Master forks workers, round-robin accept, IPC handle passing, worker health heartbeat, zero-downtime restart via SIGUSR2. Rebuild Node.js cluster from scratch. How does round-robin accept distribute connections across workers?

Generic worker thread pool: task queue, thread lifecycle, SharedArrayBuffer for zero-copy, structured clone messaging, crash respawn. Design a worker thread pool. How does SharedArrayBuffer enable zero-copy data sharing between threads?

n: Chat System — WebSocket, message persistence, presence, delivery receipts
x: WebSocket for real-time messaging. Store messages in DB (PostgreSQL/MongoDB) with conversation_id, sender_id, content, timestamp. Presence service tracks online/offline status. Delivery receipts: sent → delivered → read. Message ordering with sequence numbers. How do you design a chat system backend? How do you ensure message ordering and delivery?

n: Notification System — fanout, multi-channel delivery, preferences
x: Notification service with channels: email (SES/SendGrid), push (FCM/APNs), SMS (Twilio), in-app. User preferences per notification type. Fanout: single event → multiple channel delivery. Queue-based async processing. Delivery status tracking. How do you design a notification system that supports multiple channels (email, push, SMS)?

n: REST API with Auth, CRUD & Validation
x: Build a full production-style API — the most common Node.js senior round problem. Build a Notes REST API: JWT register/login, protected CRUD with ownership checks, request validation, and centralized error handling. How do you implement a JWT by hand?

Offload heavy computation — tests your understanding of Node.js concurrency model. Build a worker-thread pool that distributes CPU-bound tasks, handles worker crashes with requeue, supports cancellation, and reports progress. How does the main thread communicate with workers?

Build the core of a message broker — think mini-Redis pub/sub over TCP. Build a pub/sub server over TCP: SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH/UNSUBSCRIBE with wildcard channels and per-channel message history. How do you route a publish to matching subscribers?

Combine everything: LRU eviction, TTL expiry, pub/sub invalidation, and HTTP API. Design a CacheServer with an HTTP API combining LRU eviction and TTL expiry, an SSE endpoint for invalidation events, and a stats endpoint. How do LRU and TTL coexist?

Build your own node-cron — parsing cron expressions and scheduling callbacks. Build a cron-style Scheduler parsing expressions like */5 * * * * with ranges and lists, one-time tasks, cancellation, missed-run recovery, and a timezone option.

Parse multi-GB JSON files without loading into memory — a real data engineering problem. Build a streaming JSON parser as a Transform stream: JSONL lines or a streaming array, transform/filter each item, respect backpressure, and recover from malformed lines.

Cache stampede prevention, leader election, mutual exclusion - the lock everyone uses. Design a DistributedLock with SET NX PX semantics, ownership tokens, compare-and-delete release, lease auto-renewal, and retry with backoff.

n: Worker Threads & Clustering — CPU-bound tasks in Node.js
x: Worker Threads run JavaScript in parallel threads with shared memory. Cluster module forks Node.js processes across CPU cores. Explain and build Node.js Worker Threads vs the cluster module: shared memory vs process forking, offloading CPU-bound work, and scaling HTTP servers across cores. When would you use each?

n: Caching Layer — Redis, cache-aside, cache invalidation strategies
x: Redis caching layer for database query results, session data, and frequently accessed data. Design a caching layer: cache-aside vs write-through, TTL and event-driven invalidation, cache stampede prevention with a distributed lock, and the Redis data structures you would use.

Request-scoped state that survives async chains — request IDs, correlation IDs, tenant context. Build a request-context helper using AsyncLocalStorage: assign a requestId (and optional userId/tenantId) per request, propagate it through every async call, and expose get()/set() helpers that any layer can read without passing arguments. How do you wire it into an Express-style middleware?

CLOSED → OPEN → HALF-OPEN state machine so a dead dependency fails fast instead of hanging requests. Build a CircuitBreaker that wraps an async function: calls pass while CLOSED, failures increment a counter that trips the breaker OPEN after a threshold, OPEN fails fast (or returns a fallback), HALF-OPEN after a cooldown allows limited probe calls and closes on success. Emit state-change events.

Publish events reliably by writing to an outbox table in the same transaction as the business change. Build the transactional outbox pattern: in one DB transaction, apply a business change AND insert a row into an outbox table; a relay polls committed outbox rows, publishes each to a queue (or HTTP endpoint), marks it sent, dedupes re-reads, and handles poison rows. Why is this more reliable than queueing inside the transaction?

Prometheus-style counters, gauges, and histograms with a scrape endpoint — the observability staple. Build a small metrics library: counters (monotonic), gauges (settable), histograms (buckets + sum + count), named with labels, exposed at GET /metrics in Prometheus text format, plus default process metrics (event-loop lag, memory, uptime) and per-route HTTP counters/latency.

MemTable (skip list) → SSTable flush, Bloom filter per SSTable, leveled compaction. The write path inside RocksDB and Cassandra. Explain the LSM-tree architecture. How does the write path flow from MemTable to SSTable flush to disk?

B+ tree page layout, WAL for ACID transactions, SQL lexer/parser/executor. File-backed relational DB with CREATE TABLE, INSERT, SELECT. Design a file-backed relational database. How does B+ tree page layout work, and why are leaf nodes linked together?

Content-addressable object store, blob/tree/commit objects, pack files, three-way merge algorithm. Binary-compatible with real Git. How does Git content-addressable object store work? What makes the Merkle DAG tamper-evident?

Lexer → recursive descent parser → AST → bytecode compiler → stack-based VM. Closures, mark-and-sweep GC, basic I/O. Build a programming language interpreter. Walk through the pipeline: lexer, parser, bytecode compiler, and VM execution.

Leader election with randomized timeouts, log replication via AppendEntries, commit quorum, log compaction via snapshotting. Explain the Raft consensus algorithm. How does leader election work, and what safety guarantees does it provide?

Linux namespaces (PID/NET/MNT/UTS/IPC), cgroups v2 resource limits, OverlayFS layers, OCI-compatible create→start→kill→delete. Build a minimal container runtime. What do Linux namespaces isolate, and how do cgroups enforce resource limits?

page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx, error.tsx, not-found.tsx — what each file does and when it renders Route URL ka pattern jo batata hai kaunsa page khulega — /about , /blog/meri-post . App Router app/ folder ke folders hi routes ban jaate hain — alag se routing config nahi likhna padta. page.tsx Us URL par kya DIKHEGA — bina is file ke folder route nahi banta. Next.js mein routing folders se banti hai . app/users/page.tsx likha to /users URL apne aap ban gaya. Koi route config nahi, koi react-router nahi — folder ka naam hi URL hai .

Persistent layouts vs. re-mounting templates. Root layout, nested layouts, layout composition Layout Aas-paas ka dancha jo navigation par wahi rehta hai — state preserve hoti hai, re-render nahi hota. Template Layout jaisa hi, par har navigation par naya mount hota hai — purani state mit jaati hai. Root layout app/layout.tsx — zaroori hai, isi mein <html> aur <body> tags likhe jaate hain. layout.tsx apne saare child pages ko wrap karta hai aur navigation ke dauran zinda rehta hai — sidebar wapas render nahi hota, uski state bani rehti hai. template.tsx bilkul same kaam karta hai, bas har navigation par naya instance banta hai.

[slug], [...slug], [[...slug]] — catch-all, optional catch-all, generateStaticParams for SSG [slug] Dynamic segment — URL ka wo hissa jo badal sakta hai. Catch-all [...slug] Ek se zyada segments pakadta hai — /docs/a/b/c . generateStaticParams Build time par batata hai kaunse slug pages pehle se ban jaayein (SSG). [slug] folder ka naam URL mein kisi bhi value se replace ho jaata hai. app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx — /blog/react , /blog/css dono isi se chalte hain. Page ko wo value params prop mein milti hai.

Streaming with loading.tsx, error.tsx boundaries, global-error.tsx, reset() function loading.tsx Us route ke data aate tak ka turant fallback — Suspense boundary apne aap ban jaata hai. error.tsx Render fail hone par ka fallback — ErrorBoundary + reset() retry button. not-found.tsx notFound() call hone par ya galat URL par ka 404 UI. Ye teeno special files route ke error/loading states sambhalti hain — bina ek line state management ke. loading.tsx daala to data aate tak wahan skeleton dikhta hai; error.tsx daala to crash hone par graceful message + retry.

Static metadata export, generateMetadata(), Open Graph, Twitter cards, robots, sitemap, viewport Metadata Page ke <head> mein jaane wali info — title, description, OG image. generateMetadata() Dynamic metadata — URL/data ke hisaab se har page ka apna title. OG image WhatsApp/Twitter par link share hone par dikhne wali preview card. Next.js mein SEO tags likhne ke liye bas ek metadata object export kar do — framework use <head> mein daal deta hai. Dynamic pages ke liye generateMetadata() function — jo bhi data fetch karke uske hisaab se title/description lauta do.

(group) syntax for organisation, @slot for parallel routes, conditional slot rendering Route group (name) Parentheses wala folder — organization ke liye, URL mein nahi aata . Parallel route @slot Ek layout mein do-do pages saath render — named slots. default.tsx Slot ka fallback — jab refresh ke baad slot match na ho. (marketing)/about/page.tsx aur (shop)/cart/page.tsx — dono alag teams/alag layouts, par URL mein parentheses gayab : /about , /cart . @modal , @stats jaise slots ek hi screen par kai independent pages render karte hain.

Extending native fetch with {cache} and {next: {revalidate}} options in RSC. No useEffect needed. RSC fetch Server component ke andar seedha await fetch(...) — useEffect ki zarurat nahi. Extended fetch Next.js ne native fetch ko patch kiya — cache/revalidate options diye. Waterfall Ek fetch khatam, tab doosra shuru — total time judta jaata hai. Server Components async ho sakte hain . Component ke andar seedha await karo — data HTML banne se pehle aa jaata hai. Client-side jaisa useEffect + useState + loading spinner ka chakkar khatam.

Same fetch URL called multiple times in one render tree is deduped — automatic within a request lifecycle Request Memoization Ek render ke dauran same URL ka fetch ek hi baar hota hai — baaki cache se. React cache() Functions ko per-request memoize karne ka React API — fetch ke bahar wali calls ke liye. Request lifecycle Ek HTTP request ka poora render tree — isi dauran memoization zinda hai. Layout, page, aur 3 components — sab getUser() bula rahe hain? Network par ek hi request jaayegi. Baaki sab ko wahi jawab milega. Ye React ka cache() API hai jo Next ne fetch par apne aap laga diya.

Persistent across requests and deployments. force-cache (default), no-store, revalidate: N Data Cache Server-side persistent cache — requests aur deployments ke beech bhi zinda. force-cache Data ko cache karo (purani default behaviour). no-store Har request par fresh data — cache mat karo. Data Cache build/deploy se bhi lambi zindagi wala cache hai. Ek user ke liye fetch hua data agle visitors ko bhi wahi cached milega (jab tak revalidate na ho). Control: fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 60 } }) — 60 second tak cached.

Cached HTML + RSC payload at build time for static routes. Invalidated by revalidatePath/revalidateTag Full Route Cache Static routes ka rendered HTML + RSC payload build time par ban kar ready. Static vs Dynamic Koi dynamic API (cookies, searchParams) use hui to route dynamic — cache nahi hota. Invalidation revalidatePath/Tag se cached route delete, agli request par fresh. Agar route mein koi dynamic cheez nahi hai, to Next build time par poora HTML bana kar rakh leta hai. Har visitor ko wahi ready-made HTML CDNs se milta hai — server chalta hi nahi. Ek bhi cookies() / headers() / searchParams use hua → route dynamic → har request par render.

Client-side cache of visited route segments. Prefetched on hover. Duration: 30s (dynamic), 5min (static) Router Cache Browser (client) mein visited routes ke RSC payloads ki memory. Prefetch <Link> viewport/hover par route ka payload pehle se laa leta hai. router.refresh() Server se current route ka fresh data mangwata hai — cache refresh. Jab aap kisi route par jaate ho, uska RSC payload browser memory mein save ho jaata hai. Wapas wahi route par jaoge to network call hi nahi hogi — instant navigation. <Link> prefetch karta hai: static routes full payload, dynamic routes sirf loading skeleton.

Time-based (revalidate: N), on-demand (revalidatePath, revalidateTag), tags with fetch cache tags Time-based revalidate revalidate: N — N seconds baad cache "stale", agli request par refresh. On-demand revalidate revalidatePath() / revalidateTag() — jab tum kaho tab fresh. Cache tag Fetch par tag laga do, baad mein us naam se poora group invalidate. Cached data ko fresh karne ke do tarike: time-based ("60 sec baad stale maano") aur on-demand ("post publish hui? abhi revalidate karo"). On-demand precise hota hai — poora site nahi, sirf related cache tootta hai.
"use client" creates a boundary. RSC: no hooks, no events, can async/await, runs on server only
Passing RSC as children to Client Components. Server-only imports. The "leaves are clients" principle.
boundaries enable streaming HTML. loading.tsx as implicit Suspense. Manual Suspense for granular control.
"use server" directive. Form action={action}. useFormState, useFormStatus. Progressive enhancement.
useOptimistic hook — show immediate UI update while Server Action runs in background
server-only and client-only packages. Preventing server code from reaching the client bundle.
middleware.ts runs before every request. Auth redirects, A/B testing, geolocation, request rewriting.
V8-based runtime — no Node.js APIs. Runs in CDN edge nodes globally. Use for low-latency middleware.
app/api/route.ts — replaces Pages Router API routes. GET, POST, PUT, DELETE handlers. Edge-compatible.
cookies() and headers() from next/headers. Reading and setting cookies in Server Components and Route Handlers.
Session validation in middleware, protecting route groups, public vs private routes, token refresh
next-intl or built-in i18n. Locale routing, locale detection, getMessages(), useTranslations()
Automatic WebP/AVIF conversion, lazy loading, blur placeholder, responsive sizes, priority prop, remote patterns
Google Fonts via next/font/google — zero layout shift, self-hosted, subset, display swap, CSS variable
next/script with strategy: beforeInteractive, afterInteractive, lazyOnload, worker (Partytown)
@next/bundle-analyzer, dynamic imports, code splitting, tree shaking, barrel file pitfalls
Experimental: static shell + dynamic holes. Best of static + dynamic in one page. Uses Suspense boundaries.
Rust-based bundler replacing Webpack. `next dev --turbo`. Faster HMR, incremental compilation, module graph.

t: Mental Model — UI ek function hai

Declarative matlab tum sirf ye batate ho ki abhi screen aisi dikhni chahiye . Kaise pahunchna hai, wo library ka sar-dard. Analogy: imperative = taxi driver ko har tur

t: Mental Model — UI ek function hai
x: Ek formula jo poori library ka contract hai. Ek line: screen pe jo dikh raha hai wo sirf data ka function hai. Matlab agar mujhe tumhara state object de do, main bata sakta hu ki screen exactly kaisi dikhegi. Screen mein koi chhupi hui yaad nahi honi chahiye. Definition: UI = f(state) means the rendered output is a pure function of application

t: Mental Model — UI ek function hai
x: Poore project ka naksha — abhi dekh lo, phir har phase apni jagah baith jaayega. React ko log ek cheez samajhte hain, par wo asal mein 4 alag-alag layers hain, ek ke upar ek. Hum bhi wahi 4 banayenge, ussi order mein. 1. Element layer — createElement . UI ko plain object mein describe karta hai. Isko DOM ka pata bhi nahi hai. 2. Renderer layer — render . Object tree ko asli DOM

type, props, children. Bas. Aur children props ke andar rehte hain. Virtual DOM element ek plain object hai jo kehta hai "yahan ye cheez honi chahiye". Wo asli DOM node nahi hai — wo sirf ek parchi hai. Definition: A virtual DOM element is a lightweight plain-object description of a piece of UI. It is a description, not a thing. Analogy: architect ka naksha vs asli

n: TEXT_ELEMENT — text ko bhi element banana

Sabse aasan raasta ye hota: children mein string ko as-is chhod do, aur render ke waqt check karo "agar string hai to text node bana do". Hum ye nahi karenge. Hum string ko bhi ek element object bana denge jiska type "TEXT_ELEMENT" hai. Ab render, reconcile, commit — sabko ek hi shape milta hai.

n: Ye function DOM ko chhuta kyu nahi
x: Purity aur separation — layer 1 ko browser ka pata bhi nahi hona chahiye. createElement ek pure function hai: same input do to same output milega, aur wo duniya mein kuch nahi badalta. Na DOM, na koi global variable. Definition: A pure function returns the same output for the same input and produces no side effects.

Ek node ke liye kya karna hai wahi socho, children ke liye khud ko bulao. render(element, container) ka kaam teen kadam ka hai: DOM node banao, props lagao, phir har child ke liye khud ko bulao aur result andar daal do. Ye Phase 0 wale toDom se sirf ek cheez mein alag hai: ab type "TEXT_ELEMENT" bhi ho sakta hai, aur uske liye createTextNode chahiye.

n: Props lagana — asli complexity yahan hai

"props lagao" sunne mein ek line lagti hai, par props paanch tarah ke hote hain aur har ek alag treatment maangta hai: 1. children — ye prop nahi hai, isko skip karo. 2. Events ( onClick ) — addEventListener("click", fn) . 3. style object — {color:"red"} ko dom.style.color = "red" banana hai. 4. Liv

Ye ek jaani-pehchani computer science problem hai — tree diffing . Aur bura news ye hai ki general tree diff ka best algorithm O(n³) hai. 1000 nodes = 1 arab operations. Bekaar.

t: Reconciler — Purana yaad rakho, farak nikalo

Chaar cases, ussi order mein check karo: 1. !oldEl → ADD: naya DOM banao, parentDom.appendChild 2. !newEl

Har ek ke liye map se purana dhundo. Mila to UPDATE (aur DOM node reuse), nahi mila to ADD. 3. Jo purane bache reh gaye (map mein abhi bhi hain), unko REMOVE kar do. Aur ek chauthi

Wo reconciler ke liye hai, component ke liye nahi. Ye chhota sa design decision bada hai. React mein key component ko milti hi nahi . props.key undefined hota hai. n: Effect render ke baad kyu chalta hai

Definition: A side effect is any work that reaches outside the component — network requests, timers, subscriptions, direct DOM measurement, logging. useEffect(fn, deps) kehta hai: " fn ko abhi mat chalao. Jab poora render commit ho jaaye aur DOM taiyar ho, tab chalao."

n: Deps array — kab dobara chalana hai
x: Shallow compare. Aur yahi wo jagah hai jahan infinite loops paida hote hain. Deps array ka matlab: "in cheezon mein se koi badla ho tabhi effect dobara chalao." Teen roop hote hain, aur teeno alag hain: useEffect(fn) — har render ke baad useEffect(fn, []) — sirf ek baar (mount pe) useEffect(fn, [a, b]) — jab a ya b badle

n: Cleanup — jo shuru kiya wo band karo

Agar effect ne kuch "shuru" kiya — timer, event listener, subscription, WebSocket — to usko band bhi karna padega. Warna memory leak ya ghost updates (unmounted component pe setState). useEffect ka contract: agar tum ek function return karo, to library usko do jagah chalayegi — agle effect se theek

Us 16.7ms mein browser ko ye sab karna hota hai: tumhara JS chalana, style recalculate, layout, paint, composite. Agar tumhara JS akela 100ms le le, to 6 frames chhoot gaye . Browser free hote hi loop wahin se do

Loop ruk sakta hai, function return kar sakta hai, browser jo chahe kar sakta hai — aur jab wapas aayenge, us variable se kaam wahin se chalu ho jaayega. Isko resumable computation kehte hain. Har fiber ke paas uska purana version hai. Kaam naye pe, dikhta purana. Har fiber ke paas ek alternate pointer hai jo pichle render ke us hi fiber ko point karta hai. Do trees hote hain: current tree (jo abhi screen pe hai) aur work-in-progress tree (jo ban raha hai). Commit ke waqt bas currentRoot = wipRoot — aur do trees ke role swap ho jaate hain. Ek recursive walk, teen effectTags, aur DOM ek hi baar mein badal jaata hai. Commit phase seedha hai: fiber tree pe ghoomo aur har fiber ka effectTag dekh ke kaam karo. PLACEMENT → parentDom.appendChild(fiber.dom) UPDATE → updateDom(fiber.dom, alternate.props, fiber.props) DELETION → cleanup chalao, phir parentDom.removeChild

n: Hooks ko fiber pe le jao

Dekho — ye bilkul wahi pattern hai jo humne teen baar dekha hai: Phase 6: newEl.dom = oldEl.dom Phase 8: newEl.instance = oldEl.instance Phase 13: fiber.hooks ← fiber.alternate.hooks

n: useRef, useMemo, useCallback — sab ek hi cheez

Deps same to purani value do, warna dobara calculate karo. useCallback = useMemo(() => fn, deps) . Bas. useReducer = useState jisme action k

Effect hook fiber pe rehta hai, aur purana alternate se aata hai. 2. Effects commit phase ke baad chalte hain, kyunki tabhi DOM taiyar hota hai. Aur ek nayi cheez: cleanup ka waqt .
