Ye kaam karta hai, par teen problems hain: 1. 1000 buttons = 1000 listeners = memory. 2. Har update pe purana hatao naya lagao — kaam. 3. Purane browsers mein event behaviour alag-alag tha. Event delegation ka matlab: root pe ek hi list

t: Events & Review — Context, delegation aur architecture ka hisaab
x: Provider value fiber pe rakho, consumer return chain upar chadh kar dhundhe. Problem: theme ya user ko 5 level neeche bhejne ke liye har level pe prop pass karna padta hai — prop drilling . Context ka jawab: ek Provider tree mein ek value "rakh" deta hai, aur uske neeche koi bhi component wo value seedha le sakta hai.

n: Architecture review — aur kya scale karega
t: Events & Review — Context, delegation aur architecture ka hisaab
x: Peeche mud kar dekho. Layers ginno, limits likho, aur agla kadam batao. Ab tumne ek library bana li. Aakhri kaam hai usko samajhna — apne hi kaam ko bahar se dekhna. Char sawaal ka jawab likho: 1. Kaunsi layer kya jaanti hai, aur kya nahi jaanti? 2. Kaunsa hissa alag renderer ke saath chal jaayega, aur kaunsa nahi? 3. Kahan-kahan O(n) hai aur kahan O(n²) ka khatra hai?

Measures load performance of the largest image or text block. Target: fetchpriority="high" se browser LCP image ko pehle fetch karta hai. Definition: Largest Contentful Paint batata hai ki user ko page ka mukhya content kitni jaldi dikha — aksar hero image ya bada heading. Good: ≤2.5s, poor: >4s (75th percentile par). LCP 4 hisson mein toot-ta hai: TTFB, resource load delay, resource load duration, element render delay. Pehle dekho

Measures responsiveness — time from user interaction to next visual update. Target: < 200ms. Replaced FID in 2024. INP Page ke saare interactions mein se lagbhag sabse dheema (p98) interaction latency. Target ≤ 200ms. Long task Main thread par 50ms se zyada ka kaam — input handle hone se rokta hai. Input delay / processing / presentation INP ke teen phases: handler se pehle wait, handler ka time, aur next paint tak. Definition: Interaction to Next Paint click/tap/keypress ke baad screen update hone tak ka time measure karta hai. 2024 mein FID ki jagah aaya kyunki FID sirf pehla interaction aur sirf delay dekhta tha.

Measures visual stability — unexpected layout shifts during page load. Target: < 0.1. Causes: images without dimensions, injected content, font swap. CLS Unexpected layout shifts ka cumulative score. Target ≤ 0.1. Layout shift Visible element ne bina user input ke jagah badli. Reserved space Image/ad/embed ke liye pehle se width, height ya aspect-ratio dena. Definition: CLS impact fraction × distance fraction se banta hai. User click ke 500ms ke andar hone wale shifts count nahi hote (expected hain). Common causes: dimensions ke bina images, late-loading ads/banners, font swap, dynamically inject hua content upar.

First pixel of content painted. Target: < 1.8s. Leading indicator for LCP. Affected by TTFB and render-blocking resources. FCP Pehla content pixel (text/image) kab dikha. Target ≤ 1.8s. Render-blocking Head ka CSS/sync JS jab tak load na ho paint ruka rehta hai. Leading indicator FCP kharab ho to LCP bhi kharab hoga. Definition: First Contentful Paint page par kuch bhi (non-white) dikhne ka pehla moment hai. Ye TTFB aur render-blocking resources par depend karta hai.

Server response time. Target: < 800ms. Affected by server processing, CDN, database queries. Foundation for all other metrics. TTFB Request bhejne se response ka pehla byte aane tak ka time. Target ≤ 800ms. CDN / edge User ke paas ke server se serve karna taaki latency kam ho. Cache hit Server/CDN ne bina origin tak jaaye response diya. Definition: TTFB mein DNS, TCP/TLS, redirects aur server processing shamil hain. Ye baaki sab metrics ki baseline hai — TTFB 1.5s ho to LCP 2.5s mushkil hai.

Chrome DevTools Performance panel, Lighthouse, PageSpeed Insights, Web Vitals extension, CrUX dashboard, RUM via web-vitals.js Lab data Controlled test (Lighthouse, DevTools) — reproducible par synthetic. Field data / RUM Asli users ka data (CrUX, web-vitals library) — realistic. CrUX Chrome User Experience Report: public field data, 28-day rolling. Definition: Performance measure karne ke do tareeke: lab (Lighthouse, DevTools Performance panel) debugging ke liye aur field (CrUX, PageSpeed Insights, web-vitals JS library se RUM) asli user experience ke liye.

When does React re-render? State change, parent re-render, context change. What triggers a reconciliation vs a full re-mount. Re-render triggers State change, parent re-render, context value change. Reconciliation Naye virtual tree ka purane se diff nikal ke minimal DOM update. Referential equality Object/function har render naya banta hai, isliye memo ke liye alag dikhta hai. Definition: Component tab re-render hota hai jab uska state badle, parent re-render ho, ya jo context wo padhta hai wo badle. Re-render ka matlab function dobara chalana (render phase) — DOM update zaroori nahi. Props same hone par bhi child default mein re-render hota hai jab parent render ho.

memo() wraps a component to skip re-render if props are referentially equal. When it helps, when it hurts, when it's unnecessary. React.memo Component ko wrap karta hai: props shallow-equal hon to re-render skip. Shallow compare Props ke top-level values Object.is se compare. Bailout React ka render skip karna. Definition: memo(Component) render skip kar deta hai agar props pichle render jaise hi hain. Lekin har render par naya object/function bana kar pass karoge to props 'badle hue' maane jate hain aur memo bekar jata hai.

Memoize expensive values (useMemo) and stable function references (useCallback). The real cost: memory + comparison overhead. useMemo Mehengi calculation ka result cache karta hai jab deps na badlein. useCallback Function reference ko stable rakhta hai. Dependency array Jab ye badle tab hi value/function dobara banta hai. Definition: useMemo(() => compute(a, b), [a, b]) value ko cache karta hai; useCallback(fn, deps) function ko cache karta hai (useMemo(() => fn) jaisa). Dono ka maksad referential stability ya costly compute bachana hai.

Flame chart, ranked chart, why-did-this-render, interaction timing. Finding unnecessary re-renders in production. Profiler React DevTools tab jo commits ka time aur reason record karta hai. Flame / ranked chart Component tree ka render time visual / slowest-first list. Why did this render Props/state/hook ka kaun sa change render laaya. Definition: DevTools Profiler mein 'Record' dabake interaction karo; har commit ka flame chart dikhta hai. Grey = render nahi hua, rang = render hua (kitna time). Settings mein 'Record why each component rendered' on karo.

react-window, react-virtual (TanStack) — render only visible rows. Critical for lists > 100 items. Virtualization Sirf visible rows DOM mein render karna, baaki nahi. Overscan Viewport ke thoda bahar extra rows render karna taaki scroll smooth lage. Dynamic row height Rows ki height alag ho to measure karna padta hai. Definition: 10,000 rows ki list mein sirf ~20 visible rows render hoti hain; scroll par rows reuse hoti hain. Libraries: react-window , @tanstack/react-virtual .

Mark state updates as non-urgent. The UI stays responsive during heavy re-renders. Concurrent rendering in practice. useTransition State update ko non-urgent mark karta hai; isPending deta hai. Urgent vs transition Typing/click urgent; list filter ka heavy render transition. useDeferredValue Kisi value ka 'peeche chalne wala' version deta hai. Definition: startTransition(() => setState(...)) React ko batata hai ki ye update interrupt ho sakta hai. Urgent updates (input typing) pehle process hote hain aur heavy render peeche chalta hai, UI atakta nahi.

webpack-bundle-analyzer, Vite bundle visualizer, rollup-plugin-visualizer. Reading treemaps. Finding duplicates and dead code. Bundle analyzer Treemap jo dikhata hai kaun si library kitna JS add kar rahi hai. Duplicate deps Ek package ke multiple versions bundle mein. Dead code Import hua par use nahi hua. Definition: rollup-plugin-visualizer , webpack-bundle-analyzer ya vite-bundle-visualizer se build output ka treemap milta hai. Bade rectangles = bada size. Pehle sabse bade hisse se shuru karo.

Dynamic import(), React.lazy + Suspense, route-based splitting, component-level splitting, interaction-based loading Code splitting Bundle ko chhote chunks mein todna jo zarurat par load hon. Dynamic import import('./x') — Promise return karta hai, chunk alag banta hai. React.lazy + Suspense Component ko lazily load karke fallback dikhana. Definition: Route-based splitting sabse pehle karo (har page ka alag chunk). Phir heavy components (charts, editors, modals) ko interaction par load karo. Chunk prefetch se next navigation instant lagta hai.

ESM static imports enable tree shaking. Named imports, barrel file pitfalls, sideEffects flag in package.json, dead code elimination. Tree shaking Bundler unused exports ko final bundle se hata deta hai. ESM Static import/export — analyze ho sakte hain; CommonJS require nahi. sideEffects: false package.json mein flag jo bataye module import-time side effect nahi karta. Definition: Bundler static ESM imports se dekhta hai kaun se exports use nahi hue aur unhe drop kar deta hai. CommonJS dynamic hota hai isliye shake nahi hota.

Gzip vs Brotli (Brotli is 15-25% smaller). Static pre-compression vs on-the-fly. AVIF/WebP for images. woff2 for fonts. Brotli Gzip se 15–25% chhota compression; text assets ke liye best. Static pre-compression Build time par .br/.gz banana, server sidha serve kare. woff2 / AVIF / WebP Fonts aur images ke modern compressed formats. Definition: Text assets (HTML/CSS/JS/JSON/SVG) ko Brotli (ya gzip) se compress karo. Static files ko build time par pre-compress karo (highest level); dynamic responses ko on-the-fly medium level par. Browser Accept-Encoding bhejta hai, server Content-Encoding se jawab deta hai.

Multiplexing, header compression, server push (deprecated). preload, prefetch, preconnect, dns-prefetch — when each applies. Multiplexing HTTP/2 mein ek connection par kai parallel requests. preload / prefetch preload = abhi chahiye (current page), prefetch = shayad agle page mein. preconnect / dns-prefetch Third-party origin se connection pehle hi kholna. Definition: HTTP/2 multiplexing aur header compression se bahut saari chhoti files ka cost kam hota hai (HTTP/1.1 jaise 6-connection limit nahi). Server push deprecated hai; uski jagah 103 Early Hints aur resource hints use karo.

Cache-Control headers, immutable assets, stale-while-revalidate, service worker caching, content-addressable filenames Cache-Control Browser/CDN ko batata hai kitni der cache karna hai. immutable + hashed filenames app.3f9a.js kabhi nahi badalta — saal bhar cache. stale-while-revalidate Purana turant do, background mein refresh karo. Definition: Strategy: HTML par no-cache (har baar validate), hashed static assets par max-age=31536000, immutable , API/data par stale-while-revalidate . Content-hashed filenames se deploy par naya URL milta hai, cache invalidation ki zarurat nahi.

AVIF vs WebP vs JPEG — size comparison, browser support, with fallbacks, quality vs size tradeoffs AVIF Best compression, JPEG se ~50% chhota; encode slow. WebP Achi compression, near-universal support. Quality vs size Visual match par quality ~60–80 aksar kaafi. Definition: Modern formats: AVIF < WebP < JPEG size mein. <picture> mein AVIF, phir WebP, last mein JPEG fallback do. Photos ke liye AVIF/WebP, logos/icons ke liye SVG.

srcset with w descriptors, sizes attribute, art direction with , DPR (devicePixelRatio) optimization w descriptor img-800.jpg 800w — file ki actual width. sizes Layout mein image kitni wide dikhegi (browser iske hisaab se chunta hai). DPR Retina screens par 2x/3x pixels chahiye. Definition: srcset + sizes browser ko viewport aur DPR ke hisaab se sahi image chunne dete hain. Art direction (mobile par alag crop) ke liye <picture> ke media source use hote hain.

loading="lazy", loading="eager", decoding="async", Intersection Observer for custom lazy loading, LCP element must NOT be lazy loading=lazy Offscreen images/iframes ko tab load karo jab viewport ke paas aayein. decoding=async Image decode main thread block na kare. IntersectionObserver Custom lazy loading ya infinite scroll ke liye. Definition: Below-the-fold images par loading="lazy" lagao; above-the-fold (khaas kar LCP) image par eager (default) + fetchpriority="high" . decoding="async" decode ko main thread se hata deta hai.

Inline above-the-fold CSS, defer non-critical CSS, remove unused CSS, PurgeCSS, critical npm package Critical CSS Above-the-fold render ke liye minimum CSS jo head mein inline hota hai. Unused CSS Page par use nahi hui rules — coverage tool se milti hain. Async CSS Baaki CSS ko non-blocking load karna. Definition: CSS render-blocking hai. Critical CSS inline karo, baaki ko media="print" onload trick ya preload se async load karo, aur DevTools Coverage / PurgeCSS se unused CSS hatao.

font-display: swap/optional/block, subsetting, preloading, FOUT vs FOIT vs FOFT, variable fonts font-display swap / optional / block — loading ke dauran text behaviour. Subsetting Sirf zaroori characters rakhna (Latin) — file chhoti. Variable font Ek file mein kai weights/widths. Definition: Fonts ko woff2 mein serve karo, subset karo, critical font preload karo aur font-display: swap (ya optional ) rakho. Variable font se kai weights ki jagah ek file.

vs GIF (always prefer video), preload="none" for below-fold video, will-change, compositor layers, CSS transforms over position Video vs GIF MP4/WebM GIF se 5–10x chhota; GIF kabhi nahi. preload=none Below-fold video ke bytes tab tak mat lo jab tak play na ho. Compositor animation transform/opacity GPU par; layout/paint se bachte hain. Definition: Animated GIF ko <video autoplay muted loop playsinline> se replace karo. Below-fold video par preload="none" + poster. Animation sirf transform / opacity se karo.

Setting limits: max JS bundle size, max LCP, max CLS. Failing the build if budgets are exceeded. Lighthouse CI thresholds. Performance budget Metric ya size ka max limit jo build ko fail karwa deta hai. size-limit / bundlesize JS bundle size assertions. Lighthouse thresholds LCP, TBT, score ke minimums. Definition: Budget = limit: 'main JS ≤ 170KB gz', 'LCP ≤ 2.5s', 'CLS ≤ 0.1'. CI mein check hota hai; budget tootne par PR fail ya warn karti hai.

Automated Lighthouse in CI/CD. GitHub Actions integration, assertions, score thresholds, PR comments with scores. Lighthouse CI (LHCI) CI mein Lighthouse chalake results aur assertions. Assertion Metric ka threshold; fail par build red. Median of runs 3–5 runs ka median — noise kam. Definition: @lhci/cli se har PR par Lighthouse chalta hai, scores compare hote hain aur PR par comment aata hai. GitHub Actions mein treosh/lighthouse-ci-action aam hai.

Cache-first, network-first, stale-while-revalidate strategies. Workbox. Offline fallback pages. Background sync. Service Worker Browser aur network ke beech ka proxy script (background mein chalta). Cache-first / network-first / SWR Fetch strategies — speed vs freshness trade-off. Workbox Service worker routing/caching ki library. Definition: Service worker requests intercept karke cache se serve kar sakta hai. Strategies: cache-first (static assets), network-first (API/HTML), stale-while-revalidate (feed, avatars). Offline fallback page aur Background Sync (queued actions) bhi possible.

Selective hydration, islands architecture, resumability (Qwik). Reducing TBT by deferring hydration of below-fold components. Hydration Server HTML par JS attach karke use interactive banana. Islands architecture Sirf interactive widgets hydrate hote hain, baaki static HTML. Resumability Qwik: hydration ki jagah serialized state se turant resume. Definition: Poore page ko hydrate karna heavy hai (TBT/INP kharab). Selective hydration (React Suspense), islands (Astro), aur resumability (Qwik) kam JS ke saath interactivity dete hain. Below-fold components ko idle/visible par hydrate karo.

Measuring third-party script cost. Tag Manager audit. Lazy loading analytics. Facade patterns for embeds (YouTube, maps). Third-party script Analytics, ads, chat widgets, tag managers — aapke control ke bahar. Facade Real embed ki jagah light placeholder (YouTube thumbnail) jo click par load ho. Partytown Third-party scripts ko web worker mein chalana. Definition: Third-party scripts main thread, network aur CLS par asar daalti hain. Measure: Lighthouse 'reduce impact of third-party code', DevTools Network by domain. Fix: async/defer , lazy load, facades, Partytown, aur Tag Manager audit.

Sharing perf wins with the team. Automated regression detection. Grafana dashboards for RUM. Performance as a KPI. RUM dashboard Asli users ka vitals Grafana/Datadog mein dikhana. Regression alert Metric threshold se bahar jaane par automatic alert. Performance as KPI Perf ko business metric (conversion, bounce) se jodna. Definition: Performance culture = measurement + ownership. Dashboards (p75 LCP/INP/CLS by page), alerts on regressions, PR budgets, aur wins ko business impact ke saath share karna (e.g. 'LCP 400ms kam → conversion +2%').

vite.config.ts test config, test environment (node vs jsdom), globals, setupFiles, coverage providers (v8 vs istanbul) Vitest Vite-native test runner — Jest jaisa API, par bahut fast aur ESM/TS out of the box. environment node (default) ya jsdom / happy-dom — DOM chahiye to jsdom. setupFiles Har test se pehle chalne wali file (matchers extend, MSW start). Definition: Vitest vite.config.ts ke test block se configure hota hai. Component tests ke liye environment: 'jsdom' , globals: true (describe/it global), aur setupFiles mein jest-dom matchers import hote hain.

Test structure, assertion matchers (toBe, toEqual, toContain, toThrow, toMatchSnapshot), test.each for table-driven tests Matcher expect(x).toBe() , toEqual() , toContain() , toThrow() . toBe vs toEqual toBe = Object.is (reference); toEqual = deep equality. test.each Table-driven tests: ek test, kai input/output rows. Definition: describe tests ko group karta hai, it / test ek case hai, expect(value).matcher() assertion hai. test.each se ek hi logic ko kai data par chalate hain.

vi.fn(), vi.spyOn(), vi.mock(), vi.importMock(), mockReturnValue, mockResolvedValue, mockImplementation, clearing mocks vi.fn() Mock function jo calls record karta hai. vi.spyOn(obj, 'method') Existing method ko wrap karke track/override karta hai. vi.mock(path) Poore module ko replace karta hai (hoist hota hai). Definition: Mocks dependencies (API, timers, modules) ko fake karte hain taaki test fast aur deterministic rahe. mockReturnValue , mockResolvedValue , mockImplementation se behaviour set hota hai; vi.clearAllMocks() / restoreAllMocks() se reset.

async/await in tests, resolves/rejects matchers, fake timers (vi.useFakeTimers), vi.advanceTimersByTime, waitFor resolves / rejects Promise matchers: await expect(p).resolves.toBe(1) . Fake timers vi.useFakeTimers() — setTimeout/Date control mein. waitFor Condition true hone tak retry (RTL). Definition: Async tests mein async/await use karo aur hamesha await/return karo, warna test pehle hi pass ho jata hai. Time-based code ke liye fake timers: advanceTimersByTime(ms) .

v8 coverage, coverage thresholds, lcov reports, which lines/branches to cover, what NOT to test (config, types, trivial getters) Coverage Kaun si lines/branches tests ne chalayin. v8 vs istanbul v8: native, fast; istanbul: instrumentation, zyada accurate branches. Threshold Minimum coverage jo CI mein enforce hota hai. Definition: vitest run --coverage report banata hai (lines, branches, functions). Coverage ye batata hai kya chala , ye nahi ki kya sahi check hua . Config, types, trivial getters aur generated code ko exclude karo; critical logic par branch coverage dekho.

beforeEach, afterEach, beforeAll, afterAll, test.skip, test.only, test.todo, describe nesting, test isolation beforeEach / afterEach Har test ke pehle/baad setup-cleanup. Isolation Har test independent chale — shared mutable state nahi. test.skip / only / todo Temporarily skip, sirf ye chalao, ya pending marker. Definition: Lifecycle hooks ( beforeAll , beforeEach , afterEach , afterAll ) setup/teardown handle karte hain. Nested describe mein hooks scope ke hisaab se chalte hain. test.todo planned tests ka marker hai.

n: RTL Philosophy — Test Behaviour, Not Implementation
x: "The more your tests resemble the way your software is used, the more confidence they give you." Avoid testing state, class names, internal functions. Behaviour over implementation User ko jo dikhta/hota hai test karo, state/internal function nahi. Confidence Test jitna real use jaisa, utna confidence. Refactor-safe Implementation badle par test na tute. Definition: RTL ka motto: 'The more your tests resemble the way your software is used, the more confidence they give you.' Component ko render karo, user ki tarah interact karo (click, type), aur screen par jo dikhta hai wo assert karo.

getByRole (highest priority), getByLabelText, getByPlaceholderText, getByText, getByTestId (last resort). ByRole + accessible name. getByRole Sabse preferred query — accessible role + name se. getBy / queryBy / findBy getBy: turant ya error; queryBy: null return; findBy: async wait. getByTestId Last resort jab koi semantic query na mile. Definition: Query priority: getByRole > getByLabelText > getByPlaceholderText > getByText > getByDisplayValue > getByAltText > getByTitle > getByTestId . Absence check ke liye queryBy + not.toBeInTheDocument() .

@testing-library/user-event simulates real browser behaviour (focus, pointer, keyboard). fireEvent is lower-level. Always prefer user-event. user-event Real user interactions simulate: focus, pointer, keyboard events ka poora sequence. fireEvent Sirf ek low-level DOM event dispatch karta hai. userEvent.setup() Instance banao, phir await karke use karo (v14). Definition: @testing-library/user-event click par hover → mousedown → focus → mouseup → click jaisi poori sequence chalata hai, type par har key ka keydown/keyup. fireEvent.click sirf ek click event deta hai.

findBy* queries (async, wait for element), waitFor(callback), waitForElementToBeRemoved, act() wrapping. findBy* getBy + waitFor: element aane tak wait. waitFor Callback ko tab tak retry jab tak pass na ho ya timeout. act() React ko state updates flush karne deta hai; RTL zyada tar khud wrap karta hai. Definition: Async UI (API ke baad data dikhna) ke liye await screen.findByText() use karo. waitFor assertion ko retry karta hai; waitForElementToBeRemoved loading spinner ke hatne ka wait karta hai.

Mocking child components, mocking React Router, mocking context providers, wrapping with custom render function. Custom render Providers (Router, QueryClient, Theme) ke saath render wrapper. Module mock Router/hooks ko vi.mock se replace karna. Boundary mocking Sirf network/browser APIs mock karo, apne child components nahi. Definition: Component ko context chahiye (Router, React Query, Redux) to ek renderWithProviders helper banao jo wrapper deta hai. Child components ko mock sirf tab karo jab wo bahut heavy ya third-party ho (chart, map).

@axe-core/react, toHaveNoViolations, aria-label, role queries as accessibility validation, jest-axe integration. axe-core Automated accessibility rules engine. jest-axe / vitest-axe toHaveNoViolations() matcher. Manual testing Automation sirf ~30–40% a11y issues pakadta hai. Definition: axe(container) rendered DOM par WCAG rules chalata hai (missing labels, bad contrast, invalid ARIA). Role-based RTL queries bhi accessibility ka implicit test hain.

setupServer() for Node/Vitest, setupWorker() for browser. Handler registration. server.listen() / worker.start(). MSW Mock Service Worker — network level par requests intercept karta hai. setupServer Node (Vitest/Jest) ke liye; setupWorker browser ke liye. Lifecycle listen() before all, resetHandlers() after each, close() after all. Definition: MSW real network layer par requests ko intercept karta hai, isliye fetch/axios/React Query code ko pata bhi nahi chalta ki mock hai. Node mein setupServer(...handlers) , browser mein service worker.

http.get, http.post, http.put, http.delete. HttpResponse. Matching by URL, path params, query params. Handler Ek route ka mock: method + path + resolver. HttpResponse Response banane ka helper: HttpResponse.json(data, { status }) . Path params /users/:id — resolver mein params.id . Definition: Handlers http.get/post/put/delete(url, resolver) se banate hain. Resolver request padh sakta hai ( await request.json() , query params) aur HttpResponse return karta hai.

Success responses, error responses (4xx, 5xx), network errors (HttpResponse.error()), delays (delay utility) Error response HttpResponse.json(..., { status: 500 }) . Network error HttpResponse.error() — request fail jaisa. delay() Latency simulate: loading states test karne ke liye. Definition: Sirf happy path nahi, error aur loading states bhi test karo: 4xx/5xx responses, network failure, slow response ( await delay(500) ) aur empty list.

server.use() for one-off overrides in a single test. server.resetHandlers() to restore defaults. One-time handlers. server.use() Ek test ke liye handler override. resetHandlers() Har test ke baad defaults wapas. { once: true } Handler sirf pehli request par chale. Definition: Default handlers happy path dete hain; kisi ek test mein alag response chahiye to server.use(http.get(...)) se override karo. afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers()) overrides saaf karta hai.

graphql.query, graphql.mutation, graphql.link — mocking GraphQL operations by name. Variables inspection. graphql.query / mutation Operation name se match karte hain. Variables Resolver mein variables padh sakte ho. graphql.link Specific endpoint URL ke liye scoped handlers. Definition: GraphQL sab kuch ek endpoint par POST karta hai, isliye MSW URL ki jagah operation name se match karta hai: graphql.query('GetUser', ...) .

handlers.ts shared between Vitest, Playwright, and browser dev mode. Single source of truth for API mocks. Single source of truth Ek handlers.ts jo tests, Playwright aur dev mode teeno use karein. Shared fixtures Common mock data ek jagah. Dev mode worker Browser mein MSW start karke backend ke bina UI develop. Definition: src/mocks/handlers.ts ko Vitest ( setupServer ), browser dev ( setupWorker ) aur Playwright ( page.route ya MSW) mein reuse karo. Data builders/factories bhi share hoti hain.

playwright.config.ts, projects (chromium/firefox/webkit), baseURL, retries, workers, reporter (HTML, GitHub) playwright.config.ts Projects (browsers), baseURL, retries, workers, reporters ka config. projects chromium / firefox / webkit / mobile viewports par same tests. webServer Test se pehle dev/preview server start karna. Definition: Playwright config mein projects alag browsers/devices, use.baseURL , retries (CI par 1–2), workers (parallelism) aur reporter (html/github) set hote hain. webServer app ko khud start karta hai.

getByRole, getByLabel, getByText, getByTestId. Auto-waiting. Chaining. Filtering. Avoiding brittle CSS selectors. Locator Lazy, auto-waiting element handle — page.getByRole(...) . Auto-waiting Playwright action se pehle actionability (visible, enabled, stable) khud check karta hai. Strict mode Locator multiple elements match kare to error — ambiguity pakadta hai. Definition: Locators user-facing queries se banao: getByRole , getByLabel , getByText , getByTestId . Chain/filter: page.getByRole('listitem').filter({ hasText: 'Asha' }) .

Encapsulate page interactions in classes. Reusable, maintainable E2E tests. BasePage, LoginPage, DashboardPage. Page Object Model Page ki interactions ko class mein wrap karna. Reuse Selectors aur flows ek jagah — UI badle to ek file update. Fixture Page object ko test mein inject karne ka Playwright tareeka. Definition: POM mein har page/component ke liye class banti hai jo locators aur actions ( login(email, pw) ) expose karti hai. Tests business language mein likhe jate hain, selectors tests mein nahi.

test.beforeEach, test.afterEach, test.use, global setup/teardown, Playwright fixtures for auth state reuse. Fixture Test ke liye setup jo automatically banta/cleanup hota hai ( test.extend ). storageState Login session (cookies/localStorage) save karke reuse. globalSetup Poori run se pehle ek baar chalta hai. Like a singly list, plus a prev pointer on every node. The prev pointer enables O(1) deletion of a node you already have — no need to find its predecessor. This is what makes LRU Cache possible. A linked list whose tail points back to the head, forming a loop. Common in round-robin scheduling, Josephus-style problems, and as the mental model for cycle detection. A stack that always stays sorted (increasing or decreasing) by values — you pop elements that violate the order before pushing. Pick a pivot, partition the array so smaller elements sit left and larger right, then recurse on both sides. Build the sorted array one element at a time: take each element and insert it into the already-sorted prefix, shifting larger elements right. Problems about ranges [start, end] — merging, inserting, counting overlaps. The near-universal trick is to SORT by start time, then compare each interval's start against the running end. A hierarchical structure where each node has at most two children (left, right). Recursive by nature — every subtree is itself a binary tree, which is why recursion is the natural tool. Breadth-first search visits level by level using a queue: process all nodes at depth d before any at depth d+1. The queue-size snapshot trick cleanly separates levels. A binary tree with the ordering invariant: left subtree < node < right subtree. Searches halve the space each step — O(log n) on balanced trees. Inorder traversal yields sorted order. Queue-based level-by-level exploration. On unweighted graphs it finds the SHORTEST path in edges. The visited set (or distance array) is mandatory — unlike trees, graphs have cycles. An Eulerian path visits every edge exactly once (Eulerian circuit if it starts and ends at the same vertex). Hierholzer's algorithm builds it by following unused edges and splicing cycles back in. Classic problem: Reconstruct Itinerary (visit every flight edge). What is the difference between an Eulerian path and a Hamiltonian path? Ab tak har traversal ka goal tha: har node ek baar dekhna. Yahan goal ulta hai: har edge theek ek baar use karna — node dobara aa jaaye to chalega. Isko Euler path kehte hain. Wapas wahin khatam ho jahan se shuru hua? To Euler circuit . A tree where each node holds children keyed by character, and a flag marking word ends. XOR is its own inverse: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x. That makes it the perfect tool for cancelling duplicates — every element that appears twice vanishes, leaving only the singleton. When the state includes which elements are used, encode it as an integer bitmask: bit i set means item i is taken. x: Ek data chhupata hai, dusra tarika. Dono ek saath chalte hain. Abstraction Andar ka jhanjhat chhupa kar bahar sirf zaroori cheez dikhana. Implementation "Kaise hota hai" wala asli code. Contract Ek waada — "main ye kaam kar sakta hu", bina ye bataye ki kaise. Sochо tum gaadi chalate ho. Tum steering ghumate ho aur gaadi mud jaati hai. Tumhe ye jaanne ki zarurat nahi ki andar rack-and-pinion hai ya hydraulic. Steering wheel ek abstraction hai: wo batata hai ki kya ho sakta hai (mudna), aur kaise hota hai wo chhupa deta hai. n: Interface — "main ye kaam kar sakta hu" ka waada
t: Abstraction — kya hota hai, kaise hota hai chhupao
x: Sirf naam aur shape. Koi code nahi. Aur ek class kai interfaces le sakti hai. Interface Ek list jisme sirf ye likha ho ki kaunse kaam ho sakte hain — unka code nahi. implements Ek class ka ye kehna ki "main is interface ka waada poora karti hu". Contract Waada — agar tumne implements likha, to har method banana hi padega. Ek interface sirf ek list hai: "jo bhi ye interface le, usme ye-ye methods honi chahiye." Usme koi code nahi hota — sirf naam, arguments aur return type. Wo ek waada hai, ek kaam nahi. Analogy: bijli ka socket. Socket kehta hai "do pin, itni distance par". n: Abstract class — adhoori class jise poora karna zaroori hai
t: Abstraction — kya hota hai, kaise hota hai chhupao
x: Kuch code de deti hai, kuch tumse likhwati hai. Aur ye interface se kab behtar hai. Abstract class Ek adhoori class — usse seedha object nahi bana sakte, use poora karna padta hai. Abstract method Sirf naam, koi code nahi — bachche ko likhna hi padega. Concrete Poori bani hui class jisse object ban sakta hai. Abstract class ek aisi class hai jo adhoori hai. Usse tum seedha object nahi bana sakte — pehle use poora karna padta hai. Usme do tarah ki cheezein hoti hain: • Poori methods — jo sabke liye ek jaisi hain, code ke saath. • Abstract methods — sirf naam, koi code nahi. Har bachche ko khud likhni pade

n: ADT — interface aur implementation ka farak

Implementation Us ADT ko asal mein banane ka ek tarika — array se, linked list se, ya kuch aur. Ye abstraction ka sabse saaf udaharan hai, aur interview mein bahut poocha jaata hai. Stack kya hai? Wo ek cheez hai jisme tum push kar sakte ho aur pop kar sakte ho, aur jo aakhir mein daala wo pehle nikalta hai. Dhyaan do — maine ye nahi bataya ki wo andar se kya hai. Wo array se bana ho sakta hai

n: extends aur super — muft mein saaman
x: Bachcha baap ka sab kuch paata hai, aur usme apna jod sakta hai. Inheritance Ek class ka doosri class se sab kuch (fields + methods) apne aap mil jaana. Parent / Base / Superclass Wo class jisse liya ja raha hai. Teeno naam ek hi cheez ke hain. Child / Derived / Subclass Wo class jo le rahi hai. Teeno naam ek hi cheez ke hain. super Baap wale version ko bulane ka tarika. is-a Rishta jisme "bachcha ek tarah ka baap hai" — Car ek tarah ki Vehicle hai. class Car extends Vehicle ka matlab hai: "Car ke paas wo sab kuch hai jo Vehicle ke paas hai, aur uske alawa apna bhi." n: Method overriding — baap ka kaam apne tarike se
x: Same naam, alag kaam. Aur ek niyam jo tootne par sab kuch bigadta hai. Override Baap ki method ko bachche mein dobara likhna, apne tarike se. Signature Method ka naam + uske arguments + return type. Liskov ka niyam Bachche ko baap ki jagah rakha ja sake, bina kuch tode. (Chapter 10 mein poora) Overriding matlab: baap mein jo method hai, bachcha use apne tarike se dobara likh deta hai . Naam aur signature same rehta hai, kaam badal jaata hai. Aur jab tum vehicle.describe() bulao, to us object ka version chalta hai — chahe variable ka type Vehicle hi kyun na ho.

n: Ek baap ka niyam — aur Diamond Problem
x: Kai baap kyu allowed nahi hain, aur interface usko kaise theek karta hai. Single inheritance Ek class ka sirf ek baap ho sakta hai. Multiple inheritance Kai baap — TypeScript/Java mein classes ke liye allowed nahi. Diamond problem Do baap ek hi dada se aaye hon aur dono ne same method badli ho — ab kaunsi chalegi? Mixin Kai jagah ka code jodne ka ek jugaad, bina multiple inheritance ke. TypeScript (aur Java, C#) mein ek class ka sirf ek baap ho sakta hai. class A extends B, C likhna allowed nahi hai. Kyu? Kyunki ek gehri samasya hai jise diamond problem kehte hain. Socho: Vehicle mein describe() hai. ElectricVehicle aur CommercialVehicle dono Vehicle se aaye hain aur dono ne descri

n: Poochho mat ki tum kaun ho — bas kaam bolo
x: instanceof ki chain ko ek method call se badal do. Polymorphism Ek hi naam ka method alag-alag classes mein alag kaam karta hai. Dynamic dispatch Chalte waqt decide hona ki kaunsi class ka version chalega. instanceof Ye check karna ki object kis class ka hai. Aksar ek design smell hai. Do tarike hain kaam karwane ke: Tarika 1 (bura) — pooch-taach karo: "tum Car ho? To 30. Bike ho? To 20." Tarika 2 (achha) — kaam bolo: "tumhara rate kya hai?" Aur har gaadi khud jawab de. Dusre tarike mein tumhara code ko ye pata hi nahi hota ki kaunsi gaadi hai. Isko dynamic dispatch kehte hain — c

n: Overloading vs Overriding — do alag cheezein
x: Naam milte-julte hain, kaam bilkul alag. Interview mein pakka poocha jaata hai. Overriding Baap ki method ko bachche mein dobara likhna. Chalte waqt decide hota hai. Overloading Ek hi naam ki kai methods, alag arguments ke saath. Likhte waqt decide hota hai. Runtime polymorphism Overriding ka dusra naam — chalte waqt object decide karta hai. Compile-time polymorphism Overloading ka dusra naam — likhte waqt compiler decide karta hai. Ye do shabd har OOP interview mein aate hain, aur log inhe ghol dete hain. Farak seedha hai: Overriding — alag classes mein, same signature. "Bachcha baap ka kaam apne tarike se karta hai." Kaunsa chalega ye chalte waqt pata chalta hai. Overloading — ek hi class

n: Poore system par lagao — aur naapo

Shotgun surgery Ek chhota badlav karne ke liye 5 jagah file kholni pade — ek jaani-maani problem. Ab ye soch poore parking lot par lagate hain. Apne code mein teen tarah ke smell dhundo: 1. instanceof ya constructor.name ka check 2. switch (type) ya if (type === "...") 3. Aisi property jiska naam hi "type" ya "kind" ho, aur uspe branching ho Har ek ko ek method call se badlo.

Ab teen nayi baatein aayin: • Electric hai ya nahi • Handicap ke liye hai ya nahi • VIP hai ya nahi Ye teeno ek doosre se bilkul azaad hain — ek electric gaadi handicap bhi ho sakti hai aur VIP bhi. Aise azaad baaton ko orthogonal kehte hain. Ab gino: 3 vehicle

Tight coupling Do cheezein itni juri hui hon ki ek badalne par doosri toot jaaye. White-box reuse Aisa reuse jisme tumhe andar ka code jaanna padta hai — inheritance aisa hi hai. Inheritance ka ek pehlu log kam batate hain: bachche apne baap ke andar ka code jaante hain aur uspe nirbhar hote hain. Andar wale object se kaam karwao. Aur "kitna aage pass karna hai" ka faisla. Delegation Apna kaam khud na karke andar rakhe object se karwana. Wrapper / Facade Ek class jo andar wale objects ko chhupa kar ek saaf darwaza deti hai. Boilerplate Bekaar dohraya jaane wala code — jaise bahut saare ek-line delegation methods. Jab tum car.getHourlyRate() bulate ho aur andar wo this.service.rateMultiplier() bulata hai — usko delegation kehte hain. Car apna kaam khud nahi kar rahi; wo andar wale object se karwa rahi hai. n: Coupling aur Cohesion — design ka thermometer
t: Coupling, DI aur Immutability — design ko naapo
x: Do shabd jo batate hain ki design achha hai ya bura. Aur dono naape ja sakte hain. Coupling Do cheezein kitni juri hui hain — ek badle to doosri kitni tootegi. Cohesion Ek class ke andar ki cheezein kitni aapas mein judi hain — sab ek hi kaam ke liye hain ya nahi. Loose coupling Kam juri hui — badalna aasan. Ye achha hai. High cohesion Ek class ek hi kaam karti hai. Ye achha hai. Coupling = do cheezon ke beech ka bandhan. "Agar A badla to B kitna tootega?" Cohesion = ek cheez ke andar ka jud-av. "Kya is class ki saari cheezein ek hi kaam ke liye hain?" Analogy: ek almari mein sirf kapde hon aur wo saaf tarah se rakhe hon — high cohesion . Almari mein kapde, bartan, kitaabein

n: Dependency Injection — cheezein bahar se do
t: Coupling, DI aur Immutability — design ko naapo
x: Class khud apni cheezein na banaye. Aur isse test 3 line ka ho jaata hai. Dependency Wo cheez jiske bina class kaam nahi kar sakti — jaise ParkingLot ko spots chahiye. Dependency Injection (DI) Cheezein class ko bahar se dena, class khud na banaye. Constructor injection Sabse aam DI — cheezein constructor se aati hain. Fake / Mock / Stub Test ke liye banayi gayi nakli cheez jo asli ki jagah kaam kare. Agar ParkingLot ko spots, pricing aur clock chahiye — to wo unhe khud banaye ya bahar se maange ? Dependency Injection ka jawab: bahar se maango. constructor(private spots: SpotRepository, private clock: Clock) Bas. Ye poora concept hai. Naam bada hai, cheez chhoti hai.

n: Immutability aur Value Objects — galat ho hi na sake
t: Coupling, DI aur Immutability — design ko naapo
x: Ek Money class jo negative ho hi nahi sakti. Aur readonly ka dhokha. Immutable Aisa object jo banne ke baad kabhi badalta nahi. Badalna ho to naya banta hai. Value object Aisi chhoti class jiski pehchaan uski VALUE se hai, uske id se nahi — jaise ₹100 aur ₹100 ek hi hain. Primitive obsession Har cheez ko number/string rakhna, jabki uske apne niyam hain. Defensive copy Andar ka array/object bahar dete waqt uski copy dena. Abhi tumhari earnings ek number hai. Aur number ke apne koi niyam nahi hain — wo negative ho sakta hai, NaN ho sakta hai, aur usme rupaye aur paise ka koi farak nahi. Isko primitive obsession kehte hain: har cheez ko number/string rakhna, jabki us cheez ke apne niyam hain. I

x: Ek dot theek, teen dot khatra. Aur wo train wreck kyu tootti hai. Law of Demeter Ek niyam: sirf apne padosiyon se baat karo, unke padosiyon se nahi. Ek method sirf inse baat kare: 1. Khud se ( this ) 2. Apne fields se 3. Apne parameters se 4. Jo objects usne khud banaye Yaani apne padosiyon se baat karo, padosiyon ke padosiyon se nahi. n: Shallow aur Deep copy — Chapter 1 wali galti ka naam
t: Coupling, DI aur Immutability — design ko naapo
x: Copy banane ke do tarike hain, aur ek chup-chaap original ko badal deta hai. Reference Ek object ka pata (address), khud object nahi. Do variables ek hi object ka pata rakh sakte hain. Shallow copy Upar-upar ki copy — andar wale objects ki nahi, sirf unke pate copy hote hain. Deep copy Poori copy — andar tak sab kuch naya banta hai. Defensive copy Bahar bhejne se pehle copy bana kar dena, taaki bahar wala original na badal sake. Chapter 1 mein maine ek chhoti si baat chhod di thi. Yaad hai? const s = spots[0]; s.takenBy = "kuch bhi"; // humne sirf ek variable copy kiya tha... aur original badal gaya Us cheez ka naam hai: tumne object copy nahi kiya tha, sirf uska pata copy kiya tha. n: S — Single Responsibility: ek class, ek kaam
t: SOLID — paanch niyam jo tum pehle hi bana chuke ho
x: Class badalne ki ek hi wajah honi chahiye. Aur "wajah" ka matlab "insaan" hai. Single Responsibility Principle Ek class ke badalne ki sirf ek wajah honi chahiye. Responsibility Ek kaam jiske liye ye class zimmedaar hai. Actor Wo insaan ya team jiske kehne par ye code badalta hai. Definition: A class should have only one reason to change. "Ek reason to change" ka matlab log aksar galat samajhte hain. Iska matlab "ek method" nahi hai. Iska matlab hai: ek class ke badalne ke peeche ek hi insaan (ya team) hona chahiye. Tumhari ParkingLot abhi ye sab karti hai: spots manage, fee

n: O aur L — Open/Closed aur Liskov
t: SOLID — paanch niyam jo tum pehle hi bana chuke ho
x: Dono tum bana chuke ho. Aaj sirf naam aur naap. Open/Closed Principle Naye feature ke liye khula, purana code badalne ke liye band. Liskov Substitution Principle Bachche ko baap ki jagah rakha ja sake, bina kuch tode. Extension point Wo jagah jahan naya behaviour bina purana code chhoote jud sakta hai. Covariance Bachcha baap se ZYADA specific cheez lauta sakta hai — ye safe hai. Contravariance Bachcha baap se ZYADA general cheez maang sakta hai — ye bhi safe hai. O — Open/Closed: "Software entities should be open for extension, but closed for modification." Yaani naya feature jodne ke liye khula, par purana code badalne ke liye band. Tumne ye Chapter 4 mein bana liya tha. Yaad hai wo git di

n: I aur D — Interface Segregation aur Dependency Inversion
t: SOLID — paanch niyam jo tum pehle hi bana chuke ho
x: Chhote interfaces, aur upar wale ko neeche par nirbhar mat karo. Interface Segregation Principle Kai chhote interfaces ek bade se behtar hain. Fat interface Aisa interface jisme itni methods hon ki koi bhi sab implement nahi kar pata. Dependency Inversion Principle Upar wala module neeche wale par nirbhar na ho — dono interface par nirbhar hon. High-level / Low-level High = business ka niyam (parking ka logic). Low = tareeka (Postgres, SMS API). I — Interface Segregation: "Clients should not be forced to depend on interfaces they do not use." Yaani: ek bada interface banane ki jagah kai chhote banao. Warna jo class use implement karegi use aadhi methods khaali chhodni padengi — aur khaali me

n: Strategy aur Factory — tum ye bana chuke ho
t: Patterns — jinhe tumne pehle hi bana liya

Simple factory Ek static method jo sahi object bana kar deti hai. Sabse aam roop. Strategy pattern: "Ek kaam karne ke kai tarike hain. t: Anti-patterns — testing, aur OOP ki seema

n: OOP vs FP — aur OOP kab galat hai
t: Anti-patterns — testing, aur OOP ki seema
x: Do soch, do tarah ke faayde. Aur imaandari se: OOP har jagah sahi nahi hai. Functional Programming (FP) Aisi soch jahan data aur function alag rehte hain, aur data badalta nahi (immutable). Pure function Wahi input do to wahi output, aur duniya mein kuch na badle. Expression problem Ek chunav: naye TYPES jodna aasan chahiye ya naye OPERATIONS jodna. OOP aur FP ko log "dushman" ki tarah dekhte hain. Wo galat hai — dono ek hi problem ke do jawab hain, aur dono ka apna faayda hai. OOP: data aur uspe kaam karne wale functions ek saath , aur data chhupa hua. FP: data saada aur khula , functions alag, aur data kabhi badalta nahi — badalna ho to naya

The system must prevent double-booking under high concurrency (e.g. Taylor Swift tickets going on sale). Functional requirements Browse events by city/date/venue View sea

Distributed ID Generator (Snowflake) Design a distributed unique ID generator like Twitter's Snowflake. Generate globally unique, roughly time-sorted, 64-bit integer IDs at high throughput without a central coordinator. Functional requirements Generate unique 64-bit IDs across distributed nodes IDs roughly time-sorted (monotonically in

Payment Processing System Design a payment processing system like Stripe or PayPal. Users link payment methods, initiate payments, and the system processes them through payment providers, handles retries, prevents double-charges, and reconciles with bank statements. Functional requirements Add and manage payment methods (car

Chunked upload, delta sync, versioning, and real-time collaboration on binary files. Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Support versioning, offline editing with conflict resolution, real-time collaboration, and folder sharing with permission levels. Support multiple consumer groups (each group gets all messages), ordered delivery within a partition, and message retention. Functional requirements Producers publish messages to a topic

Ingest, transcode, distribute live video at global scale with < 10 second latency. Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Live Video Streaming (Twitch-like) Design a live video streaming platform like Twitch. Streamers broadcast live video, viewers watch with low latency. Design the upload pipeline, transcoding system, recommendation engine, and real-time view count. Functional requirements Video upload (up to 128GB) Transcode to 240p/360p/480p/720p/1080p/4

Graph algorithms, real-time traffic, ETA calculation, and map tile serving at planetary scale. Is problem ko kaise solve karoge? Functional requirements Content ingestion: studios upload master files Encod

Google Search Engine Design Google Search — a web-scale search engine that crawls the internet, builds an inverted index, computes PageRank, understands natural language queries, and returns ranked results in Functional requirements Crawl web pages continuously Build and update inverted index Compute and update PageRank

Ad Serving System (Google Ads) Design a digital advertising platform like Google Ads. Advertisers create campaigns with budgets and targeting criteria. ML Feature Store & Model Serving Design a ML Feature Store and Model Serving platform . Get a key, keep it secret, load it safely — never commit it An API key is your credential for the LLM provider — it is tied to your account and your wallet. You store it in a .env file (never in source code) and load it at runtime with a library like dotenv . 🧠 Analogy: the key to your apartment. The .env file is the locked drawer in the closet — the code n

A minimal chat call: create a client, send a messages array, get back the assistant's reply and token usage. 🧠 Analogy: the SDK is a well-labeled dashboard instead of a box of loose wires — same machine, far f

429s, timeouts, and the retry-with-backoff habit LLM APIs fail all the time: rate limits (429) , timeouts, and transient 5xx errors. The fix is a retry with exponential backoff — wait a little, try again, wait more, cap the attempts. 🧠 Analogy: busy phone line — you do not hang up and cry, you wait a moment and redial, each time a bit longer betw

How language models work — tokens, context window, temperature, top-p, stop sequences A language model predicts the next token. It reads your prompt as a sequence of tokens (word pieces) and, at each step, picks the most likely continuation. temperature controls randomness, top-p trims unlikely options, and the context window is how much text it can "see" at once. 🧠 Analogy: an extr

System prompts, user prompts, few-shot examples, role assignment, output constraints Prompt engineering is writing the instructions that steer the model. System prompts set the rules ("You are a code reviewer..."), user prompts give the task, few-shot examples show the desired format, and negative constraints say what not to do. 🧠 Analogy: the system prompt is an employee handbook;

OpenAI / Anthropic SDK — auth, request structure, roles array, response parsing, rate limits The API is how you talk to the model. You send a request with a model name and a messages array (roles system , user , assistant ) plus parameters like temperature . The SDK returns the reply, token usage, and more. 🧠 Analogy: a phone line to the intern. What you say is the request; what they say b

ReadableStream, Server-Sent Events, incremental token rendering in the UI Streaming sends tokens to you as the model generates them instead of waiting for the full reply. In Node you async-iterate over chunks; in the browser you read response.body and append each delta. 🧠 Analogy: batch is a letter delivered when finished; streaming is a phone call where the person talks

JSON mode, function calling for extraction, Zod schema validation, retry on parse fail Structured output forces the model to return JSON (or a schema-valid object) instead of free text. You use a JSON-mode flag, a function-calling schema, or prefill the reply — then validate with a parser like Zod . 🧠 Analogy: you asked the intern for a report; structured output is the fill-in-the-bl

Reason → Act → Observe — the fundamental loop that turns completions into agents ReAct (Reason + Act) is the pattern where the model explicitly thinks ( Thought: ), picks an action ( Action: search(...) ), observes the result, and repeats until it produces a final answer. 🧠 Analogy: solving a mystery — think, check a clue, update your theory, check the next clue.

JSON schema for tools — name, description, parameters. Description quality is everything. A tool is a function you expose to the model via a JSON schema: name , description , and parameters . The model reads the description to decide when to call it; your code implements the actual work. 🧠 Analogy: you hand the intern a phone book with descriptions — "call this number for accounting, th

while-not-done loop: call LLM → check for tool call → execute → append result → repeat The agentic loop: call the LLM → if it requests a tool, run it and append the result → repeat → until it answers without a tool call. This is the heart of every coding agent. 🧠 Analogy: you sit beside a brilliant intern who cannot touch the computer. They ask for a fact, you fetch it, read it aloud

In-context, episodic (external DB), semantic (vector store), procedural (system prompt) Agents remember four ways: in-context (current messages), episodic (conversations in an external DB), semantic (facts in a vector store), and procedural (behavior in the system prompt). 🧠 Analogy: in-context is working memory, episodic is a diary, semantic is a library, procedural is habits.

Token limits, history summarization, sliding window, message trimming strategies LLMs have a fixed context window, so history must be managed: count tokens, trim old messages, summarize the middle , and keep the most recent turns verbatim. 🧠 Analogy: a small whiteboard. You erase old scribbles and write a one-line summary so the important stuff still fits.

Text → dense vector. What they represent, how to generate them, cosine similarity An embedding turns text into a list of numbers (a vector) that captures meaning — similar texts get similar vectors. You compare them with cosine similarity to find related content. 🧠 Analogy: every sentence maps to a point in space; sentences with similar meaning land near each other.

Pinecone, pgvector, Qdrant, Weaviate — indexing, ANN search, metadata filtering A vector database stores embeddings and finds nearest neighbors fast using ANN (approximate nearest neighbor) indexes like HNSW or IVF, plus metadata filters. 🧠 Analogy: a library card catalog organized by meaning — you describe the book and it points you to the right shelf.

Implement the full while-loop without frameworks. Understand every line before using abstractions. Writing the while-loop yourself with raw SDK calls — no framework. You parse tool calls, run them, append results, and loop until the model answers. 🧠 Analogy: you build the machine that moves the intern's hands. The model reasons; your loop is the only thing that can act.

Thought → Action → Observation format. How to structure prompts so the model reasons before acting. ReAct with an explicit scratchpad: the model writes Thought/Action/Observation lines, your code parses the action (regex), injects the real observation, and loops until "Final Answer". 🧠 Analogy: a detective's notebook — every hypothesis and every clue check is written down so the chain of rea

Task decomposition, step-by-step planning, plan validation, re-planning on failure Planning means the agent decomposes a task into steps before acting: write a plan, execute step by step, validate, and re-plan when a step fails. 🧠 Analogy: a blueprint before hammering. A good plan catches missing details early and avoids wasted tool calls.

Tool failures, invalid JSON, API timeouts — teach the agent to diagnose and retry Teaching the agent to handle failures: tool timeouts, invalid JSON, API errors. Instead of crashing, the agent reads the error, diagnoses, and retries with a fix. 🧠 Analogy: the intern calls you with "that lookup failed" — you read them the error text and let them decide what to try next.

Pause points, approval gates, interrupt handling — how to add a human review step Pausing the agent before risky actions (editing files, running commands, sending emails) so a human approves, edits, or rejects first. Some tools are auto-approved; dangerous ones always gate. 🧠 Analogy: the intern drafts the email, but you press send. You trust them to write; you keep control of w

Running multiple tools concurrently, Promise.all patterns, merging parallel results Running several independent tool calls at once ( Promise.all / allSettled ) instead of one at a time, then merging the results. 🧠 Analogy: not making 5 phone calls back-to-back — you hire 5 people to call in parallel and collect all answers.

Fixed-size, recursive character, semantic chunking, overlap, parent-child chunks Splitting documents into retrievable pieces: fixed-size with overlap, recursive character splitting, semantic (by meaning boundaries), and parent-child (small chunks retrieved, larger parent given as context). 🧠 Analogy: cutting a book into cards. Too big and a card is off-topic; too small and a ca

OpenAI text-embedding-3-small/large, Cohere, Sentence Transformers, dimensionality tradeoffs Models that convert text to vectors — OpenAI text-embedding-3-small/large , Cohere, Sentence Transformers. Tradeoffs: cost, dimensionality, multilingual support, accuracy. 🧠 Analogy: different mapmakers. A cheap map might skip alleys; an expensive one captures every street.

Cosine similarity, dot product, HNSW, IVF — how vector DBs find nearest neighbors fast Finding nearest neighbors by vector distance — cosine similarity for search, and ANN indexes (HNSW, IVF) that trade a little accuracy for huge speedups at scale. 🧠 Analogy: finding the closest gas stations. In a small town you check all of them; in a city you use a map index that narrows the search

BM25 keyword + vector dense retrieval combined via reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) Combining keyword search (BM25 — great for exact names and acronyms) with dense vector search (great for meaning), merged by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). 🧠 Analogy: asking both a librarian who knows exact titles AND one who understands topics — then combining their shortlists.

Cross-encoder reranking (Cohere Rerank, FlashRank) — second-pass scoring for precision A second-pass cross-encoder that scores query+document pairs together to reorder the top candidates — far more accurate than the bi-encoder first pass. 🧠 Analogy: a first-pass recruiter shortlists 20 resumes; a senior engineer then reads each against the job description to pick the best 5.

Context recall, answer faithfulness, answer relevancy — RAGAS framework metrics Measuring RAG quality: context recall (did we retrieve the right chunks?), answer faithfulness (is the answer grounded in the context?), and answer relevancy — via RAGAS or LLM-as-judge. 🧠 Analogy: a chef tasting every dish before it leaves the kitchen — you cannot improve what you do not measure.

useChat, useCompletion, streamText, generateObject, tool rendering in React A framework for AI apps in Next.js: streamText on the server, useChat on the client, generateObject for structured output, and built-in tool rendering in React. 🧠 Analogy: a pre-built cockpit — the same dials you would hand-wire, but assembled and tested for you.

Nodes, edges, conditional routing, state annotations, compile() and invoke() A graph runtime for agents: nodes are functions, edges define flow, state is a shared object, and you compile() then invoke() . Conditional edges route based on state. 🧠 Analogy: a flowchart that runs — every box is a function, every arrow is a decision.

Cyclic graphs, loops, human interrupt nodes, checkpointing with MemorySaver Cyclic graphs with loops, conditional edges, human interrupt nodes , and checkpointing (MemorySaver/SqliteSaver) that persist state between runs and resumes. 🧠 Analogy: a recipe you can pause mid-step, put in the fridge, and continue the next day without losing progress.

Master agent delegates tasks to specialist subagents, aggregates results A master agent decides which specialist subagents to call (each with focused tools/prompts), then aggregates their structured results into a final answer. 🧠 Analogy: a team lead who never codes — they assign tickets to specialists and merge the pull requests.

Crews, agents with roles/goals/backstory, tasks with context, delegation A framework where agents are roles with role , goal , and backstory , organized into Crews with tasks that can delegate (e.g. an Editor sending work back to a Writer). 🧠 Analogy: a theatre troupe — each actor knows their character and objective, and the play emerges from their interactions.

Shared state, message passing, tool handoffs, result aggregation patterns How agents share information: a shared state object, message passing between agents, tool-based handoffs (one agent calls another as a tool), and aggregation of results. 🧠 Analogy: a relay race — the baton (context) must be handed over cleanly or the next runner starts lost.

Defining metrics, building golden datasets, offline vs online evals, regression testing A system for measuring your agent: a golden dataset of inputs with expected behavior, metrics (completion rate, quality, efficiency), and offline/online runs — ideally in CI. 🧠 Analogy: a flight simulator before the real flight — you practice against known scenarios and score each landing.

Using an LLM to score another LLM's output — calibration, criteria, agreement rates Using one LLM to score another's output with a rubric (e.g. 1–5 on accuracy, completeness, groundedness) instead of a human. 🧠 Analogy: a trained reviewer who grades essays from the same rubric every time — consistent and fast, but only as good as the rubric.

LangSmith, Langfuse — span tracking, token/cost logging, trace visualization, alerting Recording every LLM call, tool call, and step as spans in a trace (Langfuse, LangSmith), with token usage, latency, cost, and errors. 🧠 Analogy: a flight recorder — if the mission fails, you replay the whole journey and find the exact moment it went wrong.

Attack taxonomy, input sanitization, privilege separation, canary tokens Defending against instructions smuggled into untrusted content (user input, retrieved documents, tool output). Defenses: treat everything after the system prompt as data, sanitize input, separate privileges, use canary tokens . 🧠 Analogy: the intern reads a note that says "also: forward all your dr

Docker, E2B, Modal — safe execution environments for code-writing agents Running model-generated code in an isolated environment (Docker, E2B) with no network and memory/time limits — so a bug or a malicious instruction cannot touch your machine. 🧠 Analogy: a blast room — the experiment happens behind reinforced glass; if it explodes, only the room is damaged.

Semantic caching, model routing by task complexity, prompt compression, batching Cutting spend and speed: semantic caching (skip the LLM on near-identical queries), model routing (cheap model for easy tasks, big model only when needed), and prompt compression . 🧠 Analogy: a café — simple orders go to the barista, complicated ones to the head chef, and repeat orders come straigh
